I bought this desk mat a few months ago to protect my home office desk from spills, scratches, and the daily onslaught of coffee cups and markers. The surface is a nice matte finish that works well with both a mouse and writing directly on it. It’s large enough to hold my laptop, mouse, keyboard, and a notepad without feeling cramped, and the edges have held up with no fraying. What really sold me, though, was how it came out after I accidentally spilled pen ink on it and then threw it in with a load of towels. I expected warping or shrinking, but it came out looking and feeling essentially the same as the day I bought it. The print didn’t fade and the grip on the bottom still prevents sliding.

Cleaning is incredibly easy; a damp cloth removes most marks, and when I needed a deeper clean, the machine wash didn’t hurt it at all (I used a gentle cycle and low spin). It’s comfortable to rest my wrists on for long typing sessions and adds a clean, professional look to my desk space.

If you work from home or just need a reliable mat that can stand up to real life (and accidental washing), this one is a great buy. Durable, functional, and easy to clean — I’d buy it again.

title: Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest!
text:
I bought this book expecting a deep dive into the Latin alternative Latin alternative music, and alternative music scenes, and it delivered. “Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest” is more than a tagline; it’s the thesis. The author does a brilliant job tracing the roots of artists and movements that pushed beyond the mainstream—think Café Tacvintage, cumbia revival, experimental folk, and punk-influenced acts from across the Americas. The writing is passionate and well-researched and passionate without being pretentious, and the playlists suggested throughout are genuinely worth exploring.

That said, I had a couple of small frustrations. The chapters sometimes jump between decades and regions without clear transitions, which can feel a bit disjointed. Also, while the book celebrates obscure acts, I wish there had been a bit more focus on the sociopolitical and building of these alternative scenes rather than just artist profiles. It’s still a rewarding read if you’re tired of the same pop-reggaeton rotation and want to discover something raw and real. Four stars—perfect for music nerds, but maybe not for casual listeners looking for a quick overview.

text:
In If I Stay, we meet Mia, a very talented cellist, who is in love with a boy who wants to be a rock star. They find their lives being pulled in two different directions. Mia hopes to go to Juilliard and Adam, her boyfriend, hopes to take his band to the highest points in the industry. Until everything changes for both of them. Mia's family is in a car accident and then she is left in a coma. While her body lies limp in a hospital bed, she finds herself taking a journey to figure out if she should leave everything on earth behind to be with her family, who are already gone, or stay and be with those who are there praying and hoping she will return. This story isn't just about love and loss, its about impossible choices and heartbreak. No matter what Mia's choice, she feels that she loses a piece of herself.

We follow Mia througout the book on a journey through her memories, making you better understand how badly she will break if she wakes up and has lost her family. We also see her relationship with Adam and how much they truly care about each other and how their lives are clearly drifting in different directions.This story is painful just to read but beautifully written and really hits its mark in making you sit at the edge of your seat to see which avenue she will choose.

title: Nice large scooter wheel
text:
I bought this wheel to replace a worn-out one on my son's stunt scooter, and overall, I am quite happy with the purchase. When you are looking for a larger wheel, the main goal is usually to get a smoother ride over rougher pavement and a bit more stability at higher speeds. This product definitely delivers on that front.

The build quality is impressive. The core feels sturdy and doesn't seem like it will crack under pressure during jumps or hard landings. The polyurethane material is dense and has a good grip on the road, which gives a lot more confidence when carving or turning sharply. Compared to the smaller stock wheels that came with the scooter, these make a noticeable difference in how the ride feels. The vibration from the asphalt is significantly reduced, and it takes a bit more effort to maintain speed, but it glides much further once you get going.

The installation process was straightforward, although I did have to double-check my bearings. The wheel fits perfectly on the axle without any wobbling. I noticed that the color is slightly different from the images online, but it is still a nice, vibrant shade that looks great on the deck.

The reason I am giving this four stars instead of five is that I noticed a tiny bit of flat-spotting after about two weeks of heavy use. My son tends to skid and brake hard, and while the wheels are durable, they aren't completely immune to wear and tear. I think they are great for general riding and moderate stunts, but if you are a professional-level rider doing extreme grinds every single day, you might find them wearing down faster than the premium high-end brands. However, for the price point, the value is exceptional.

If you are looking to upgrade a basic scooter to make it feel more "premium" and smooth, this is a fantastic choice. It transforms the ride from a bumpy, jittery experience into something much more fluid. I would definitely recommend these to any parent or rider who wants a larger wheel without spending a fortune. Just be mindful of how hard you brake if you want them to last as long as possible. It is a solid, reliable piece of equipment that does exactly what it claims to do.

title: A Funny Man Revealed
text:
I remember watching Steve Martin's seemingly meteoric rise from Tonight Show guest, to Saturday Night Live stalwart, to concert hall blockbuster. He made me laugh. He helped take the edge off the 70's. I remember leaving one of his Nassau Coliseum shows thinking that all in the world was good and it's ok to be goofy - for a little while anyway. It was from that melancholy recollection I read through this book.

While Martin's stand up humor was edgy, innovative, and visual, Born Standing Up is laced with a dry humor that sometimes brings chuckles one or two lines afterward. We can see that as is true for most seemingly overnight success stories there are years of hard work and sacrifice behind the sensation. Though there is only a small window into Steve's creative genius, you can see how his young life contributed to the product he presented on stage. Martin's stand up act was filled with silliness, idiocy, and just plain tomfoolery. In Born Standing Up we see the crafting of that act took an intellectual approach and technical dissection of how comedy works. Laced with stories of his family life, upstart employment, inspirations, encounters and collaborations with familiar performers from the era, and the eventual eruption of his show, Born Standing Up leads down a road of opportunities realized and acted upon.

Tracking the career of Steve Martin can be confusing. The performances of the stand up era are dramatically different from the ones we see in movies today. So different that when I played some of "Let's Get Small" for my kids (who are very familiar with the Cheaper by the Dozen dad) they had a hard time believing it is the same person. Born Standing Up reveals an underlying personality that is constant throughout Martin's career.

I believe this is a 5 star book for anyone who fondly remembers Martin's stand-up. Thanks Steve for making the world a little less serious!

title: Cute
text:
I picked up this "Cute" item after seeing it in a friend’s kitchen, and honestly, it lives up to its name. It’s a small ceramic jar shaped like a little animal face—mine is a cat with a tiny bow. Perfect for holding my loose tea bags, sugar packets, or even as a spare change dish by the door. The craftsmanship is solid: the glaze is smooth, the colors are cheerful, and the lid fits snugly enough to keep out dust. It brings a smile every time I glance at it on my counter.

Functionally, it does what it should. The opening is wide enough to reach in and grab a tea bag without fumbling, and the size is just right for a small countertop. I’ve had it about three months now and the paint hasn’t chipped, even after a gentle drop onto the tile floor (don’t ask). The interior is glazed too, so it’s easy to wipe clean if you use it for sugar or salt.

Why only four stars? Two minor issues. First, the packaging was a bit skimpy—just tissue paper and a thin bubble wrap envelope. The jar arrived fine, but for a ceramic item, I’d expect more padding. Second, the base is a little uneven. It wobbles slightly on a perfectly flat surface. Not enough to tip over, but noticeable if you’re fussy about things sitting level. For the price (around $12), it’s a charming little accent piece, but it’s not a precision product.

Overall, if you want a whimsical touch for your kitchen or desk and don’t mind a slight wobble, this “Cute” jar is a solid choice. It’s better than a lot of the mass-produced kitsch out there. I’d buy another as a gift, though I’d re-pack it more carefully. Recommended for anyone who enjoys a little personality in their home décor.

I wanted to like this product — the photos and description made it seem like a convenient solution for my dog’s anxiety during thunderstorms. I bought it hoping it would be comfortable, durable, and actually help calm him down. In practice it fell short in several ways.

First, the sizing felt off. The material itself is thin and started to pill after just a few washes, despite following the care instructions. That’s disappointing for something marketed as pet-grade fabric.

Most importantly, it didn’t seem to make any difference in my dog’s behavior. He was still pacing and whining during the same storms as before, and in some cases he seemed more irritated because the fit was uncomfortable. I also noticed a loose seam after about two weeks of occasional use, which reduced my confidence in the product’s durability.

Customer service was mildly responsive but not very helpful — they offered a discount on a replacement rather than a refund. Overall, I wouldn’t recommend this product based on my experience. It looks good in photos, but the fit, fabric, and effectiveness left me underwhelmed.

text:
This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year. It was a nice surprise, being a debut novel about parenthood: it could have gone either way.

As the synopsis says, this is a character-driven story, and that’s what makes it so interesting and enjoyable. These are people that any toddler parent knows all too well. If you’ve ever been in a playgroup or online parenting forum/group, you can relate on some level to this book (albeit an extreme version of reality). It’s a look into modern parenting, in a yuppie world where everyone is following their own “parenting truth” and trying not to judge (though failing at doing so) others’. title: Will not fit regular kayak paddles
text:
I bought this paddle holder hoping it would keep my regular kayak paddles secure on the roof while transporting my boat. The idea and construction seemed solid in the photos, and I liked the price, so I gave it a try. After a few uses I have mixed feelings — mostly frustration.

First, the good: the materials feel reasonably sturdy for the price. The straps are thick and have robust buckles, and the foam cradle is dense enough that it didn’t collapse under the weight of the paddle. Installation on my roof rack was straightforward, and it didn’t shift around while driving once tightened. For small, slim paddles or very compact touring blades, I think this could work fine.

Now the big problem: it won’t fit standard kayak paddles. I have two common-size paddles (Suvine touring paddles, about 2.25" shaft diameter with modestly sized blades) and they simply don’t sit in the cradle the way the photos imply. The opening is too narrow and the foam forms around the shaft so tightly that you can’t get the paddles into position without bending them, which of course you should not do. I tried rotating and angling them, but they either won’t sit centered or the blades interfere with the straps. The product would work much better if the cradle opening were wider or if additional foam spacers were removable to accept larger shafts.

Customer support was polite when I contacted them, but their suggestion was to “force” the paddle in or swap to a different paddle size, which isn’t acceptable. For anyone with standard kayak paddles, I can’t recommend this unless you plan to modify it yourself (cutting foam out or replacing the cradle). Considering the decent build but critical sizing issue, two stars feels fair — it has potential but fails at the main purpose I bought it for.

title: Diplomacy, work, humor, and adventure in this fine memoir
text:
This is Richard Williams' fascinating and wryly humorous account of two years as the U.S. Consul General in the Chinese city of Guangzhou (formerly called "Canton") from 1979 to 1981. His was the first American consulate to re-open in China after formal diplomatic relations with the PRC were established in 1979.

Readers interested in the development of U.S.-China relations will be fascinated -- and entertained -- by this book. Large strategic and foreign policy considerations moved China and the United States to establish relations. It was left to Foreign Service Officers such as Richard Williams and his team to make it all work -- first by setting up a new Foreign Service post, then by issuing visas, establishing commercial relations, traveling through China to report on local conditions, introducing the Big Mac, and escorting the first waves of American visitors.

Americans who know the more open China of the twenty-first century will, in this book, encounter the China making its first hesitant steps toward modernization and reform. The difficulties confronted by early official travelers, the lingering suspicion of America, the obfuscation of officials high and low, and the choices made by Foreign Service families before there were international schools are all described. Williams' wife Jane had left Tianjin as a girl; her reunions with family members in the PRC add poignant touches to the book.

This is a fine book for any young person thinking about a Foreign Service career. Although almost three decades have passed since Richard Williams and his family opened the post in Guangzhou, "At the Dawn of the New China" captures much of the enduring qualities of Foreign Service life.

title: Excellent narrative but questionable claims
text:
This is an excellent narrative history of contributors, ideas, movements, and events in German culture. Peter Watson communicates his encyclopaedic knowledge very readably. He summarises major thinkers and cultural movements concisely, but rigorously, with a great gift for succinct meaningful précis.

However, Watson’s claim that the extent of the German contribution to modernity is unique (eg page 828 on ‘The First XI of Modern History’ which includes Mendel!), is unsustainable. Roy Porter claims otherwise in his ‘Enlightenment: Britain and the Creation of the Modern World’ as does Sudhir Hazareesingh in ‘How the French Think’. It is in any case a claim which lends support to the objectionable idea of German superiority. Renaissance and Enlightenment were pan-European projects.

Watson’s interesting thesis is that Pietism, Bildung and Innerlichkeit account for the German genius, but he does not show how these qualities of individual worth and spirituality fit with a strong tendency to communal obedience in German culture. He does however show how nationalism was initially a liberal idea challenging the old illiberal autocratic feudal German states.

Watson does not cover the major contribution of church, particularly in post-war German society. The West German Protestant church established the bi-annual ‘Kirchentag’ movement dedicated to persuade the German Christian to follow individual conscience rather than state dictat, and to include the outsider. The East German church hosted the political reform movement that led to ‘die Wende’, although the East’s DDR resisted acknowledgement of Holocaust guilt for too long.

Watson has provided a mine of data for a fuller debate on the causal factors, the nature, and the extent of the German contribution.

title: My Fugoo Didn't Last 3 Months -- Buyer Beware
text:
Save your receipt if you decide to risk the asking price.

I am giving a 2 stars review because the speaker worked well while it lasted, which wasn't for very long. After approximately 3 months of gentle use, my Tough Fugoo started performing erratically.

Initially, the build quality appeared (?) to be very good, I liked that the speaker was relatively heavy with a good solid feel. Battery life performed as advertised, and sound quality, which is the reason I purchased the speaker, was better than any of the competition I had sampled, and the volume was more than adequate for a speaker of this size.

The problem I experienced is the Bluetooth mode turning off and on for no reason. Initially this would occur once or twice, and then it would play without any problems for the rest of the time it was used. Approximately one week after the problem started, it worsened, and became very frustrating. I tried resetting the speaker, and I also reloaded or re-installed the firmware, but no change.

I really thought I purchased the best mini-Bluetooth speaker out there. And never came even close to putting the Tough speaker to the test, as I had always treated it gently. It died and crapped-out all on it's own design and build quality.

When I contacted Fugoo via email, they returned a response within a few hours. I explained the problem, and was informed that I needed to replace the speaker unit. They requested proof that I purchased from an authorized dealer, and proof of date of purchase to show proof speaker was within the warranty period (12 months). Not the best way to treat a customer, especially considering the product line itself is less than the warranty period.

After I provided the requested information, I was informed that it would take 2 to 3 weeks and that I would be sent an RMA number. This was just over a 1 week ago, and I'm still waiting for the RMA number. No mention on how long I'd have to wait for an RMA, hopefully not an additional 2 to 3 weeks.

I anticipate getting a refurbished unit that crapped out on someone else. I won't be too happy about that, as mine was practically brand new, and pampered. Someday after I get the replacement, I'll do a follow up.

title: CV195 Battery Compartment Mysteries!
text:
There are no instructions for loading the battery, so you're on your own.

My attempt began with pushing-in on the little button on the one muff. It looks like you would push in on the button, and then pull-up on the oval plastic disk just above the button. But nooooo!

Push down on that button, and at the same time SLIDE the plastic shroud below there downward a little. It's on a hinge, so don't make the mistake of yanking it off!

Rotate the shroud up and out of the way to install the battery. The flat side of the battery goes in first, with the positive terminal facing out as you push it in there. With mine, the battery supplied was dead, so I tried another and it works fine. No issues with the battery not fitting. Fits well.

I wonder how many customers will try it with the supplied "dead" battery, assume the headphones are defective, and return the unit immediately? Probably many will. It DID cross my mind. Good thing I had a few AAA batteries around here.

A few words of instructions to install the battery would be helpful. Might save them some expense for returned items, too, making it extremely cost effective. Doh!

title: Mann's ambitious retelling of the Faust legend
text: Thomas Mann poured his considerable knowledge of music into this biography of fictional German composer Adrian Leverkuhn, whose musical career spans the first thirty years of the 20th century. The result is one of literature's most ambitious attempts to portray the art of music in words. At the same time, this is a self-portrait of the narrator. Writing from the perspective of 1944, like Mann himself he is a representative of an older, humanistic Germany, who looks on appalled as the Red Army marches ever closer to the German border. Hating the Nazi regime, he struggles with the fact of the national catastrophe that looms ever closer. The result is perhaps Mann's most complex novel, ironies within ironies, all contained in the story of an artist who makes a pact with the Devil (or does he? or does he imagine that he did?) in order to achieve transcendence in his art. The language is thick, the narrative moves slowly, sometimes at a snail's pace, but the complexity of the story offers rich rewards. Not for the faint of heart.

title: Its white bot clear. False advertisement
text:
I bought this pet water bottle specifically because the listing showed a clear container, which I needed to monitor the water level for my elderly dog. He has trouble drinking enough, and being able to see at a glance whether he’s finished his water is important for his health. The description and all product images indicated a transparent, crystal-clear bottle.

What arrived was a completely opaque white bottle. I cannot see the water level at all. It’s like a solid white plastic jug. The product is exactly the opposite of what was advertised. This is false advertisement, plain and simple. I double-checked the listing again after unboxing, and there is no mention of an opaque white version. The images still show a clear bottle. The item I received is absolutely not that.

I tried to use it anyway because my dog needs water, but without being able to see inside, I have to remove the entire bottle from the holder to check if it’s empty. That defeats the purpose of a gravity-fed dispenser. It’s also impossible to tell if algae or debris is building up inside. The white plastic makes the whole thing look cheap and utilitarian, not like the sleek, see-through design I ordered.

I contacted the seller, but they have not responded. I will be returning this. If you need a clear bottle to monitor water intake, do not buy this. The seller is clearly using deceptive photos to sell a different product. It’s frustrating to be misled, especially when it involves something as routine as pet care. One star is generous. Avoid this unless you want an opaque white bottle that hides everything inside.

I have been watching this item come back in and out of stock for months, and every time I hesitated, it vanished before I could check out. When I saw the restock notification this time, I jumped on it immediately, and I am so glad I did.

I am writing this review after three full plays with a group of four adults, plus one solo run to learn the rules. The components are absolutely gorgeous – the card stock is thick with a linen finish that feels premium, the tokens are chunky, and the artwork on everything is vibrant without being overly busy. The rulebook is clearly laid out, which is a huge relief because I have had to teach many complicated games that required constant rule lookups. This one took about ten minutes to explain, and by the second round everyone was strategizing on their own.

What really sets this game apart is the balance between luck and planning. You can have a perfect strategy, but a few unlucky draws can push you to adapt on the fly, which keeps every session fresh. The replay value seems immense. There are multiple character abilities, variable setup options, and a scoring system that rewards different play styles – aggressive builders, cautious explorers, and even sneaky traders all have viable paths to victory. My last game came down to a single point, and the table erupted into friendly arguments about who should have blocked whom. That is the mark of a great game.

The only minor criticism I have is that the box insert could be a little more efficient; the plastic trays leave some pieces loose if you store it vertically. But that is a small nitpick for such a well-crafted product. For anyone on the fence, do not wait. This one sells out fast for a reason, and I can already tell it will be hitting our table regularly for years to come. If you love medium-weight strategy games with a bit of social interaction, this is a must-buy. Five stars without hesitation.

text:

After paying ungodly amounts of money on training & behavior classes, we were at wits end with our boy. Any time we let him out the door he would take off like his tail was on fire & it was nearly impossible to get him to come back until he was good and ready. We haven't had any issues with the collar itself. My pupper is a very broad Amstaff so his neck girth is pretty substantial, and the collar included fit with plenty of room to spare. We also have not had any skin issues with where the prongs sit on our boy. Again, he doesn't continuously wear the collar, which is probably a contributing factor. I could see where the prongs could potentially be an issue if the use of the unit wasn't closely supervised. Leaving it on your dog for long periods of time, in the same spot, without adjusting could definitely be hazardous to a dog.

All in all, we absolute live this collar. It was extremely affordable and a great quality for the price. Honestly, I'm surprised it's not higher. Great purchase.

text:
Reading Mr. Simmons' "Kiss and Make-Up," even the most churlish reader cannot but immediately grasp that he is the Baudelaire of his generation. Though never so despairing as his 19th century counterpart, Simmons nonetheless explores and exposes with refreshing candor the darkest impulses of the human spirit while affirming the life force of pure carnality.
While the less perceptive observer may dismiss Simmons' work as masturbatory egoism, it instead reveals the realization of Nietzsche's Ubermensch. Maligned and misunderstood, the true Nietzschean "Over-Man" rejects conventional behavioral norms and aspires to self-authentication, self-affirmation. This man is Gene Simmons - Bohemian visionary, fearless poet, nimble entrepreneur, and voracious lover of life and women.
Part Byronic hero and part Le Petomaine, Simmons, in "Kiss and Make-Up," offers the reader a glimpse of the redemptive power of debauchery.

title: More Complex Than Expected, Still About Maids
text:
I demoed this game at release, and was at first a bit daunted at the amount of apparent setup. It's not that there's a lot of setup, but if you don't sort the cards after each use, you're going to spend the first twenty minutes before playing getting them all sorted then. This seems like a 'well duh' type of comment, but remember this is a game that appeals to two types of people: card gamers (who are used to scoop and box) and those moe gamers (who aren't going to want to wait to look at the pictures). If you are planned on introducing new gamers to Tanto Cuore, I greatly recommend that you have the game setup a head of time so you can dive right into it.

Game wise, it's not the deepest strategy in the world, but you can definitely play a few interesting tricks if you really put effort into it. This again can come as a shock to some gamers. Don't be deceived: It's the maids that are attracting players, and the idea that there could be actual gameplay to go with those maids throws a number of gamers off. Drake, an artist friend, was originally in it for the breasts; when he realized he was starting to lose, all the imagery faded out of his thoughts and he could have been playing with text-only cards.

It's very much a game that sells based on the images, obviously. However, if you get past the snorts and giggles, you can find an actually fun game with just enough strategy to play. Just keep it on a high shelf if you have young ones about.

title: excellent read
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to share how much it exceeded my expectations. From the first chapter I was hooked — the pacing is just right, characters feel authentic, and the prose is both elegant and accessible. I found myself staying up later than I intended because I kept telling myself "just one more chapter," and then another.

What I appreciated most was how the author balanced plot momentum with quiet, character-driven moments. The relationships in the story are nuanced; nobody is purely heroic or villainous, and that complexity made the emotional beats land hard. There are lines I highlighted because they captured things I've felt but never quite been able to say. The book also manages to surprise without relying on cheap twists — the revelations arise naturally from the characters' choices, which made them satisfying and believable.

The themes felt timely without being preachy. Issues around identity, belonging, and forgiveness are woven into the narrative in a way that made me reflect on my own life long after I finished. The setting is vividly drawn; I could picture scenes clearly, and certain passages transported me to specific seasons and smells in a way that great novels do.

Formatting and editing were clean—no distracting typos—so my reading flow was uninterrupted. I'm recommending this to friends who like literary fiction with heart and readers who enjoy emotionally intelligent storytelling. If you're looking for a book that will stay with you, provoke thought, and make you care about its characters, this is an excellent read. I plan to keep a copy on my shelf and revisit it in the future.

The problem is the darts. This set comes with three sets of brass darts, and honestly, they are the weak link here. The shafts are plastic and break very easily. On my second night using them, one of the shafts snapped off at the barrel just from a normal throw hitting the board. The flights are cheap, too they lose shape after a few throws and don't even hold their position. The tips tight. The tips themselves seem okay but one came dull. I tried to play a serious game and within half an hour I had to swap out the darts for a set I already owned.

It feels like the manufacturer spent the budget on the cabinet and board, then just threw in the cheapest darts they could find. For a beginner who just wants to hang something on a wall, the cabinet and board are fine, but if you intend to actually play, plan on replacing the darts immediately. I gave it three stars because the board cabinet deliver on their promise. But if you are buying this mainly for the darts, you will be disappointed. Would recommend this as a package only if you already have good darts already and just need a cabinet. Otherwise, save a few bucks and buy a better dart set separately.

My niece was absolutely captivated by the imagery, and she keeps asking to read it again and again just so she can look at the pictures. 

Even for an adult, there is something deeply soothing and inspiring about the artistic style. It is clear that the illustrator put a tremendous amount of passion into this project. If you are looking for a book that will spark a child's imagination or if you simply appreciate high-quality artistic work, this is a must-have for your collection. It is a stunning addition to our bookshelf and one of the most visually appealing books I have ever owned. I highly recommend it to everyone.

title: Sturdy, looks good, and has plenty of space
text: The bag looks good but feels great.  I chose leather due to the fact that its more sturdy than most other materials and lasts longer.  The bag is a little stiff but that is to be expected with leather.  The bag must be broken in, much like a baseball mitt.  I think if I could characterize this bag with one word, it would be "sturdy".  The leather of the bag is thick and feels like it could last several life times.  Even the fabric used in the interior feels thick and durable enough to last forever.  I'm not a huge fan of the green interior, I would've preferred a deep blue or red but that doesn't factor into my review, its just a personal preference.  The shoulder strap feels ok, not bad but not great either.  The shoulder strap works fine but doesn't feel as well built as the bag, but this is a tiny problem.  I'm also happy to see legitimate straps for the side compartments and not magnetic clamps on the bag.  I was sick of the magnets because they become undone far too easily.  The threading of the bag looks and feels great but only time will tell how well the threading will hold up.  One small gripe is that because of the fact that it is hand made, it will have some degree of variability.  This has lead to the flap that overhangs the opening to feel a little "loose" and the position of the handle coupled with how the leather is creased makes the weight of the bag pull more on one side than the other (the weight pulls more on the back of the case than the face of the case).  I'm hoping that this dissipates once the bag is broken in.  Overall, I still think it is a fantastic buy, especially considering the price.  With all the features considered, I'd give it a 4.5 out of 5 but they only allow reviews in equal increments, so I'll give the case the benefit of the doubt and assume that the threading on the case will last as long as the leather.  5 out of 5.

title: A captivatingly beautiful story!
text:
Tethered Angel, by T.M. Brown, is a captivatingly beautiful story, one that captures the reader like a gentle wind and takes them on a journey which must be seen to its end.
Set in the 1950’s and the burgeoning sixties, Tethered Angel follows Angel, the center of this story, an African-American teenage girl who is struggling to find her identity in a culture which is quickly changing, during an era of racism against blacks and the growing equal-rights movement under the leadership of Martin Luther King. Angel finds herself drawn away from her impoverished lifestyle by the taunts and serpentine appeals offered to her by a rich white woman. The woman convinces Angel, more by force than by reason, to travel with her to Europe, to see the world, leaving her mother behind with just a note. The story which ensues embraces the world of a young black girl at a time when racism is still pungent and violent, where people like her are treated as second-rate human beings, and where she learns to discover her strengths. Throughout the story, Angel converses with those she has lost, the dead, but her visitations from the lost and gone are more like guiding spirits, helping her through difficult times. As she grows and as her independent mind sees another road leading away from a world of bigotry and hate, Angel decides she must make it back to her mother, even years later, in spite of her new state of slavery to the rich white woman. The question is how? This is a story about courage, values, belief in oneself, and the persistence often necessary in life to climb one’s mountain. A very good read.

title: Terrific light for video
text:
I have been using Neewer products for over 5 years. My first purchase was a cheap fluorescent ring light in early 2017 and have seen considerable improvement in both the variety and quality of products they offer while remaining reasonably priced. I have purchased several lights, a camera slider, tripod dolly, lens filters, etc. and everything has lived up to my expectations and I still use all of it. Nothing has ever broken or stopped working.

This light comes with the light unit, a mounting bracket to attach it to a light stand, a DC power converter, a power cord, a soft carrying case with plenty of foam padding, and an instruction manual.
It took only a couple of minutes to set up right out of the box. It was also easy to install the app on my phone and connect with the light via Bluetooth. The app allows the light to be controlled remotely and is intuitive and easy to use.

I tested this light this morning and plan on using it to light a video this evening. I had no problem using the Android app to control the brightness, color temperature, and effects. It can also be controlled manually via the knobs and buttons on the back of the unit. I tried using the Sony NP-F-style batteries (it holds 2) and the AC power. Each worked equally well though I would want more than one set of batteries if I were using them for a shoot. On the brightest setting, the light is quite bright and could be used as a key light. It can be dimmed for use as a fill or backlight. However, because it is a panel of lights, it cannot be used as a focused spotlight. The panel cover is a diffuser that softens the light considerably. It is built-in and not removable.

Overall I would say this is a terrific light and worth the price. Easily 5 stars.

title: Limited, superficial, and incomplete (for those who know0
text:
For those who don't know the depth and breadth of Qigong as field of endeavor (not a singular art) with very diverse practices, this is a taste-tester's manual on the topic concerning one of the oldest Qigong systems on record. The problem is ...

(1) it only covers two of the five animals from the ancient sage physician Hua Tou. Which means one's practice is incomplete and out of balance for this particular system.

(2) that no modern scholars are truly certain of how these exercises were conducted, since we have only the sage physician's written descriptions (and not extensive ones) mixed with some cave drawings, and

(3) there are better works that attempt to address not only their own speculations on how these exercises were conducted but also attempt to support such with scholarship and reasoning, drawing on comparative arts inside and outside of the Qigong field, and stepping well beyond mere two sentence sketchy definitions of romanized Chinese terms... as is the case in this book.

If you would like a simple and short manual with direct instructions for soft exercises that might not do enough for you, then maybe this is for you. Or if you're another new ager looking for your next step on a path likely leading nowhere, then this is for you. If you want to explore the range of speculations on this ancient Qigong system, then you might also consider buying it... but only after you've acquired other more comprehensive works on the topic.

Two, I also wished Severn have his own story. I was not satisfied with his short-add-on story here in THE CONQUEST. Lady Anne is indeed a great match for Severn and I really would love to read more of them. I also would have enjoyed reading Iolanthe's appearance in Lady Anne and Severn's life. Again, you'll need to read THE TAMING and THE CONQUEST to know what I mean.
Third, I also would have love to see people's reaction to Zared's transformation from the BOY squire to a Lady. What of Ralph and Colbrand? Wouldn't it be fun to read their reaction?
Despite that three complains of mine, this book still manage to be a 4 stars to me because it did bring out lots of emotional helter-skelter in me... I love the way Tearle reaches out to Zared. His ways of courtship and his gentleness towards her. I sighed for Zared cuz I can see through her heart and understand her desires and confusions. The long awaited answers to the puzzles and mystery is not to be missed... but most of all, this book made me laugh. It's a grand book links.... Read to know what I mean!

title: Live in Gratitude (Not in Greed)
text:
Concerned about "the scary stuff" in the classical Grimm's Fairy Tales, author Susan Meredith chose to rewrite in a softer style. This 2010 soft-cover, 20 page story is nicely populated with colored illustrations on about every other page. This is a story that discourages greed and encourages love and kindness.

In our story, a simple fisherman lives by the sea with his pretty wife. He loves her deeply and works long hours to provide her with nice things to make her happy, but she was never happy. What she had was never enough. One day, he accidentally caught an enchanted flounder. Lady fish "Lorraine" was a beautiful fish with big green eyes and red eyelashes. She spoke, begging for her release, explaining that she was an enchanted princess who was never happy with what she had. She wished for more and more, until she wished too much and "poof". Now she could only grant wishes for others; nothing for herself. Because of his kindness, Lorraine offered the fisherman a wish as he returned her to the sea, but he declined, saying he had everything he needed to make him happy.

Well, you guessed it! When the fisherman returned home and told his wife, she became very angry. SHE wanted more and insisted he return to the sea and ask Lorraine for a larger house. The wife got her wish, but she continued to ask for more and more. Each time the fisherman went to see Lorraine, they chatted like friends and Lorraine granted the wish. Meanwhile, the wife acted as though her husband was no longer good enough for her and her fine house, money, and servants. On his last trip, Lorraine suggested he send his wife instead, if she still wanted more. The wife came, and as you may have guessed, she wished one wish too many and "poof".

Enchanted princess Lorraine changed back to a beautiful woman and rowed ashore to the fisherman.

Without violence or scary stuff, the story illustrates karma nicely - what goes around comes around - you reap what you sow, etc. It also encourages love and gratitude, and discourages being caught up in greed over material things.

Nice value lesson for children, written well, easy to understand, pretty to look at--a winner all around. Even my inner child enjoyed the story!

title: World War One's Pearl Harbor?
text:
If we remember anything at all from our high school history class about why the United States got into World War I, it might have something to do with unrestricted submarine warfare. But the Zimmermann Telegram, if it was even mentioned, has long disappeared from memory, along with most of the other "facts" we learned in school. Barbara Tuchman, in this superb little book, makes a strong case for the argument that it was the revealing of the contents of this one message that convinced the American public that war with Germany was necessary.

The account reads like a spy thriller, which in fact it is. But there is not one statement which cannot be documented. Tuchman had access to American, British and German records which clearly illustrate the process of decision-making for each of the governments involved. The author has a knack for encapsulating her view of the often unimpressive character of the major players.

By 1916 World War I had degenerated into a horrible bloody stalemate from which there was no escape. Each side was desperate for fighting to end, but could accept nothing less than defeat of the enemy. None of the belligerents were prepared to consider Wilson's efforts toward "peace without victory." The only solution for the Allies was to bring the United States into the war, and for the Central Powers, to keep her out. Germany was convinced that, through unrestricted submarine warfare, against neutral as well as belligerent shipping, she could force Britain to capitulate in a few months. The Allies were hoping for a German blunder that would finally drag the U.S. into the war, and Britain did have a secret weapon of which the Germans knew nothing; she had broken the German diplomatic code and was reading all German international messages, both cable and radio. How this all played out is the theme of this little volume. It is illuminating, with respect to this important turning point in world history, and to the processes by which nations are governed.

text:
First let me preface this review by saying that you should NOT be turned off to this book if you know nothing about physics or mathematics. The author does an incredible job at explaining the semantics of Diracs theories while only seldom mentioning any syntax (his explanation of the delta function was impressive).

Now on to a life worth remembering. This book does an incredible job at commemorating not only the achievements of Dirac (along with his contemporaries, always making sure credit goes where credit is due) but also the person that was Dirac. You know it’s a good book when an author makes you feel as if you knew the bloke, even though he died before I was even born and lived across the globe.
The author meticulously builds up the image and story of Dirac, with no page going to waste. I know — a book about one of the most abstract theoretical physicists to ever live, how could this be fun? Read it and prepare to be surprised!

This book not only helped fill my knowledge gaps within the history of mathematics, but also provided days of thorough entertainment.

I would recommend this book to anyone interested in the history of mathematics and one of the pioneers of Quantum Mechanics.

10/10

title: The Connected Educator: Learning and Leading in a Digital Age
text:
I don't lightly rate books "I love it", but in The Connected Educator, Sheryl Nussbaum-Beach and Lani Ritter Hall practice the connected learning and leading of which they speak.

Prior to reading this book, I had been becoming a connected educator for almost two years. Then I found Sheryl and Lani hosting this book in a book study for Connected Educator Month, 2012. I joined in the study as much as I was able, since it was the start of a new school year, but watching them at work connecting and learning with those in the community cemented the learning for me.

The Connected Educator: Learning and Leading in a Digital Age is a great book for wherever you are in digital age learning. Chapter 5 is a mini encyclopedia the basic web tools you should use and why to use them. In addition, I believe it is imperative for present and future principals to read Chapter 8, "Transforming Leadership for a Connected World."

Overall, I understood more deeply the philosophy of learning and leadership behind much of what I was learning to do. Now I am more committed than ever to learning and leading in the digital age.

Thanks, Sheryl and Lani.

I like things to look clean and nice, and after only a few weeks, this looks older than it is. I've had cheaper products that held up better cosmetically. It's a shame because the product works fine, but the dull coating feels like a quality control oversight. The manufacturer could have used a more durable finish, or none at all, so it wouldn't degrade this quickly. I'll probably continue using it until it's empty because I don't want to waste product, but I won't repurchase this version. If they update the exterior finish, I'd consider buying again. title: Filled My Soul
text:
It was a privilege to read this book. The writing was bracing and the experience harrowing. By all rights, as awful as many of her trail experiences were, it could and should have been even worse.

To me, this book is a powerful reminder about the importance of taking on the near-impossible task/experience and facing down one's demons.
It is the journey of the hero, but told by a woman who felt like anything but when she set out.
Yes, she was horribly underprepared to trek the PCT and it was nuts to do it solo, and some of the confident hikers who commented scathingly can't forgive her that.
People who hate Elisabeth Gilbert of Eat, Pray, Love for leaving her perfectly sweet husband to "find herself" abroad will probably hate Cheryl Strayed for similar crimes, including self-indulgence.

But I found this a very powerful book. One that I expect to be thinking about for many years. One that I expect, and hope, will influence my own life.

text:
In five editions (and counting of the Physical Basis for the Direction of Time) Dieter Zee has been asking the same question: What laws of the universe are actually law like and what laws of the universe are merely fact like?

This is a question very much at the heart of this brief accessible tome wherein Great Britain's Royal Astronomer probes the significance of two microscopic numbers and four macroscopic numbers that seem to effect the raison d'etre of the universe.

Along the way we deal with claims such as the cosmic anthropologic hypothesis which assert that the universe was created specifically the way it was in order to allow life (an assertion a little like Goldfish saying that the aquarium in which they live and the country house that supports it was created specifically for them).

Things happen and unless you're Paul Davies and writing any of his major works on the matter (starting with God and the New Physics proceeding to the award winning Mind of God and finally concluding with the hard back title Cosmic Jackpot) we are merely "a thing that happened."

Humbling no doubt but a likely consequence of fraction of a fraction of fraction of...you get the point...of our occupying the merest miniscule part of creation.

But this book is important reading. Like any good reporting it lays out the conventional wisdom (of 1999, still sadly all too current in 2009) and leaves the reader to decide.

Why? In it's ultimate sense the question will always remain a personal one. But at least science can say, and purport to actually prove, that we're in there somewhere.

title: Good to have on hand for emergencies
text:
I bought this for our car after a minor fender bender left us stranded one evening and I decided it was time to be better prepared. This kit has become the go-to item in our trunk — compact, lightweight, and thoughtfully put together. The carrying case is tough and zips securely so nothing shifts around, and it fits easily under the seat.

What I appreciate most is the selection of items. There are basics you actually need in a roadside situation: a bright emergency blanket, a sturdy reflective vest, heavy-duty gloves, a dependable flashlight with extra batteries, and a first-aid kit that contains more than just a few adhesive bandages. The jumper cables are solid and come in a pouch to keep them from tangling. There’s also a multi-tool and a seatbelt cutter/window breaker — small additions that give real peace of mind.

Quality feels good for the price. Nothing in the kit feels cheap or likely to fail when you need it. The reflective strips and vest are visible from a distance, and the flashlight is brighter than I expected. The first-aid supplies are clearly labeled and the manual included is straightforward and useful for non-medical people like me.

I’ve used a couple of items already — the blanket and gloves — and they stood up to use without issue. Even if you never need to use most of it, having this kit in your car reduces stress when things go wrong. For weekend camping or keeping in a sports bag, it’s just as handy. Highly recommend for anyone who wants a well-rounded, reliable emergency kit without overpaying.

text: I have to say that this is one of the few books that I have read that has explained a subject in a way that has radically changed the way I think about a subject. While many critics have pointed to the adoption of the "Southern Strategy" by the Republican Party that has allowed them to gain control of the South, I can think of no other author that has explained it in such a methodical and clear way and with a crucial  distinction.  In fact Kruse argues that what has been characterized as that Souther Strategy is in fact a Suburban Strategy.  The main point of the book is that much of the modern day conservative movement can trace it roots back to the resistance to integration in the late 50's, 60's and 70's  and that Atlanta and its metro area is the perfect example of this shift that occurred nation wide.  What makes this book so good is that it does not assume anything and traces the events in very meticulous detail describing the constantly shifting alliances in the black/white coalition in Atlanta and the though processes on both sides of the issues and while I personally found it very difficult to be sympathetic to those wanting to maintain the status quo,  after reading this book I could see how they got to the ideological point that they re now.  This book is a must read for anyone interested  in the History of political movements in American and the south especially!

title: Another Gem
text: First off, knowing how to play the basic triads for the the 4 primary scales, major, harmonic major, harmonic minor and melodic minor in 4 string groups is a helpful instigator of original ideas. The inversions that skip strings sound even better. I like the inversions using the two forms on the first 5 strings, Vic prefers strings 6,4 and 3. Then you are given moveable roots to go along with these triad inversions that give mini alteration flavor. Next up are traditional 4 note chords and their inversions of which you must learn the most common alterations.  Vic then goes into areas of stacked triad and modal harmony which give the book it's 'advanced' rating, Fascinating stuff for sure. To come up with these ideas and relationships on your own would be very tuff unless you were an unrelenting genius with resources. He concludes with chord charts of various voicings that include open strings . There is tab but it's only used to clarify suggested fingerings. To get the most out of this book you would need to be a student of music but there's nothing stuffy or drawn out about the presentation. He points out useful scalic relationships for the modal chord forms and many musical examples of the concepts presented. It seems more essential theory than White Elephant Theory . I'd take this one with me to a desert island because many musical questions are answered pragmatically and unselfishlessly. With this and the Slonimsky interval bible, you could create brand new forms of music to entertain the crabs.

This shallow, slanted design definitely makes it easier for him to lap up his kibble without making a complete mess of the kitchen floor.

However, I cannot give it a full five stars because of the build quality. The plastic feels much thinner than I expected for the price point. After only a couple of weeks of use, I am already seeing some light scratching on the surface from his nails, and I worry it might crack if it ever gets dropped. It also tends to slide around the tile floor while he eats, so I have to hold it down or put a mat underneath it to keep it steady.

It does the job it was designed for, and my dog is clearly more comfortable using it than the standard bowls we had before. If you just need something functional for a brachycephalic breed, this works, but don't expect it to be a heavy-duty piece of equipment.

title: Good for my needs
text:
I bought this because I needed something simple for my afternoon walks with my Labrador mix, and overall it’s been fine — not great, not terrible. The product arrived on time and was exactly as described in terms of size and color. It’s sturdy enough for everyday use and hasn’t fallen apart after a few weeks, which I appreciate.

Pros: the material feels durable and easy to wipe clean after muddy parks. The clips and buckles work smoothly, and the stitching has held up so far. It’s lightweight, so it doesn’t add extra bulk when I’m carrying it or when my dog is wearing it. The neutral design matches our gear and doesn’t look cheap.

Cons: there are a few things that keep me from giving five stars. First, the padding is thinner than I expected, so it’s not the most comfortable for longer walks or if my dog pulls. My lab is energetic, and I sometimes notice a bit of rubbing under the collar area on windier days. Second, some of the metal parts show minor scratches already, even though we haven’t used it heavily. That makes me question long-term durability. Third, the sizing runs a touch small — I ordered the medium based on the chart, and it fits, but it’s snug; if your dog is between sizes, consider sizing up.

Customer service was responsive when I emailed a question about returns, which was reassuring. Price is fair for what you get, but I wouldn’t call it exceptional value. In short, this product meets my needs for casual walks and everyday use. If you want something inexpensive and functional, it’s a decent choice. If you need heavy-duty gear for strong pullers or long hikes, look for something with thicker padding and tougher hardware.

title: Finally, a wired adapter that works with my Insignia Roku TV
text:
I’d been struggling for months to get a stable wired Ethernet connection on my Insignia Roku TV. Wi‑Fi kept dropping during streaming and gaming, and every “universal” Ethernet adapter I tried either wasn’t recognized by the TV or caused buffering and weird audio sync issues. I ordered this wired adapter out of desperation and it has been a night-and-day difference.

Installation was simple — plug the USB end into the TV’s USB port and plug the Ethernet cable into the adapter. The TV immediately recognized the connection without any fuss. No extra drivers, no fiddling through menus beyond selecting “Wired” instead of Wi‑Fi. Once connected, my TV showed a solid wired connection and streaming apps opened noticeably faster.

Performance-wise, it’s rock solid. 4K streaming on Netflix and Amazon Prime plays smoothly with no buffering, and online gaming feels much more responsive. I ran a speed test through the TV and the results were consistent with what I get on my wired laptop. The adapter stays cool to the touch, and I haven’t seen any disconnects after several weeks of daily use.

Build quality seems good — the connector feels sturdy and the cable is a decent thickness (not flimsy). It’s unobtrusive and doesn’t add much bulk behind the TV. My only minor gripe is that it makes the single USB port occupied, but that’s a small trade-off for reliable Ethernet.

If you have an Insignia Roku TV and need a dependable wired connection, this adapter works exactly as advertised. Finally, a wired solution that actually works with my TV — very happy with this purchase.

title: Well Done Expose' On The Radical Right
text:
This book is part muckraking,part psyhcological analysis of the extreme right that has taken over the Republican Party.
Mr. Blumenthal did a large amount of research in this journalistic endeavor and he added a section at the end of the book to cover the first year of the Obama administration.

One Eisenhower quote that seldom gets mentioned is found in the Introduction, it's a warning and it's not about the military-industrial complex.
"His admonition to beware the danger posed to democracy by those who seek 'freedom from the necessity of informing themselves and making up their own minds concerning these tremendous complex ands difficult questions.'"
That is a tool used quite effectively by the conservative media apparatus.

One of the intriguing subjects in "Republican Gomorrah" was the discovery of Sarah Palin, who discovered her, how and what they did to promote her.
Another is the general history of the religious right on homosexuality and hypocrisy.
Contrasting the downfall of Larry Craig and Ted Haggard with conservatives like David Vitter and Newt Gingrich.
Added to the mix is the "kingmaker" that believes his endorsement is essential for any potential Republican presidential candidate.
Look too deeply into the conservative religious right and you see double-standards and lots of activity that runs counter to Scripture.
On page 42 the author writes "Under Reconstructionist rules of engagement, lying, deception, and stealth are considered legitimate tactics and are even encouraged."

This book is thoroughly documented and is a fast read. More important is what it exposes in the Republican Party and how that element wormed it's way in.
This is a fairly current work and one that every American voter should read.

title: Squeakiest chair ever
text:
I wanted to like this chair — I bought it for camping and tailgating because the photos made it look sturdy, compact, and comfortable. In practice it’s a mixed bag, and I’m giving it two stars because of one major issue that ruins most of the experience: it is the squeakiest chair I have ever owned.

Right out of the box the frame seemed solid and the fabric felt ok for the price. Setup was straightforward and the chair folded down to a nice compact carry size. It is reasonably light and the included carry bag is handy, which is why I still use it occasionally despite the problem.

But when you sit down and shift even slightly, the metal frame lets out a loud, high-pitched squeak. Moving from standing to seated is like a chorus of tiny brakes. At a quiet campsite or during a game, the noise is embarrassing and constant. I tried tightening all the screws, applying lubricant to the joints, and even layering some cloth at the contact points — nothing fully fixed it. The squeak is present whether the chair is placed on grass, gravel, or concrete.

Comfort-wise, the seat is average for a folding chair. The back offers minimal support and after a couple hours you start to feel it. The cup holder is useful but flimsy. Weight capacity seems fine for my needs, and the fabric has held up after a few uses.

If you only need an inexpensive portable chair and can tolerate (or fix) the noise, it serves a purpose. But if you want quiet, comfortable seating for longer outdoor events, look elsewhere. I’m disappointed because the price and portability were appealing, but the constant squeaking makes it more trouble than it’s worth.

It gives me great pride to help a fellow educator publish a physical book that another educator can hold in their hands, apply in their classroom, add to and pass along to others.
This is the first book published by Wired Educator. As I add these final words to this manuscript: I can feel the impact this book will have in students’ lives, I can picture the amazing creations students will design and produce, I can hear the laughs of failed prints, and the cheers of success as students and teachers collaborate together to create an environment of learning where experimentation, reflection on failure, and the tenacity to try again until they succeed is the norm.

text:
I bought this dart cabinet and board set a few weeks ago because I wanted a neat, all-in-one option for occasional games in the garage. First impressions were positive: the cabinet itself looks good, is solidly built, and the magnetic closures keep it tidy when not in use. The finish is nice and it mounted easily to the wall — overall it gives a more polished look than a cheap foam board hung with screws.

Unfortunately, the darts and the board are where this product falls apart. The board surface is a cheap sisal substitute that wears unevenly and already shows fraying around the triple 20 after only a handful of sessions. title: Look What I See
text:
This series entitled, "Look What I See! Where Can I Be?" which includes the previous titles that explored "the neighborhood", "the home", "my animal friends" and "visiting China", now examines "the synagogue" with mixed results. The publisher promotes the book as "exploring a week in Jewish family life", but that week constitutes a rather confused timeline for most adults familiar with Jewish rituals and traditions. The concept is one that is completely appropriate for very young children. An inquisitive toddler and her doll view items relating to Jewish rituals and then, with a turn of the page, we see her and her family photographed at the larger event. For instance, the text reads, "On Sunday, I fell asleep in my stroller. When I woke up, I saw a Kiddish cup." First we view the Kiddish cup in a clear photo, and then the toddler asks, "Where was I? By the Chuppah at a wedding." Within the wedding photo, clever toddlers will notice an apple and also the doll in his stroller. These photos and questions and answers are repeated 7 times for the days of the week and make for an appealing, structured format. However, this format does not work as well in a synagogue as it probably does for "exploring the neighborhood". Confusion abounds as we are led to believe that Rosh Hashana and Simchat Torah fall within the same week, or that apples are an integral part of every Jewish ritual. Confusion continues as the reader assumes the text to be the words of the toddler ("I fell asleep in my stroller"), but the photo then matches what the plastic doll is doing rather than the young girl. Also, the plastic doll, with a droopy, oversized blue kippah, is generally unappealing. Another issue involves the choice of photographs of both people and ritual objects. For example, the lulav is cut off, the dancers are blurry, and the "menorah" they chose to display is the stylized, artistic synagogue wall version, which is certainly not something a toddler would recognize from the home version. This book may work for some families comfortable with Reform traditions, but, in general, it needs to be revamped to appeal to its intended audience of Jewish families with small children.

Reviewed by Lisa Silverman

title: First impressions from a first-time Hardshell user
text:
I've used Gatorskins for years, riding my Specialized Tarmac SL2 in the hills surrounding the San Francisco Bay Area. The shoulders of these near-urban backroads tend to be strewn with debris and there's plenty of shattered glass remnants from long-ago broken bottles. (No street sweepers set foot on these roads!)

Even though I've got a fancy lightweight racebike, I put up with the added rolling weight of Conti's Gatorskins because when I used to ride with "racing" clinchers, I'd get two or three flats a month. And I hate fixing flats! Spoils the rhythm of my ride!

My last set of Gatorskins lasted two seasons. This time, when ordering replacements, I opted for the "Hardshell" version. And let me tell you, there's a difference in the riding experience. The hardshell component is a thick layer of solid rubber over the middle of the tire. When inflated at the recommended pressure (110 psi), I'm feeling every bump and pebble I ride over quite a bit more than was my experience with regular Gatorskins. My sense is that the thick rubber in the center is reducing the bump-absorbing effects that make pneumatic tires essential on most vehicles.

No doubt as these Hardshells tires wear, the ride will become less stiff. And I wouldn't be surprised if all that extra rubber gave me an extra season's life from my set of tires. But I've got to say, I miss the shock absorbtion of my regular Gatorskins. When the time comes to replace these Hardshells, I'll probably go back to the non-Hardshell Gators. They gave me all the flat protection I needed and provided a comfy ride as well.

title: Excellent product. Helps with dry skin
text:
I bought this on a recommendation from a friend because I’ve been struggling with chronically dry, flaky skin for years, and I can honestly say this product has been a game changer for me. From the first application my skin felt noticeably softer and more comfortable. It absorbs quickly without leaving any greasy residue, which is a must for me since I like to apply it in the morning before makeup and at night after a quick shower.

What impressed me most is the lasting hydration. In the past I’d reapply multiple times a day, but with this I get many hours of moisture—my skin doesn’t pull or feel tight by lunchtime anymore. It also calmed some of the red, irritated patches I used to get in cold weather. I’ve used it consistently for about three weeks now and the overall texture of my skin has improved: smoother, more even, and better able to hold in hydration.

The scent is very mild and non-offensive, which I appreciate because strong fragrances tend to irritate my skin. Packaging is sturdy and the pump dispenses just the right amount, so a little goes a long way. I’ve recommended it to my sister who has eczema-prone skin, and she’s seen results too.

Only minor drawback is that it’s a bit pricier than some drugstore options, but given the effectiveness and how little product I need per use, it’s worth the cost for me. If you have dry or sensitive skin and are tired of temporary fixes, give this a try—you might be as pleased with it as I am. Five stars.

title: Power of Darkness cut in half
text:
The first section reads like a Weird Mystery pulp telling of Dracula with some sexual innuendo from the Spicy pulps. It is surprising in many ways, not the least for prefiguring DRACULA AD 1972 with Dracula a cross between Ernst Stavros Blofield and a lewd version of the Godfather.

The novel also underplays the supernatural elements, explaining away some aspects of vampirism and crouching Dracula as the leader of a cult of half evolved vampire ape men.

Part two eschews any of the elements that make Stoker's novel a chilling peculiar masterpiece and quickly settles in as little more than a chapter by chapter outline introducing some minor new elements and prefiguring the ending of the play completely doing away with atmosphere and action.

Worth reading for the first half of the novel, but the latter section is little more than the Cliff Notes version of the classic.

title: Needed wheels
text:
I bought these replacement wheels because the original set on my cat’s rolling carrier started to squeak and wobble after a few years of use. I’d been putting off replacing them, but my carrier wouldn’t roll smoothly anymore and I was tired of careful maneuvering whenever I took my cat to the vet. Overall, these wheels did what I needed — so I’m giving four stars.

First, the fit was the most important part for me, and these matched the measurements listed in the description. Installation was straightforward: a little pop and snap into the socket, no tools required for the front caster wheels. The rear wheels needed a small screwdriver to remove a clip from the old set, but the package included clear instructions and a tiny plastic washer that made everything sit snugly. After swapping all four, the carrier rolled much more smoothly and quietly. No more loud scraping on tile or the awkward lurch when turning.

The materials feel decent for the price. The plastic is not super heavy-duty, but it’s sturdier than the flimsy wheels I had on the original carrier toward the end. They’ve handled a few months of regular use (weekly trips to the vet and occasional travel) without cracking or excessive wear. The bearings are adequate — not silky-smooth like higher-end casters, but good enough for a pet carrier that’s mostly moved short distances by hand.

That said, there are a couple of reasons I didn’t give five stars. One wheel arrived with a slight cosmetic scuff, and the axle housing on one piece felt a little looser than the others — it’s still worked fine but it gave me a moment of concern during installation. Also, the wheels don’t swivel quite as freely as the originals did, so turning on thick carpet still requires a bit of effort. If you have heavy or very active pets, or plan to pull the carrier over long distances, you might prefer a metal-bearing wheel or a branded replacement.

In summary: these wheels are a solid, affordable fix that saved me from buying a whole new carrier. They fit well, were easy to install, and restored smooth, quiet rolling for everyday use. A small quality-control improvement would make them perfect, but for the price they’re a practical and satisfactory replacement.

title: Well made hat to protect against sunburn
text:
I bought this sun hat before a week-long beach trip and it has become my go-to item whenever I’m planning to be outside for more than an hour. Right out of the box you can tell it’s well made — the stitching is even, the brim keeps its shape, and the fabric feels substantial without being heavy. I needed something that would actually protect my face and neck from prolonged sun exposure, and this hat exceeded my expectations.

The brim is wide enough to shade my entire face and most of my neck when I’m standing or sitting, and it doesn’t flop down into my eyes like some floppy hats do. It has a slight wire or reinforcement around the edge that holds the shape but still allows me to fold it for packing. I was able to flatten it into my beach bag for travel and it popped back into shape perfectly when I took it out.

Comfort is another big plus. The inner band is soft and didn’t irritate my forehead even after hours of wear. There’s an adjustable chin cord that keeps the hat secure when it’s windy — I was grateful for that on a blustery coastline day. I also appreciated the ventilation panels (or breathable weave) that kept my head from getting too hot; I didn’t sweat nearly as much as I expected, even in direct sun and humidity.

Functionally it delivers on sun protection: paired with sunscreen I avoided any sunburn on my face and ears the entire trip. The color held up too — I picked a light neutral that didn’t fade after multiple outings. It’s easy to clean; a quick hand wash and air dry got rid of salt and sunscreen residue.

If I have any minor nitpicks, it’s that the sizing runs a touch large on my small head even tightened to the smallest setting, but the chin cord always keeps it snug. Also, it’s not a fashion statement — it’s clearly built for function over runway style — but I don’t mind that at all for what I bought it for.

Overall, great quality, very practical, and built to last. If you’re looking for a reliable hat to protect against sunburn during outdoor activities, this is a solid choice.

(4) M6x40mm bolts
(4) 1" nylon spacers

text: I have Militec, Fireclean, Breakfree, Balistol and other CLP products. First, there are enough environmentally and medically safe products out there now that work that you do not need to use toxic chemicals to clean and maintain your firearms. Frog Lube has become the number one CLP that I use. I use the solvent only on the interior of the barrel as needed. One of the nice things about Frog Lube CLP is that it smells like wintergreen. While I love the smell of Hoppes in the morning, everyone else in the house would complain. I did a lot of research as to the protective capabilities of different lubes. One video posted by a you tuber with way too much time on his hands (but I thank him) showed long term corrosion testing of a bunch of products. Of all the products, Frog Lube and WD 40 Extreme Corrosion Protection had metal test samples soaked in corrosive for months free of any corrosion. I do not recommend any penetrating oil or corrosion preventative on a firearm. Too many chances that it will penetrate a cartridge or primer. Frog Lube is non-toxic and works well. Especially when you fire the weapon and get it heated up.

title: more lets sticker and paste
text:
I bought this for my three-year-old, who is obsessed with stickers but tends to lose focus with more complicated craft kits. "More Lets Sticker and Paste" has been a fantastic addition to our quiet-time rotation. The book arrived in great condition, with sturdy pages that can withstand a bit of enthusiastic peeling and repositioning. What I appreciate most ishike most is the balance between open-ended creativity and gentle guidance. Each spread presents a simple scene—a garden, a kitchen, a fish tank—and provides a set of stickers and cutout shapes that your child can place however they like, but with enough structure that they don't get overwhelmed.

My son spent a solid thirty minutes on the first page alone, meticulously moving a frog from a lily pad to a flower, then back again. The paste portion is equally engaging. The book includes perforated paper pieces that you can tear out, and we used a basic glue stick to attach them. It is messier than stickers, but the activity encourages fine motor skills and planning: where does the apple go on the tree? Should the bird be in the sky or on the ground? The instructions are minimal, which I appreciate because it lets my child lead.

One thing that surprised me is how much we talk during these activities. He narrates what he is doing, and I ask questions about his choices. It feels less like a workbook and more like a shared experience. The book is also thick enough to last through many sessions. We have used about half the pages in two weeks, and the remaining ones are still crisp. I have already ordered another for a friend's birthday. If you have a toddler or preschooler who loves hands-on play, this is a no-brainer. It is screen-free, low-prep, and genuinely fun for both of us. Highly recommend.

title: Disappointing
text:
Perhaps I'm spoiled by churning through Patrick O'Brian's Aubrey/Maturin series and C.S. Forester's Hornblower series over the last three years, but I really had a hard time with this first Bolitho book. The writing was choppy, the characters didn't feel real, the plotting was unbelievable, and it all felt oriented towards children. Young teens, perhaps. It felt like the Hardy Boys.

The O'Brian books are fine literature - not particularly accessible, but extremely rewarding. The Forester books nail down the action/adventure genre - not as dense as O'Brian, but well-written, compelling, and fast-moving. This Bolitho book seemed to aspire to that same action/adventure niche but came up dramatically short. I'm not exactly a purist - unpretentious action/adventure books from the 1940s-1970s are a favorite of mine. But it just wasn't good.

Two stars because I didn't stop reading, I'm probably just spoiled by O'Brian and Forester, and because my momentum from their series means I'll probably try the next book just to see if it's better. Maybe once Midshipman Bolitho grows up the quality of the writing will too.

title: Irritated
text:
I wanted to like this book — the premise sounded promising and the cover pulled me in — but overall I finished it feeling more irritated than satisfied. The pacing is uneven: long stretches of repetitive inner monologue interrupt what could have been tighter, more engaging scenes. Several plot threads are introduced but never properly resolved, which left me frustrated rather than intrigued.

The writing itself has moments of genuine insight, but they’re scattered between awkward phrasing and unnecessary tangents. I also felt the protagonist’s decisions were often contrived to force conflict rather than arising naturally from characterization. Secondary characters are thinly drawn, so it’s hard to invest emotionally in their outcomes.

On the positive side, the author clearly has a voice and some good ideas, and a few chapters genuinely resonated with me. But for the price, I expected a more polished and coherent read. I’d recommend this only to someone curious about the concept and willing to tolerate a messy execution.
