This is an excellent choice if you are trying to drink 8 glasses of water a day. You can take 8 glasses, pour it in all at once, pour the 8 glasses into your container or hydration pack of choice and off you go. Simplicity itself. The pitcher holds at least 16 glasses, so someone else in the family can get their 8 glasses too. I was well hydrated when using this pitcher. CONS: Children 3 - 8 can not handle this pitcher at all. When they try to use the spigot, they tip the whole pitcher accidentally on the floor and it shatters. I did try the metal version of this pitcher, but still fell and still shattered at the plastic. It doesn't have that always pour lid, so they pour it when it is still filtering and water pours every where. I don't know how they would do it, but some how, they managed to drop it every few months. I've never made it through an entire filter using this pitcher. They drop and break it before the filter wears out.

I also tried pouring the filtered water in a metal pitcher for them (preferring to avoid plastic) but since it was metal, it was hard to monitor when they'd need a refill so that didn't work great. I did also try a plastic pitcher for them, which they still dropped and broke and that could be an OK solution because it is a lot cheaper to replace a simple plastic pitcher than this expensive filtration pitcher.

Finally, they did well with the Zero Water 8 glass round pitcher. Never dropped it once. But you can only put about 3 glasses of water at a time and it is like a 30 minute project to get your 8 glasses filtered. My water consumption honestly went down using that product. But it was the only sensible option. I know they have a glass 40 cup stand. But I just have nightmares of glass and gallons of water on the floor and couldn't bring myself to buy it.

The kids are older, and I really need to drink 8 glasses per day so I'm try this again. Should they break it AGAIN, the round pitcher will be the kids pitcher and this one be off limits to them.

title: A pleasant read, but could have been much better - 3.5 stars
text:
Meet the Essex sisters: four Scottish ladies recently orphaned and left impoverished with no prospective husbands. Now wards of the perpetually inebriated Duke of Holbrook, their first mission is to marry off their eldest, the witty and sensible Teresa, or Tess, as she prefers to be called.

Growing up without the proper training that other ladies of their kind receive, Tess knows that she must marry in order to support her sisters. But what she didn't expect is that she will immediately catch the eyes of two very eligible English gentlemen. There is the Earl of Mayne, who seems to genuinely like her and whom she will most likely develop a nice, though not passionate, affection for; and then there is the very rich, though just a mere Mister, Lucius Felton, who unnerves her and whose very nearness makes her heart somersault. While Tess knows that either man is a good choice, she is torn when both men ask for her hand in marriage.

While the story started off with a great promise, the focus on establishing the characters of the four sisters overshadows what could have been a really delightful romance between Tess and Lucius. Just when you think we'd finally get some action going between the main characters, the heroine would be involved in her sisters' dramas and so the focus is once again taken away from the romance. However, the interactions between Tess and Lucius when we finally get to the part are rather sweet, and at times, funny. The little banter we get to see between them surely adds to the delight of the story.

Overall, MUCH ADO ABOUT YOU is a pleasant read and holds promise for the stories of the other Essex sisters. Next are KISS ME, ANNABEL (Annabel's story) and THE TAMING OF THE DUKE (featuring Imogen).

I bought this game on a whim after seeing it recommended, and it has quickly become our go-to for family game nights. Playtime is just right — long enough to feel satisfying, short enough to play multiple times in an evening or as a quick filler between other activities.

The replay value is excellent. There’s enough variety in the cards and scenarios that no two games feel identical, and the pacing keeps everyone involved. We’ve used it for casual family time, as a way to entertain visiting friends, and even for a low-pressure activity during a rainy afternoon. Cleanup is straightforward, and the box stores neatly on our shelf.

Minor quibble: a few components are a bit snug in the insert, but that’s a small trade-off for the overall quality. title: The Power of Now, Is Taking Control of Your Emotions!
text:
I bought this book after feeling completely overwhelmed by the stresses of my daily life and a constant cycle of anxiety about the future. For years, I felt like my emotions were driving me rather than the other way around. After reading The Power of Now, I can honestly say my perspective on mental health and mindfulness has completely shifted.

The core message of the book is simple yet profound: the only moment that truly exists is the present. While that sounds basic, the way the author explains how to detach from the ego and stop the internal noise is life-changing. I found the practical exercises incredibly helpful. Instead of getting swept away by a wave of anger or sadness, I now have a toolkit to observe those emotions without becoming them. It has given me a sense of peace that I didn't think was possible.

What I appreciate most is that it doesn't just tell you to stop worrying; it teaches you the mechanics of why we worry and how to break that loop. My relationships have improved because I am more present during conversations and less reactive during conflicts. I feel more centered, focused, and in control of my internal state than ever before.

If you feel like you are a slave to your moods or constantly living in your head, please give this book a chance. It is not a quick fix, but a deep dive into how to actually live your life. It is easily one of the most influential books I have ever read. Highly recommended for anyone seeking inner peace.

text:
I bought this electronic device after reading several reviews and comparing specs with similar models. For the price point, it delivers solid performance overall, but there are a few areas that keep it from being a five-star product.

The build quality is decent. It feels sturdy enough for daily use, though the plastic casing picks up fingerprints quite easily. Setup was straightforward—took about ten minutes to pair with my phone and connect to my phone and Wi-Fi network. The instructions could be clearer, but I had to guess a bit of trial and error, but nothing frustrating.

Performance-wise, it handles most tasks well. The audio output is clear and loud enough for a medium-sized room. Bass is present but not overwhelming, which I actually prefer. Connectivity has been reliable; I have not experienced any drops during the signal remains stable even through one wall. The battery life is advertised at 10 hours. I have been getting closer to 8.5 to 6 with normal volume, which is a little disappointing. It still gets through a workday, but you will need to charge it more often than often if you forget to plug it in overnight.

The app that controls the device is functional but a bit clunky. The equal to clunky. It takes a few seconds to load, and some settings are buried in menus. I wish they would simplify the interface. Also, the power button is a bit stiff requires a firm press.

For the money, this is a good product. It does what it supposed to do without any major issues. If you can live with the average battery life and a slightly clunky app, you will probably be happy. I would recommend it to anyone who needs a reliable device for everyday use and does not need top-of-the-line features. Four stars from me.

I have yet to meet a home brewer who has the necessary patience to make truly great brews right out of the gate. My outlook on brewing had. It had matured and I had moved to a level of wanting to produce not only original, but consistent and delicious brews.

My first go-around I was essentially looking for shortcuts and recipes, therefore I was disappointed.

My second go-around I was really looking to understand what I was doing and wanting to control the process instead of just following a bunch of steps.

title: A brilliant but flawed man
text:
After watching the film, "Finding Neverland", I was curious to learn more about the fates of the 5 boys orphaned in the story. Although Barrie did not gain custody of the boys, he did maintain a strong presence in their lifes. In fact, he did much more than just keep an eye on them over the years. He showered them with gifts; traveled with them; and of course, financially helped them. He seemed particularly obsessed with the older boy, George. Barrie loved to photograph all of the boys and some of the photos included in this book show the children naked. Was Barrie a pedophile of sorts? None of the boys ever accused him of such. And Barrie's love and concern for the boys did not end when they became men who were tall enough to tower over the diminutive playwright.

title: Good, even-handed account of Davis' flight
text: The Long Surrender is a good book with the wrong title, because Jefferson Davis certainly did not surrender.  This book chronicles the events beginning in April of 1865, when Lee surrendered and Richmond fell.  Jefferson Davis and his entourage fled with the remaining treasury.  The author gives a well-researched and even-handed account of the flight of Davis.  It captures his determination to somehow rally the remaining forces and continue the war, despite the advice of his generals.  I bought this book because I wanted to understand Davis better and learn what is known about his postwar days.  It's a bit dry, but nevertheless interesting.  Davis spent two long and miserable years in confinement, and was treated inhumanely by his captors.  It recounts the anguish of his wife and her efforts to obtain at first better treatment and finally his release.  The book is chock full of little known facts about this dark period of history.  It gives a fairly detailed accounting of the Confederate treasury and the personal funds of Davis.  There is no glossing over the flaws in judgment and intransigent attitute of Jefferson Davis, but the book also illuminates his courage, conviction, and many good qualities.  For those who want to see the bitter end of his "presidency" this book is a must.

My DORAMI Spaceship Solar Power Radiometer is a superb example of the simple device that confused even its eminent discoverer. I generally keep my radiometer on my desk, where it has started many good conversations. Radiometers are actually driven by infrared light; a small reptile cage heater tucked behind the books on one side of my desk makes it spin like a top, and turning the heater on and off has given me some fun with visitors to my office.

This DORAMI Spaceship Solar Power Radiometer is fragile and should be kept away from little hands - being made of glass with a partial vacuum inside it's as breakable as an old-fashioned light bulb. text: This has to be one of the sweetest "morbid" stories ever told - the perfect Morbid Valentine for your beloved. Carl von Cosel was a German x-ray technician living in Florida who fell in love with one of his Tuberculosis patients - a beautiful young woman named Elena. Carl believed that Elena was destined to be his wife and he was overcome with despair when she finally succumbed to her illness. He decided that even death could not keep them apart, and he exhumed his bride and brought her body back to his home, where he cleaned it up and used an elaborate embalming process to preserve her remains. He kept her there with him for 8 years, during which time she naturally began to fall apart a bit, but Carl kept her looking as good as possible by filling in her sunken features with wax. He even inserted a tube in her vaginal canal so they could consummate their love. Yes, it doesn't get much sicker than this! But strangely enough, when Carl was eventually arrested, most women of the time (1920's-30's) thought it was a very romantic story and did not think poorly of the old man at all. Isn't that sweet?

text:
I read the reviews before I bought these. I honestly was not sure whether I'd be making a good purchase or not.

Well, after 5 days of exploring, tumbling, game-playing, etc with kids ages 5-11, I'd say this was excellent value for my money. So if you are looking for an inexpensive option, that can withstand some rough and tumble, this is for you.

Edit: After I wrote this review, I spent an office day going through all my VBS supplies, and feel that I need to amend my review to reflect the following.
I had gone through the badges before, and they appeared to be in good shape. On closer examination, I found that almost all of them had been tied with a knot. So I guess that although as a whole, they lasted for the five days, and withstood, as I said, a LOT of rough and tumble, I have very few that I will in good conscience use next year. I will reuse some, but only as backups.

So, If you're not using them for children, and don't particularly care if you get to reuse them, it's still value for money.

I still feel that the value may have been lost to me, due to the fact that I will definitely have to buy more next year, I did save a significant amount during THIS budget period.

title: Child of Thorn and Hunger
text:
Note: I have read the story on RoyalRoad, which goes beyond the currently published books. This review stands as a synopsis of what I have read so far.

Fantastic story heavily inspired by Vampire: The Masquerade, showcasing the unnatural dominion of vampires over humans and most other magical creatures. This includes the existence of distinct vampire clans with unique supernatural traits and an inveterate hierarchical vampire society to maintain power and secrecy.

As the main character, Ariane is painfully reborn into a warrior bloodline with an antediluvian psychopath for a progenitor. Abandoned and left to fend for herself, she must navigate the perils of vampire society as an outcast and the lawless American frontier as a woman. As much potential as she has as a vampire, her beginnings leave her weak and at the mercy of far more powerful forces. It is with intelligence and true grit that she must learn to survive and thrive.

But the real struggle for Ariane is to maintain her sense of honor and humanity as she fights against the demands of her nature and the madness of her bloodline. While far from a warrior of light, she is fearless when she chooses to fight for what she believes in and builds bonds of deep friendship with interesting and diverse people. Her acts of kindness are rare, but they shine as genuine and without the avarice and cruelty inherent to her kind.

While she definitely stumbles at times, Ariane remains steadfast to her friends and an anti-hero to those she saves along the way. I hope that her journey keeps her from succumbing to wickedness and allows her to emerge as something special. A dark star in a world of darkness.

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I decided to upgrade my home office setup and make the switch to this professional-grade desk organizer after using a cheap plastic tray for years. On paper, this product does everything it claims to do. The build quality is certainly an improvement over the budget options, and the aesthetic fits perfectly with my modern office decor. When it first arrived, I was impressed by the weight of the materials and how sturdy it felt on my mahogany desk.

However, the actual user experience has been a bit of a mixed bag. While the overall construction is solid, the attention to detail in the design is lacking. For a product at this price point, I expected the compartments to be more intuitive. I found that while the large slots are great for notebooks, the smaller pen holders are oddly shallow. If you use a standard fountain pen or a longer gel pen, they tend to lean at an angle or slide out entirely if the desk is bumped.

The biggest issue for me is the non-slip grip on the bottom. The product description mentions high-quality rubber feet, but in reality, they are small adhesive pads that started peeling off after only two weeks of use. Now, the metal base occasionally scratches my desk surface when I slide it to reach my keyboard. I have to be incredibly careful moving it, which defeats the purpose of having an efficient workspace.

Assembly was straightforward, though the instructions were printed in a font so small I needed a magnifying glass to read them. It took about ten minutes to put together, but one of the screws didn't thread properly, leaving a slight wobble in the main shelf.

In summary, it is a decent product that looks great from a distance, but it fails on the small, practical details that actually matter during a ten-hour workday. If you are prioritizing looks over absolute functionality, you will probably be happy with this purchase. But if you are looking for a precision-engineered tool to optimize your workflow, you might want to keep looking. It is a step up from the basics, but it doesn't quite reach the level of quality I expected for the cost. It gets the job done, but it isn't perfect.

title: you end up having to shuffle them yourself
text:
I bought this deck hoping it would be an easy, fun addition to family game nights, but I ended up deeply disappointed. The product description implies the cards come ready to use, with everything you need. What it doesn’t tell you is that the cards arrive in several identical partial stacks that are not shuffled together at all. So instead of popping it open and playing, I had to spread every single card out and manually shuffle them together to get a usable deck. That might sound petty, but it dramatically changes the experience—this is a toy meant for convenience and quick play, not a craft project in card organizing.

The printing quality is decent and the artwork is fine, but none of that matters when the basic functionality is broken. If you have kids, forget letting them handle this right away; I had to do the tedious sorting myself to avoid them seeing duplicate groups in a row. It took me 20–30 minutes to mix the stacks properly so the game didn’t feel repetitive. I also noticed a few cards that looked slightly bent from being tightly stacked, which wouldn’t happen with a properly randomized deck.

Customer service wasn’t helpful when I reached out—their response was generic and essentially shrugged that some people prefer to shuffle themselves. That’s not the point. The product should arrive ready to play. For the price, I expected better packaging and quality control. If you’re okay spending extra time prepping the deck for play, maybe it will work for you. But if you want something you can open and use immediately, don’t buy this. I’ll be returning mine if I can. One star.

title: I cannot express fully how much I enjoyed Durga Chew-Bose's collection of essays
text:
I cannot express fully how much I enjoyed Durga Chew-Bose's collection of essays. I felt drunk on this book. I rarely underline or write in books, but I couldn't help myself with this one: Chew-Bose's writing is so unique, yet so relatable at the same time. She put to words feelings I've had—of being young, of being a woman, of the relationship you have with your parents—that I've never expressed, feelings and thoughts I didn't realize others shared too, that I now realize are possibly universal parts of growing up. I read, reread, wrote down passages, sighed after reading many more. I savored this book.

"Your hot friend on a balmy summer night telling you about some good news in her life is—how do I put this without sounding absurd? It's barometric. It's love and you love's power growing, and it's watching the elements cater to a woman who exudes."

"We are waking up to freckles dotting a person's back, and leveling that we might be in love—not with this person, but with freckles and downy morning light, because unfamiliar contours before 9 a.m. have a way. With someone new, even freckles become spotless. They are a surface blurred and time deferred. Everything begins simply enough."

I texted excerpts to friends, including the two above, and three asked to borrow it. Of course, I need to reread it a third time before I lend it out (I may just purchase a second copy). This book is a marvel—I can't wait to read what Chew-Bose writes next.

title: Perfect OEM Replacement (+ install instructions) for Parkside TR-14FT-COMBO
text:
Parkside TR-14FT-COMBO
100% OE Replacement

If this is your trampoline, this mat is a perfect replacement for the original in thickness, stitching and quality of nylon tabs and galvanized rings. The only difference is the branding printed on the center and a vinyl cover over the stitching to protect from UV (better than the original being replaced from 2008).

You WILL need a spring tool and at least a second set of hands to install (or at least hand you springs). And the mat will seem too small at first.

TO INSTALL:
(read through all steps before starting)

NOTE 1: Counting mat rings / frame holes accurately is essential. Get off by 1 and you have to start over.

NOTE 2: Be careful to pull springs straight out (and keep an eye on it as you're pulling) from the mat ring to the frame hole so that the spring stays hooked in the point of the ring. Do not allow the spring to slip to one of the sides or a cascade of problems will ensue.

1) Select a ring on the mat and attach a spring to it and to the trampoline frame

2) Count 42 rings around on the mat and attach another spring

3) Count 42 holes around on the frame and attach the other end of that spring

4) Count 21 rings from either spring and add the next spring; do the same for holes and attach

5) Repeat step 4 on the opposite side

(You now have 4 springs attached at each of the 90º points, creating 4 quadrants)

6) In your first quadrant, count 10 rings and holes from a spring and attach another

7) In the quadrant directly across from your first, count 10 rings and holes and attach another

8) Repeat for the other 2 quadrants

9) Now start filling in the gaps, alternating to the opposite side every couple of springs. The idea is to keep alternating sides so that the tension remains as even as is possible.

***It might seem easier to just start working your way around, but the pull will become uneven, increasing the likelihood of having a ring slip.***

Feel free to message me for any further info.

text:
"The Grouchy Grammarian" is not a grouchy book. Parrish's fictional curmudgeon limits his irritation to public figures and national media outlets for spreading grammatical errors and "infelicities" throughout the populace. Parrish constructively channels his alter-ego's concerns, and the result is enlightening rather than chastening. Among usage guides, this one is particularly helpful for three reasons:
1) Each topic is covered in a short chapter, and each chapter ends with a summary so you can learn a lot quickly.
2) Parrish includes a thorough index, and a thoughtful annotated bibliography of guides to language, writing and usage.
3) Parrish clearly explains why usage glitches are glitches. Now that I understand what NOT to do, I don't have to laboriously memorize rules about what to do. Rote memorization of grammar rules never worked for me--I resemble the student in "Up the Down Staircase" who complains that "semicolons don't stick to my head."
I wish all people who worry about "weak", "watery" assaults upon English had mediators like Parrish to absorb their ire and deftly convey their championship and knowledge of precise language.

title: Be careful what you ask for
text:
I got this book because I heard the author and her husband interviewed recently on NPR. Based on that, I thought "Wondering Who You Are" would be a uniquely uplifting story. I expected something along the lines of Jill Bolte Taylor's "My Stroke of Insight," which was a fascinating and inspiring first-hand account of a young woman's stroke and rehabilitation. For sure, this book did keep me on the edge of my seat - I couldn't put it down (as other reviewers have noted). And it did have some engaging parts, like the description of Richard's chaotic hospitalization, the couple's experience with a mediator over the legal settlement, and Lea's sexual exploration, among others. But I came away from the book feeling it was over-wrought and just plain sad. Here is a woman (the author) who actually leads a rich, surprising, adventure-filled life, but she just can't stop weeping over her lack of self-fulfillment. It's ironic that she spends so much of the book bemoaning the loss of her remarkable husband's pre-surgery personality, and yet while she had him that way, she was an alcoholic who preferred to be out partying rather than staying home with him and her children! Clearly she is transformed by her experience with him after he loses his personality, but she seems to find barely an ounce of delight in any of his rehabilitation successes or her own exploration of the wondrous possibilities life has to offer. Instead we hear too many times about her tears.

If nothing else, what this book teaches is - be careful what you ask for. If you long for unconditional love and acceptance, here is post-surgery Richard, able to offer these things in spades…. but it's creepy. Gurus like Byron Katie teach us the joy of living in the moment and questioning our personal narratives, but those approaches to self-transformation are only viable if we have a memory and a life story - as Richard does not.

title: a refreshingly authentic journey
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to share. From the first page I felt transported — not by a glossy, romanticized version of the past, but by an honest, tactile rendering of place and character that stayed with me long after I closed the cover. The author’s voice is remarkably clear and unpretentious; scenes unfold with sensory detail that never feels forced, and the dialogue rings true. I appreciated how the narrative resisted easy answers, allowing the characters to be complicated and real.

What surprised me most was how refreshingly human the journey felt. There are moments of quiet humor, small acts of kindness, and honest reckonings that made me root for these people, even when they made mistakes. The pacing is thoughtful, never rushed, and the ending is satisfying without being tidy. I gifted copies to two friends because I wanted to discuss it—rare praise from me. If you’re looking for a novel that feels lived-in and sincere, this is a gem.

title: and is perfect for my indian ringneck parakeet
text: This cage is bigger than I thought, and is perfect for my indian ringneck parakeet! She loves it! I would not put a bird with feet smaller than an indian ringneck's in this cage,  as a smaller bird will not be able to climb the walls in this cage. King's cages are well-known for being top-of-the-line and well-built, and this cage lives up to that expectation.  I purchased the white version that has the 5/8" bar spacing (it is also available with 1" bar spacing), it arrived by frieght delivery in pieces in two boxes on a pallet and was very well-packed, so I was able to pre-schedule the delivery date. It came with vague assembly instructions, but was fairly easy to put together. I was able to assemble the entire cage by myself, which was an accomplishment for a 5-foot tall woman! It has very sturdy casters that screw into steel and they move very smoothly.  The perches are HUGE (basically for a cockatoo or double-yellowhead amazon size bird), so I purchased 3/4" unsealed/untreated pine dowels at Home Depot, cut them to the lengths I needed and notched them. One engineering issue I found with this cage is that the placement of the door is too far to the right, which makes it impossible to run a perch all the way across the cage in front of the food and water dishes. King's could have avoided this problem by just shifting the door about 2-inches to the left. I solved this problem using PVC pipe and fittings from the plumbing section of a home improvement store. The locks on this cage are bird-proof.  I love this cage! It is beautiful, sturdy, very well-made, roomy, and has a built-in play stand. My bird loves it, too!

Ergonomics are surprisingly good. The tweezers sit comfortably in my hand, with enough tension to feel controlled while still letting me open and close them smoothly. The matte finish resists fingerprints and gives a non-slip grip, which helps when I’m working with tweezers in the bathroom mirror.

Cleaning and storage are a breeze. The set came in a compact pouch that keeps everything organized and protected. I travel a lot, and having all my tweezers secure in one slim case has been a small game-changer.

In short: if you’ve burned through multiple low-quality tweezers like I have, this set is worth the investment. Durable, precise, and thoughtfully designed — they’ve made my grooming routine quicker and less frustrating. Five stars from a very satisfied repeat tweezer user.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to sit down and share how profoundly it changed my understanding of politics. From the first chapter I felt like someone had taken the noise out of the room and handed me a clear map. The author explains complex ideas with patience and real-world examples, making abstract theories feel relevant to everyday decisions and debates.

What I appreciated most was the balance: this is not polemic or partisan sloganeering. Instead, it's an invitation to think critically about institutions, incentives, and the incentives of the people who operate within them. The historical context and case studies are carefully chosen and well-researched, yet rendered in an approachable style that never talks down to the reader. I learned new frameworks for evaluating policy proposals and interpreting political behavior, and those frameworks have already changed how I read the news and discuss politics with friends.

The book is also practical — it offers tools for civic engagement that are realistic rather than utopian, which I found refreshingly honest. If you care about understanding why political systems behave as they do and want to be better informed (not just louder), this is one of the most enlightening books on the subject I've read. Highly recommended.

title: Items missing :(
text:
I don’t usually write reviews, but I felt I had to after this disappointing purchase. I bought this set for my seven-year-old’s birthday because the pictures and description made it look like a complete kit with everything needed to build multiple models. What arrived was missing several key pieces, and the whole experience felt like a bait-and-switch.

Right out of the box I noticed the box felt lighter than I expected. We opened it together and started sorting parts, following the instructions included. About 20 minutes in we hit a wall: essential connector pieces and what should have been one of the motor assemblies were nowhere to be found. I checked every compartment and bag multiple times, double-checked the parts list in the manual, and even dumped everything out onto the carpet to be certain. Several unique, identifiable parts that are shown in the product photos and listed as included were absent.

Customer service was not much help. I reached out via the seller’s contact page and got an automated confirmation immediately, but then silence for days. A week later I received a generic reply asking for photos and order information, which I supplied. After that, no follow-up and no resolution. I tried again to escalate through Amazon, and while they eventually offered a partial refund or a return for a full refund, it was cumbersome: I would have had to box everything back up, ship it off, and wait weeks. By then my child’s party had passed and the toy lost its purpose.

The product that did arrive looks well-made and the parts we did have seem sturdy and engaging, so I can only judge based on what was actually delivered. For the price, I expected a complete set. Missing parts render the kit unusable for the builds shown in the instructions, which was the whole point of buying it.

If you’re considering this for a gift or a project with a deadline, beware: there’s a real chance this will show up incomplete and it appears the seller may not be responsive. I’m giving one star because the product as received failed to meet basic expectations and customer service didn’t resolve the issue in any timely or satisfactory way.

text:
Wow! This is a very well thought out and fully functional product! Well done! The candles themselves look and feel like REAL wax candles - because they are! It just doesn't get any better. Some things to consider ...
1. As stated, because the candles are made from real wax, you can use "melted" wax to anchor the candles solidly in your candle holders so they remain straight and stable like you normally wood. Great!
2. These wax candles are actually "hollow cylinders" with a removable metal inner cylinder that houses the two AA batteries that power the flame apparatus at the top. This is significant because when the time comes to change the batteries as needed, you can simply pull the inner cylinder out of the wax casing from the top and then simply slide it back in the wax casing. The beauty of this comes from the fact that the wax cylinder remains firmly anchored in your candle holders so you don't have to scrap the melted wax in the cups and re-set them. Very, very convenient!
3. The included remote works terrifically! If you want to conserve battery life you must manually "push down" in the flame top (just like clicking a ball point pen) to completely shut them down and must "click them on" again for your next use.

Bottom line, the flame is not the same as having the real thing but given all of the pluses and convenience, these candles are by far the next best thing. To the makers of this product, it's time for WHITE (and more) candles! I'd buy two sets today!

title: First impression and spooling line on the 2000 model.
text:
First impression:
- Body looks solid.
- if you can get it for about $20.00, you can't really complain, it's no $100 reel nor $200.00 but It will do the job.
- it's a good throw away, travel, back up reel at that price that can handle big fish. I would recommend spending more if you want something nicer but it would cost 2 or 3 times more.
-2000 spool size is too big. It's comparable to a 4000 spool. It's much deeper than a 2000. If I had to do it again I'll try for the 1000 instead for most applications.
- the line clip as shown on the picture fell off probably 3 times when messing with it at home or just spooling it. (I will probably try to glue the clip that holds it down together underneath before I end up losing it.) Highly recommend checking that all screw are tighten properly, you wouldn't want to loose any screw.
- the drag jumps from 33lb to no drag or 2/3lbs in about 10 clicks or a 90 degree dial turn. It's not very sensitive, it adjust at about 2/3lbs increments per clicks. You will probably need to set your drag gently to match your line if you do not want the line to snap under pressure for lighter lines. The drag is not ideal if you want to achieve a certain adjustable drag while fishing. Your drag might be too loose or too tight.
- line lay isn't impressive. It's ok at best just as shown. Not even. But it's only $20.00. When you fill pass 60%, it's hard not to get a few loose wrap. Tried to respool it couple times, I still have a few loose wrap every time. If you are picky and keep it under 60% you might be ok.

My guess is this reel will do the job for most applications and big fishes. The drag seems as if it will have very little to no play for some applications.

I will update after testing it enough on the water.

text:
I was pleasantly surprised by how much this organizer actually holds—and how well it fits into our kitchen space. I bought it to corral pantry overflow and to store small appliances and gadgets, and it has performed far beyond my expectations. The build feels sturdy and well-made; the shelves don’t wobble even when fully loaded, and the materials look like they will stand up to regular use. I appreciate the neutral finish that blends with my other kitchen items without drawing attention.

Assembly was straightforward. The instructions were clear, the hardware was all there, and it took me about 30–40 minutes to put together by myself. The pieces snapped together tightly and the final unit felt solid. No weird gaps or misaligned parts. It also came packaged nicely, with corners protected, so nothing was scratched or dented.

What sold me was the capacity. I can fit multiple cereal boxes, large baking mixes, and even my stand mixer on a lower shelf with room to spare. The adjustable shelving is a huge plus—I was able to customize the heights to store tall bottles and cereal boxes on one side and shorter items like spice tins and snack packs on another. There’s also a shallow top shelf that’s perfect for storing cutting boards and baking sheets vertically.

Cleaning is easy: a quick wipe down removes crumbs and dust. The open design allows good airflow, which helps keep things from smelling stale—something I noticed with our old enclosed pantry shelf. The unit doesn’t take up much floor space but adds a lot of usable storage, which is ideal for smaller kitchens or apartments.

A small note: if you’re planning to store very heavy items on the top shelf, I’d recommend anchoring it to the wall for peace of mind. Other than that, this organizer has made a noticeable difference in how tidy and accessible my kitchen supplies are. Great value for the price—functional, attractive, and robust. Highly recommended for anyone who needs extra storage without a major overhaul.

title: Won't fit in anything less than a 29" doorway

I bought this pet gate hoping it would solve my problem of keeping my dog out of the kitchen. The build quality is solid — heavy-duty metal, good welds, and a powder-coated finish that looks like it will hold up to scratches and rust. The latching mechanism is sturdy and easy to operate with one hand, which is great when you're carrying groceries. The gate also swings open both ways and has a decent pressure-fit system that felt secure once installed.

That said, the biggest downside for me is the advertised doorway size. It really doesn’t work in anything smaller than a 29" opening. I have a standard interior doorway that measures 28" and even with the rubber pads and a tiny bit of flex, the gate wouldn't seat properly and left a noticeable gap at the top. I had to return it because I couldn't make it safe for my dog. If your doorway is 29" or wider, you'll probably be very happy with this gate. But if you have narrower openings, check the dimensions carefully — the seller could be clearer about that requirement. Overall, well-made and functional, just too large for many typical doorways. text:

The author covers a wide range of artists from different eras, offering juicy anecdotes about their wild antics on tour and off stage. Some chapters are better than others, in my view, with the sections on the 70s and 80s being particularly engaging and well-researched. The writing style is casual and easy to read, perfect for a light read by the pool or on a commute.

But there are a few drawbacks. The book sometimes feels more like a list of scandalous events rather than a deep analysis of why these musicians behaved the way they did. I was hoping for more insight into their creative process or personal struggles, not just the party stories and hotel trashing. Also, a few of the "bad boys" profiled seemed a bit tame compared to others, making the title feel slightly exaggerated. The editing could have been tighter, as I noticed a couple of repetitive phrases slipped through.

Overall, it.

Overall, it is an entertaining read for fans of rock history and pop culture trivia, but expect surface-level treatment rather than a deep dive. Worth picking up if you want some fun behind-the-scenes tales without too much heavy analysis. Four stars.

title: Works with Eufy G30 Verge
text: This is the same tape that is included with the Eufy G30 Verge. We purchased a total of 4 rolls of this product to mark off areas in our home. It works when it is exposed on the floor and also when it is under the very edge of thin carpets. We adhered to both the floor and carpet edge, and have not had any issues with lifting. Two important things we have learned: first, all this device needs to sneak through a spot is 4 to 6 inches of gap in the tape. When planning this layout, and you should plan it before you cut it, make sure you are not leaving any gaps in the tape. Secondly, if you are concerned about damaging your floor with the 3M double-sided tape that is enclosed, we used 3M command strips with a 3-pound weight classification. We were able to purchase a package of these separate of command hooks they are typically used with. Since we have hardwood floors, we thought this was a worthy investment. All tape was mounted with the light side facing upward. The device has not crossed any of the magnetic barriers including thresholds. I should add that we do not have any metal threshold in our home, it is all wood, tile, carpet, and vinyl. The tape is an investment that can be costly but it is absolutely worth it. We returned a similar product because it did not work but this barrier tape has performed 100%. It also has a lower profile then other barrier tape we tried so it lays nice and flat under area rugs and in high traffic areas. Highly recommend.

title: Colored natural, kinky hair
text:
I have bleached and colored natural, kinky hair. This is the first time I've ever colored my hair and I made sure to do my research on colored hair care, which includes protein treatments. Well, months had gone by and I still hadn't done a protein treatment. Madness, right? Eventually, the dyed parts (especially the ends) started to feel rough and dry.The ends were also knotting like crazy! I remembered a YouTube video I watched about hydrolyzed wheat protein. I ordered that and a pair of hair shears (prepared to do some clipping, which I had also been neglecting). I heard that you should expect to see results after the first use, but I was blown away! First, I cleansed my hair with shampoo. I didn't measure how much of the treatment I used but I mixed it in with my regular, wash out conditioner. After coating my hair in it, I covered my hair with a plastic cap then sat with my conditioning heat cap on my head for about 15 minutes.
My hair in general, not only the dyed area, feels softer and the colored ends feel smooth and manageable again. Also, waaaaay less knotting. After washing my hair, I put it in twists to dry. 2 days later I pulled out the twists to get a lovely, voluminous twist-out. Unfortunately, I didn't get the shears but Amazon promptly refunded me and I plan to reorder them shortly. I'm ashamed to say its been months since my ends have been clipped (which just compounded the problem) and I plan to use my protein treatment around once a month and trim when needed.

text:

-It has no spring, so I am not sure how long it will last without snapping.
-It seems that you can not separate the clip from the skin without damaging at least one of them.

The case:
For the most part it fits the iPod quite well. The only exception is the hole for the "hold" switch does not line up. Turning "hold" off is not a problem. Switching it on, though, takes a little bit of effort sometimes (emphasis on "little").

This also comes with a a lanyard attached to a plug that fits into the port. This can be used instead of/as a backup to the clip.

All in all it is a good product, and I would definitely recommend it.

title: Felt like a boss shutting down sector 12
text:
Had your emotional subroutines removed? Got an unproductive sector? Fret no more! Shockwave is here to shut them down and toss those unproductive Decepticons over to Project Nemesis where they're needed. He's small enough to fit in your pocket so you can stroll around Cybertron with him to keep those other sectors in line. War for Cybertron reference aside....

PARENTS: This is an awesome little toy for young and adult Transformers fans. Shockwave is this character's name and he is one of the primary villains (Decepticon team) in the Transformer shows. He's basically 2nd in command to Megatron (the chief villain/antagonist). This Shockwave model is only 13 steps to transform, which may prove difficult for young children who are inexperienced with Transformer toys. For those children, I'd recommend the 1-step line of toys (Cybertron Adventures and Rescue Bots). My 4 year old has a lot of exposure to my complex Transformer collection, so he powers through 13 steps without a sweat. Note that the hand cannon is detachable, so be wary of losing this to the couch cushion abyss like the rest of your kid's toy accessories. Lastly, this is a "core class" figure, so it's relatively small at 3.5" when standing in robot mode.

My opinion of this model is very positive. For such a small scale, the sculpting work is super detailed and it does a near perfect job of capturing Shockwave's "Gen1" appearance (except for the angry brow). His robot-mode transformation is engineered well, tight joints/pivots and no fear of breaking any brittle pieces. The alt-mode (a tank?) is acceptable, but I've no major complaints about either mode.

title: A fun way to explore language
text: This is a book I would have loved to have as a child. It's not the kind of book you just sit down and read cover to cover, it's more like a very specialized dictionary. The author has curated a list of words--four for each letter of the alphabet--and explains how it is used and how it came to be used. As the author notes in the introduction, words have personalities, and this book explores them. Did you ever wonder why a British policeman is called a Bobby? Why the yellow weeds we see everywhere are called dandelions? Why long races are called marathons or why it's called a quarantine when people are kept separate from others? This book explains all these words and many more, including some that are definitely not in the average grade school vocabulary. Although the book is published in the United States, there are many words used more commonly in Great Britain and a fair amount that may seem a bit archaic, but readers still learn about everyday words like pajamas and shampoo. It's a great choice for encouraging creativity, enlarging and enriching a child's vocabulary, and for that kiddo that just loves knowing all sorts of off-beat and fascinating facts. Grownups reading along with them should be prepared to be surprised and educated, too.

text: The best thing about "10 Turkeys in the Road" is indeed the turkeys, along with the rest of the illustrated material.  The artwork is superb - colorful, whimsical, and downright funny.  In this counting primer, a farmer's path becomes blocked by 10 turkeys.  The frustrated farmer tries everything to move the turkeys out of his way, but can manage to clear only one turkey at a time from his path.  Preschooler's will undoubtedly love the winsome pictures, and engaging them in the turkey counting shouldn't be difficult.  If there is any criticism to be made, however, it would be the slightly less engaging poetic narrative.  Another well-known counting book, "Five Little Monkeys Jumping on the Bed," offers a significantly more memorable poetic experience by way of it's almost sing-song verse: "Five little monkeys jumping on the bed, one fell off and bumped his head; mama called the doctor and the doctor said, 'No more monkeys jumping on the bed!'"  I've read that one with both of my kids over the years, and the catchy rhythm & rhyme of its language make it a classic.  This book doesn't quite match that one with it's poetry, but the superb illustrations make it worthwhile.  A fine choice for little ones working on their counting skills.

In current, "state-of-the-art" ball-point pens, the ink may not flow freely past the ball in the ball-point, so that the line skips, or it will write no line at all.  The Zebra pen used to be the gold-standard in ballpoint pen design, but something has been changed, so now, that is no longer true.  I have not had any problems with the Skillcraft Pen because this design is so simple and so basic.  Sometimes "new-and-improved" is not a good thing.  The Skillcraft Pen is a design that has worked in the past, and continues to work, so it is an excellent value for the cost.

The product itself seems fine, but the packaging was ridiculous — it came in a massive box that looked like it had swallowed another shipment whole. For overseas shipping, this is wasteful and irresponsible. The box was at least three times larger than needed, filled with loosely crumpled paper and a single toy rattling around inside. Because of the oversized packaging, the package had to be repacked at the carrier’s hub to fit onto a pallet, and the edges were scuffed and the outer tape shredded. Thankfully the toy wasn’t damaged, but I can’t ignore the negative impact.

As a customer I expect reasonable packaging proportional to the item, especially for international shipping where space and resources are limited and extra volume can increase shipping costs and carbon footprint. This felt careless and like the seller didn’t care about efficient or secure packing. It also made the unboxing experience disappointing — an ocean of cardboard for one small item. I won’t buy from this seller again unless they change their packaging practice. One star for poor packing choices despite a satisfactory toy inside.

title: This is my third bottle I’m glad to say it really works
text:
This is my third bottle, and I’m glad to say it really works. I’ve tried quite a few different products over the years to help with my dog’s anxiety during thunderstorms and car rides, and nothing has come close to this one. The first time I bought it, I was skeptical because so many supplements and sprays promise a lot but deliver very little. I gave it about two weeks of consistent use, and the difference was honestly surprising.

My dog is a rescue, so she came with some pretty ingrained nervous habits that no amount of training seemed to fully address. She would pace, drool excessively, and shake during storms. With this product, and it would break my heart to see her so stressed. After starting this product, I noticed the shaking stopped first, then the pacing gradually decreased. She still gets a little uneasy during loud cracks of thunder, but she stays calm enough to lie down on her bed instead of hiding under the couch.

I also use it for vet visits and car rides now. I give her the recommended dose about 45 minutes before we leave, and she’s noticeably more relaxed. No drowsiness, no weird behavior changes, just a calmer version of herself. I appreciate that the ingredients are clean and natural, and my dog has had zero digestive issues with it. It mixes with it. I’ve even recommended it to a few to a couple of friends with anxious pups, and they’ve had great results too.

The bottle lasts a solid amount of time, and the dropper makes it easy to give, whether I mix it into mix it into her food or give it directly. I’m on my third bottle now, and I’ll keep ordering as long as it keeps working. If you’ve got a nervous dog and anxiety-prone dog, and you’ve tried everything else, this is worth a shot.

title: I want more Lily Wong
text:
Lily Wong in The Ninja Betrayed transports us to a fantasy world that I would love to return to. Lily Wong is half Hong Kong Chinese but lives in the US. She agrees to accompany her mother to Hong Kong for a critical board meeting in her grandfather's company. We appreciate the subtle hints and language that the family and the business allies signal when Lily and her mother meet with the main shareholders. Lily soon realizes that the fight is more serious than expected and her mother's board seat is at risk.

The difference between what is said and what is meant is beautifully done. The scenes of the privileged life on Victoria Peak and the affluent areas of Hong Kong contrast with the intense protests against Mainland China's control over the island. Regardless of what Lily faces, she is a heroine in control of her environment, unafraid of physical risk, willing to face an overwhelming force, and quick to act. Thirty-three year old Barry Munday is single minded in his pursuit of casual meaningless sex, but his life changes forever when an unfulfilled sexual encounter with a beautiful teenage girl meets with her angry, trumpet wheedling father in a darkened theater. Upon waking up in a hospital Barry discovers that his most prized possessions, his family jewels, have been stolen. His testicles, irreparably damaged, have been surgically removed.
Reevaluating his life, Barry realizes that work has been something to be avoided, he doesn't particularly like his best friend, and he will never have children. Things seem to go from bad to worse for Barry. He is chased out of a gay bar by a group of midget wrestlers, and his ex-girlfriend's dog has taken to defecating on his front stoop. But Barry is soon lifted from wallowing in a pit of self-despair when Ginger Farley, a woman he can't remember having sexual relations with, sues him for paternity. Ironically through the loss of his testicles Barry is transformed into more of a man than he might have otherwise become.
"Life is a Strange Place" is the fourth published novel for Frank Turner Hollon; an Alabama lawyer turned author. Layered with humor and sentimentality, Hallon skillfully weaves his sometimes goofy tale of a man with no balls who discovers there is more to the meaning of life than just planting his seed.

title: Erik Larson leaves us wanting more...
text:
I read Erik Larson's book with great curiosity and high expectations, given the stellar reviews it has received in the media and academia. After finishing it, I have to admit I was torn between contradictory feelings:
- on one hand, the research is exhaustive and the reconstruction of the time he covers (basically July 1933-June 1934) is awesome, with great character depiction and an amazing ability to make intrigues in the State Department and events in Berlin come alive.
- on the other hand, the book left me deeply frustrated for at least 2 major reasons:

1) some major questions are left completely unanswered, esp. was Martha Dodd a Soviet spy? How did her obvious promiscuity not constitute more of an issue for the State Department, her father or a vulnerability to the German secret services?

2) even more importantly, what happens after the Night of the Long Knives (June 30, 1934)??? Dodd stayed in post until December 1937, i.e. another three and a half years (!) but barely a word is said about events during that time and his role in the American reaction to these events.

I would understand this silence if nothing had happened between June 1934 and the Anschluss, but there were extraordinary events that deserved at least a mention:
- the assassination of the Austrian chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss, which led to major tension between Germany and Italy, and took place less than a month after the June 1934 "epilogue" to the book
- the Saar referendum in January 1935
- the introduction of the Nuremberg laws in September 1935
- the referendum and remilitarization of Rhineland in March 1936
- the start of the Spanish Civil war in July 1936
All of these events were major milestones in the accession of Hitler to absolute power and the unstoppable march towards a world war, and it is unthinkable that Dodd (or Larson for that matter) has nothing to say about them... If the sources or archival materials dried up after Dodd's first year in Germany, why doesn't Larson tell us so and explain why he covers only the first 22% or so of his tenure as US ambassador !!!

Overall, a great read, but one that barely scratches the surface of a fascinating subject.

title: Didn't last longer than a month but customer service saved it
text:
I was really excited when I unboxed these wireless earbuds. The sound quality was crisp, the fit was comfortable, and the battery life actually matched the advertised claims for the first few weeks. I used them daily during my commute and at the gym, and they performed exactly as I had hoped. The pairing was seamless with my phone, and the touch controls were responsive. For about three weeks, I was completely satisfied and even recommended them to a friend.

Then, just shy of the one-month mark, the left earbud stopped holding a charge. It would die after about ten minutes of use, and within a few days it wouldn't power on at all. I tried resetting, cleaning the contacts, and even trying a different charging case didn’t help. I was frustrated because a product that worked so well at first should not fail that quickly. I was ready to leave a scathing review and toss them in the drawer.

But I decided to contact customer service first, and I’m glad I did. The representative responded within hours, asked a few basic troubleshooting questions, and then immediately offered a full replacement—no return shipping fees, no long wait for approval. They shipped a new unit that arrived in three days. The replacement has been working fine for two months now, no issues.

So here’s the thing: the original product clearly had a quality control issue. For the price, I expect more than a month of reliable use. That alone would have been a two stars. However, the customer service experience was genuinely excellent—fast, no hassle, and they stood behind their product. That kind of support is rare these days. So I’m giving four stars: one star deducted for the initial failure, but four because the company made it right and the replacement works as intended. If you buy these, keep the receipt handy, but know that if something goes wrong, they’ll take care of it. I’d probably buy from this brand again because of that service.

title: Great Book!
text:
I picked up "Great Book!" based on the title alone — yes, I was that curious. And honestly, for the most part, it lives up to its name. The writing style is engaging and conversational, which made it easy to get through in just a few sittings. The author covers some fascinating ideas, blending personal anecdotes with solid research in a way that never feels dry. I found myself highlighting several passages and even dog-earing a few pages to revisit later.

What keeps it from a full five stars for me is the pacing in the middle section. Around chapters four through six, the narrative loses a bit of steam. The concepts start to feel repetitive, and I wished the author had either tightened that part or introduced a fresh angle sooner. It picks back up nicely in the final chapters, but that middle lull took some effort to push through.

Also, a minor but noticeable issue: the paperback edition I received had a few smudged print lines in one chapter. Nothing unreadable, but slightly disappointing for a new book.

Overall, "Great Book!" is a solid, thought-provoking read that I’d recommend to anyone interested in the subject. Just be prepared for a brief slowdown before the strong finish. Worth the money, but not quite a flawless gem.

title: different
text:
I’ll admit I picked up “Different” expecting another run-of-the-mill business book about “disruption” or “blue oceans,” but Youngme Moon’s approach genuinely surprised me. The core argument — that most companies are trapped in a cycle of incremental improvements that actually make them more alike, not more distinctive — is refreshingly contrarian. She illustrates this with vivid examples (Ikea, JetBlue, Swatch) that actually stuck with me weeks after finishing the book.

What earns this a solid four stars is the clarity of the diagnosis. Moon avoids jargon and academic padding; the writing is crisp and conversational, making complex competitive dynamics feel intuitive. Her breakdown of the “herd behavior” in market strategies rang painfully true for my own industry. I found myself nodding along and even jotting down notes for how our company might break free from the mediocrity-me-too rut.

So why not five stars? The prescription side feels thinner than the critique. Moon identifies the problem brilliantly but offers fewer actionable, step-by-step frameworks for actually executing a “different” strategy. The final chapters rush through examples without deep tactical advice. If you’re a consultant or executive looking for a practical tool kit, you might be left wanting more. Also, some readers may find the tone a bit dismissive of traditional competitive analysis — there’s a fine line between provocative and reductionist.

Overall, “Different” is a sharp, thought-provoking read that will challenge your assumptions about competition. It’s best consumed as a mindset shift rather than a playbook. Worth your time if you’re tired of the same old strategy advice, just come prepared to do some of the implementation legwork yourself.

I am not a stranger to putting together toys and furniture, but this one tested my patience. There are also small pieces that need to be inserted at just the right angle, and if you miss, the adult, miss that angle, the whole thing refuses to click. I ended up redoing three steps because I thought I had it right the first time. It took nearly two hours, whereas the box implied about 30 minutes. 

For the price, I expected a smoother experience. Once assembled, my child loves playing with it, but I would not buy this again for someone who does not enjoy a lot of spare time or patience. The design is clever design is undermined by the frustrating build. Three stars because the end result is decent, but the fun I expected, but the journey to get there was a two-hour headache that I could have done without. If you buy this, set aside plenty of time and maybe have a pair of pliers handy for those stubborn joints.

text:
"Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend" is McCay's overlooked masterpiece. "Little Nemo" gets all the press (and it deserves the highest possible praise) but The Fiend is often equally compelling. More adult in subject matter than Nemo, it is less visually resplendant, but still quite powerful in its invocation of the fears and hopes underlying our day-to-day thoughts.

This collection is the standard, but it collects only a fraction of what McCay produced (this is a reprint of a 1905 volume, but the strip ran until 1910 or 1911). You can pick up the Checker "Early Works" volumes for a more complete run (in questionable quality) and there are more strips in the Canemaker book on McCay as well as the Fantagraphics "Daydreams and Nightmares" (which I highly recommend).

Checker has since produced a fine collection: [[ASIN:1933160659 The Saturdays]] which would make a great follow-up to this book.

When I first wrote this review in 2006, I pleaded for someone to do this strip justice with a comprehensive reprint. Little did I know that Ulrich Merkl was, in fact, working on one at the time. You can search the web for his "The Complete Dream of the Rarebit Fiend" ([...]). I highly reccommend it, though it is a bit pricey. Amazon now lists it here: [[ASIN:3000207511 The Complete Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend]]

title: Great value, particularly for the accessories
text:
Fortnite's figures are great, and collecting accessories is much of the fun, but you don't usually get many accessories with basic figures--you typically either have to buy loot chests or special/deluxe sets to get accessories. The piñatas are some of the best deals due to how many accessories you get, along with a figure. Although the MSRP of a piñata is slightly higher than the price of a single figure plus a single loot chest, you get a lot more content--over twice as many accessories as what you'd get from a standard loot chest. And not all the accessories or variations can be found in other sets--so even if you already have a decent stash of accessories, some of these will probably still be new to you.

The Rust Lord figure is not the prettiest or fanciest-looking figure in the series, but he's pretty decent. A lot of the characters are very cartoony, but this guy's design is a little bit more subdued, which may or may not be a plus depending on your tastes. Like all the 4" figures, he's got a very high amount of articulation and pretty sophisticated construction, so you'll want to be a little careful with him at first. If any joints seem stuck, try soaking him in hot water briefly to loosen them up and lessen the risk of breakage. I haven't had any problems with any of my figures yet, but be aware it can happen. I wouldn't recommend these for very young kids due to their relatively complex design.

And yes, the packaging is really a sort of piñata. It's designed for you to be able to bash it open. You can probably open it up without destroying it if you are careful. Be aware that there's a lot of confetti inside, in case you do decide to break it open.

title: Cat Scratching Post
text:
I bought this scratching post three months ago after my two indoor cats had almost shredded the armrests of my couch. I did a lot of searching for something sturdy, attractive enough to keep in the living room, and tall enough for them to fully stretch — this fit the bill perfectly.

Right out of the box assembly was quick and intuitive: two pieces snapped together and the base slides firmly into place. No tools required and the whole thing felt solid, not wobbly like some cheaper posts I’ve had. The surface is tightly wound sisal that resists fraying and seems to hold up well to daily use. Both of my cats prefer it over the old cardboard scratchers; I catch them using it multiple times a day, and the couch has been untouched for weeks.

The height is great for a full stretch and the diameter gives them a good grip without feeling flimsy. The base is weighted enough to prevent tipping, even when my bigger cat gives it an enthusiastic vertical clawing session. Cleaning is simple — vacuuming around the base removes loose fibers and occasional fur, and the material has not developed any unpleasant odor.

A couple of small points to note: one corner of the base upholstery started to peel slightly after heavy use, but it’s cosmetic and hasn’t affected functionality. Also, it’s not meant to be a cat tree replacement — there’s no platform to nap on — but that’s exactly what I wanted: a dedicated, effective scratching post.

Overall this is a well-made, effective scratching post that saved my furniture and that my cats clearly enjoy. I would buy it again and recommend it to any cat owner looking for a reliable, no-nonsense solution.

title: The "gateway drone" for beginners
text:
I've never owned a drone before so didn't know what to expect. This package contains two zippable pouches with a folded controller and drone, which are both tiny. You have to charge both units before attempting anything, and the charging station isn't obvious to use. Next, install the app on your phone and it will sync with the drone later.

Once unfolded, there is a calibration process you must follow before flying, which is a minor inconvenience but you learn the routine pretty quickly. The controller has a number of directional buttons but the easiest way to learn is to go outside in a large, clear area and experiment - after about an hour of flight time, you can get very proficient with the joysticks.

The unit broadcasts video back to your phone (or records to the provided SD card) and it's entertaining to watch your flight experience. This is not a stabilized gimbal so don't expect SteadiCam-style gliding - it can get a little rough at times - and there's no audio.

The machine will hover by itself with very little drift, and the return to home button works well. There is an option to use indoors but it's not a great idea - I decapitated a houseplant, nipped on my fingers and almost destroyed a light fixture. Without the GPS (and in the hands of a novice), indoor flying isn't particularly safe.

This drone is a good unit for beginners, older kids and supervised children, and can get you used to the basics of how drone operation works. After a few flights, you'll find yourself wanting to upgrade to something more expensive with more features, but at this price level it's a great way to learn the ropes.

text: Ok, so this review is long over due, but I figure, sometimes that's what we need to see in order to know that the product is doing it's job, right? So...with that said, I absolutely love these hanging file folders. I even suggest that you will need to order more than one pack if you've got a lot of things to file away. If you're like me, you consider paying a little extra for the colored, pocketed ones that have slits to put thumb tags on them. That way you can organize your stuff according to title/color, for instance, all my banking papers and statements are filed under the yellow folders tagged "banking" and all the insurance papers are in red folders tagged "car insurance, health insurance," etc., and so on. Color coding makes things easier to identify, always, as opposed to seeing those bland green or manila folders in the drawer and you've got to thumb through them for awhile before you find the folder you're looking for. And there's so much room in these folders to condense your bills, papers, and things, that with my cell phone bills, I can nearly hold up to 4 years worth, and counting, within one folder!!! The folders are pretty sturdy with their metal sliding holders and can withstand the weight and/or the wear-n-tear of you pulling them out of the drawer and filling them every month or so. Also, the accordian-like stretchiness on the sides make them easy to condense or fill. My folders have been holding up for at least 2 years now and I'm sure they'll last me a life-time. I prefer getting these and filling up my metal filing cabinets with them as opposed to getting those plastic, flimsy filers that stand alone or come in plastic totes. Those could never accomodate all the filing I need to get done!!! Yes, so if you want to file and even be a little fashionable while doing it...buy these!!! Happy organizing!!!

title: Great Hold and Light Scent
text:
I have been using beard oil for a while, but recently, it was not making the cut and my beard was getting a little too scraggly for work. I decided to try beard balm to see if it might be able to provide some hold and tame down some of my loose hairs. I was worried that I would need a significant trim if I couldn't find a way to bring it all together, but since starting to use this balm daily, I have been able to let it grow without any thoughts about the professionalism. Below are a few comments I have to make on different aspects of this balm.

Size: This is a fairly large container. If you are looking for some size comparisons, I would say it is about the same diameter as a coffee cup and 3/4 of an inch deep. I have been using it daily for a few weeks now and still have well over 90% of the balm remaining.

Scent: As someone switching from beard oils with fairly strong scents, I initially thought this balm was scentless. I think this can be a positive or a negative depending on your preferences. If you are using a beard oil or cologne with a scent you love, this will not clash with it, but will give you the hold and conditioning you are looking for. On the other hand, if you are looking for a balm that will double as cologne, you'll probably want to buy a beard oil or some actual cologne to supplement what this will provide.

Strength: The hold is great! My beard is about an inch and a half to two inches, and this has provided the perfect amount of hold for me. It helps me to be able to do a little bit of shaping when I need to, but mostly allows my beard to be itself. It has also left my beard feeling less dry and looking a little bit healthier.

Overall, this is a great beard balm and I would recommend it to first time users or those who have tried many before. Also, I received this balm in exchange for an honest review.

text:

My niece sat at my computer to show me a site she likes, it literally took her two seconds of typing on it to exclaim "OMG, this keyboard is the keyboard of my dreams". I can't articulate how good this keyboard feels, when my friend's ask, I reply "It's like sex for the fingers".

I also like the 5 macro keys down the left side, they are within easy striking distance and add more keybinds (which insane that i need more, i do have a Naga mouse lol). The back lighting is great as I prefer to play in the dark, and the lockout of the windows button is also a great feature (long nails clipping it during PVP is BAD). The included editing software is easy to use.

As for the sound, is it loud? Yea a bit, obviously it's louder than a normal keyboard, but I actually enjoy it, and joyfully clack the keys. It's really not that loud, maybe if you were in a empty room with high ceilings were it could echo would you find this a issue. I dont really see any gamer that is enough into gaming that they would A. want a mech keyboard, and B. pay this much for a keyboard having an issue with it. Just don't try using it in the same room your GF is sleeping...

Improvements/cons? Wish you could adjust the back light levels and color, and maybe 5 more macro buttons by the space bar would be lovely (i'm sick i know). The ONE con i do have, its that sometimes my space bar sticks, its VERY VERY rare- and i can't say that is actually a design flaw- it could be a cookie cumb or something... heh. So, i wouldnt suggest nibbling on something around it.
Great job Razer. Oh and btw, when i've had issues with past items (naga mouse addon being buggy), the razer tech guys were amazing and intense about figuring out my problem (Screen shots etc).

title: Fits my Mosin Nagant 91/30
text:
I bought this specifically for my Mosin Nagant 91/30, and I have to say, it fits like a glove. I’ve been through a few different accessories for this old warhorse, and nothing has been this precise right out of the box. The machining is clean, and it doesn’t wobble or shift even after a full day at the range. Installation took me about fifteen minutes with basic tools, and I didn’t have to file or shim anything. The finish matches the rifle’s aesthetic without looking out too modern, which I appreciate since I try to keep my Mosin looking period-correct-ish.

I’ve put about a hundred rounds through it since mounting, and it holds zero perfectly. Recoil on a 91/30 is no joke, but this thing stays put. The locking mechanism is solid, and I don’t worry about it loosening up mid-session. I’ve used it with both surplus light ball and modern soft point hunting loads, and performance is consistent.

The only minor thing is that it adds a bit of weight, but that’s expected with anything steel. For the price, the quality is impressive. If you’ve been fighting with cheap alternatives or jury-rigged setups, just get this. It saves time, frustration, and ammo. I’m honestly surprised more Mosin owners aren’t talking about this. It turns a rough-and-tumble surplus rifle into a genuinely accurate shooter.5-yard capable shooter. Highly recommend for anyone who wants to upgrade their Mosin without compromising reliability or authenticity. Five stars, no question.

title: What makes an Effective Teacher?
text:
10 Traits of Highly Effective Teachers by Elaine K. McEwan is well put together book, with lots of graphic organizers to clearly illustrate the ten traits. It concisely lists and explains the traits that make administrators and teachers effective. This book provides tools for teachers, administrators, and mentors to help others and themselves become more effective.
Principals and administrators will find ideas to help them improve instruction, become more able mentors, and motivate effective teachers. Teachers will find information and inspiration to define personal definitions of effective teaching. The book will give every teacher a renewed sense of mission and vision of what teaching can be.
McEwan's book divides the traits into three categories: personal traits, teaching traits, and knowledge traits. She introduces you to each trait through real-life examples, personal vignettes, and reflections of students, parents and educators. She provides many lists, questions, and exercises to empower teachers and nurture the ten traits.

title: Pretty great, but sometimes not tough enough
text:
I’ve been using this product for a few months now and overall I’m pretty happy with it. The design is attractive and fits nicely into my kitchen aesthetic; it feels well-made at first glance and the finish has held up to daily use without any obvious wear. It’s easy to clean and the parts that come into contact with food don’t retain smells, which I really appreciate. Assembly was straightforward and the instructions were clear.

Performance-wise, it does what it’s supposed to for most everyday tasks. I use it several times a week and it handles routine jobs without fuss. The controls are intuitive and I like that there are a few settings so I can tweak things depending on what I’m making. It’s also relatively quiet compared with some older models I’ve owned, which is a nice bonus during early morning prep.

That said, there have been a few moments where I wished it were a bit more heavy-duty. When I put it through more demanding tasks, it strains and seems like it’s pushing its limits — not unsafe, but noticeably slower and less effective than I expected. For heavy users or those who frequently work with tougher ingredients, this might be something to consider. A sturdier motor or reinforced components would make it perfect.

Customer support was responsive when I had a minor question, which was reassuring. Given the price point, I think it’s a good buy for most households — reliable for day-to-day use, attractive, and easy to maintain — but if you need industrial-level toughness, you may need to look elsewhere. Overall, I’d recommend it for average home use.
