text:
[[VIDEOID:7ae84ae66b1c39445d7e5289bdae27ae]] I live in a 2nd story apartment and installed a Swann 2.4GHz wireless that I picked up from the local hardware store about a year ago. I installed it after scaring off some would-be car thief's. I decided to replace it because one of my receivers went out and I replaced it with the standard Astak 2.4GHz wireless receiver. I was impressed with the receiver (w/remote) and so I thought I'd give these cameras a try (the Swann was very choppy and I had to mess with the brightness controls in the software I use, a lot). I use the second receiver to hook to the TV in my living room. The cameras and receiver are in the same location as when I was using the Swann.

These cameras are way better than the Swann. The video that comes with this review was taken from my PC (I wire it through a Roxio RCA to USB connector) and use a freeware program to capture it (Debut). There are three walls between my computer and the cameras.

Others post about bad reception because of wireless routers. I don't use one, but there are several that appear in my wireless network list on my Windows PC. To be fair, they could have changed their routers after I installed the Swann a year ago.

Downside: The audio is choppy and has static. I don't use the audio; I didn't use the audio with the Swann, either. This is the reason for my "low" marks. Also, in the manual I discovered that in low light the cameras will switch to black and white. However, as you can see from the video, the b/w hasn't switched on. There is a big flood light in my parking lot which may be the reason. Color 24/7. Judge for yourself.

Tip: you may need to adjust the antenna on the receiver to get the lowest amount of static. I've found that moving it about 20 degrees at a time lets you see the difference.

I love how Austin's stories all knit together within the same small town community! You don't have to have read the other books in the series to enjoy each one individually, but by reading them all you get a fuller picture and more background on each of the characters. This start to the Bonfire Boys is a perfect example, taking minor characters from her other Love on Main series and putting them front and center.

Wild horses was a lot of fun, with city-girl-goes-country vibes. I loved Theron's inner battle and his relationship with his mother hits an unexpectedly heart-wrenching crux near the end. I didn't expect such a real moment in a romance novel, so it was a delightful surprise.

Skye is a satisfyingly believable character, with childhood damage and a lot of self-esteem issues. The way Austin describes her approach to and opinion of her paintings is incredibly accurate and gives the story an authenticity that many romance novels lack. Skye also gets her own personal wins that are unrelated to the romance, making you root for her even more. This (in addition to the sense of tight-knit small town community and over-protective family members) helps set a relatable stage full of players the reader can identify with.

Age gap usually isn't my thing, but this one worked fine for me. Skye is far more mature than her age. I enjoyed the self-conscious girl meets worshipping boy and city-vs-country tropes more. Theron has just the right amount of alpha-hole attitude and the steam is top notch. Looking forward to more in this series!

title: Something of a Find
text:
I'm very happy with this cart, and two reasons stand out: its sturdiness and its size.

It's a very clever design, and the parts are of high quality. The result is a rigid structure that's perfect for applications like mine: support for a wide-carriage "pro" printer that can be placed on the top shelf without the somewhat massive printhead action causing side-to-side sway.

The size is a difficult one to find elsewhere. In my case I needed to replace a cheap TV cart made of low-density fiberboard and formica. I was using it to support not only the aforementoned wide printer on top but also a laser printer and scanner on the lower shelf. Any replacement would have to be almost the same size because of my office setup. I was ready to give up -- most shelving/carts like these are dimensioned in multiples of 12 inches -- but then I found this guy (the 16x28). Perfect! A little taller than the crumbling TV cart, but that's OK. I gained a third shelf for supplies that previously lived on the carpet under the cart.

One problem (for me): Carts like these have no sides onto which you can stick things -- in my case USB hubs. The solution was fairly simple: pegboard material cut to size, held in place with toggle bolts (with shortened screws).

One caution: unlike wood shelf units, which typically have uniform shelf width front to back, carts like these have tubing at the four corners that you might need to take into account. If your printer, for example, is a tight fit on one of the lower shelves, it might fit fine and work fine but not allow you to pull out the paper supply drawer if you can't skooch it over. The inner post-clearing distances for the shelves in this case is about 25.5 inches (left-to-right as pictured) and about 13.5 inches (front-to-back as pictured).

Someone else gave a review saying they couldn't get these bottles to spray. The bottles I received have a screw type nozzle. Tighten the screw and it will spray a fine mist. Loosen the screw nozzle and it will spray a heavy stream.

The bottles are semi-transparent and have graduations on the side in ounces, milliliters, and a neat feature in the middle called "dilution ratio". It makes sense when you see it.

All 3 of the bottles I got came with the red handle/nozzle/neck. So I used my label maker (also purchase from Amazon) to ensure I don't get the three chemicals mixed up.

In the past I've used cheap junky spray bottles that leak out the handle when you squeeze them. I have NOT had that problem at all with these.

I use these bottles to a variety of tasks around the house. One is filled with bleach for aggressive cleaning, such as the bathroom or to kill mold growing outside my house. One is filled with a home-made cleaning mixture of equal parts rubbing alcohol, vinegar, and distilled water (works great on glass!). And the last one is diluted hydrogen peroxide used to treat indoor and outdoor plants. Hydrogen peroxide will break down quickly when exposed to light, so make sure you store it in a dark/cool/dry place.

title: Great fragrance!  Horrible shampoo!
text:
I really wanted to love this shampoo because the scent is absolutely incredible. As soon as you open the bottle, it smells like a high-end luxury spa. It has these beautiful, sophisticated notes that linger in the air and make the actual process of washing your hair feel like a treat. If I were rating this based on fragrance alone, it would be a five-star product without question. Unfortunately, a shampoo needs to actually function as a cleanser and conditioner, and this one fails miserably in that department.

The first thing I noticed was the texture. It is far too thin, almost watery, which meant I had to use twice as much as usual just to get it to lather. Even then, the lather was weak and didn't feel like it was actually lifting any oil or buildup from my scalp. After rinsing, my hair felt strangely tacky, as if there was a film left behind that wouldn't wash away.

The real disaster happened once my hair dried. I have medium-textured hair that is usually manageable, but after using this, my strands felt like straw. It stripped every bit of moisture from my hair, leaving it frizzy, tangled, and completely lifeless. I spent twenty minutes trying to brush through the knots, and I genuinely feared I was going to cause breakage. It felt as though the chemicals used to create that amazing scent completely overwhelmed the moisturizing ingredients, or perhaps there weren't any moisturizing ingredients to begin with.

I tried using a deep conditioner afterward to save my hair, but the damage was already done. My scalp also felt itchy and tight for a few hours after the wash, which makes me suspect that the fragrance is too strong or the formula is too harsh for sensitive skin.

It is such a shame because I love the way it smells, and I almost considered using it as a body wash just to keep the scent around, but for the price point, I expect a hair product to actually improve the condition of my hair. I cannot recommend this to anyone who cares about the health of their locks. Save your money and buy a shampoo that prioritizes hair care over perfume. It is a lovely scent, but a horrible shampoo.

title: Great yarn
text:
I’ve been knitting for over fifteen years, and I’ve read a lot of pattern books, technique guides, and inspirational collections. When I saw “Great Yarn” is something else entirely. It’s not a pattern book, though it does have dozens already. Instead, it’s a deep, thoughtful exploration of the history, culture, and craft of yarn itself. The author has a gift for storytelling, which is fitting since “yarn” literally means a good tale. Each chapter weaves together the origins of different fibers from sheep farming in the Shetlands to small-batch indigo dyeing in Japan along with profiles of spinners, dyers, and designers I’d never heard of. I learned why some wool feels scratchy and others drape like silk, how yarn thickness is measured internationally, and even the surprising role of yarn-related superstitions from various traditions.

The writing is warm and personal, not dry or academic. It felt like sitting with a knowledgeable friend who just happens to be obsessed with fiber science. The photos are gorgeous, but not just pretty pictures they actually illustrate the text. I’ve already tried two new spinning techniques and a dye method using onion skins after reading about it here. My knitting group passed this around, and everyone came away with something different: one friend started researching local fleece suppliers; another finally understood why her merino pills.

If you love yarn, or if you love great writing about making things, this book belongs on your shelf. It made me appreciate every skein I own just a little more.

I have mixed feelings about "Another Triumph to Maureen." The writing is sharp and the pacing keeps you turning pages, but I’m not sure it fully delivers on its promise. The central character, Maureen, is wonderfully drawn—fierce, flawed, and utterly human. Her journey through her journey she goes on feels authentic, and there are moments of real emotional weight. The dialogue crackles, and the author clearly has a deep understanding of the small, quiet triumphs that define a life.

That said, I found some of the subplots underdeveloped. A few side characters appear promising but then fade into the background without resolution. The ending also felt a bit rushed, as if the author was trying to wrap things up too neatly after such quickly that the emotional payoff didn’t quite land. It’s a solid read, but not the knockout I was hoping for.

If you enjoy it for the strong central character and the vivid writing, but go in knowing that not every thread gets tied off neatly. If you like character-driven stories with a slightly imperfect finish, this will still be worth your time. Four stars from me—good, but not great.

title: The Irish Banana Review
text:
Ask the Passengers is exactly the type of book you think you're getting when you read the summary: It's a book about a teenage girl who is trying to sort out her life and figure out who she is and who she wants to be. And yes, it has the added twist of the main character coming to terms with her sexual orientation.

I was a little surprised at how ordinary Astrid felt. Not that I expected her to be some dramatic, overblown character, but I felt like there was nothing spectacular that set her apart from a lot of the other teenage girls I read about in contemporary novels. Her parents don't get her--her mom is more concerned with her sister and her dad is fairly oblivious. That just felt formulaic to me. Aside from the lesbian angle to the story, Astrid felt like any other girl dealing with feelings for that special someone, but unsure of how to express them.

This book is all about emotion. I expected that going in, and A.S. King really does a nice job of expressing those emotions. She phrases things splendidly, and I truly enjoy her writing style. The story flowed nicely. It wasn't overly long or excessively wordy, which could have been an easy pitfall to stumble into.

Overall, this book was exactly what I expected, but that's what disappointed me. I was hoping for something that would wow me. Something I could get really excited about and sink into. The setting is a small town where everyone knows everyone's business, but again, that just felt so done already. I feel like I've read variations of this novel before, but the way King wrote it kept me engaged to the end.

title: Should Be a Movie
text:
I picked up Should Be a Movie because the premise — a story so cinematic it feels like a screenplay waiting to happen — sounded irresistible, and for the most part the book delivers exactly that kind of experience. From the opening chapter I was immediately swept into lush, vividly described scenes that felt staged for a wide-screen adaptation: sweeping locations, sharp, witty dialogue, and a cast of characters who are equal parts charming and flawed.

The narrator’s voice is one of the book’s biggest strengths. There’s a self-aware, slightly sardonic tone that kept me smiling aloud on the subway and turning pages faster than I meant to. The protagonist is likable without being perfect; their internal monologue balances humor with genuine vulnerability, which made it easy to root for them even when their choices were messy. Secondary characters are well-drawn and memorable — a friend who steals every scene with deadpan one-liners, a love interest with complicated motives, and a rival who’s both infuriating and oddly relatable.

Pacing is generally strong. The middle section unspooled like a montage: set-ups, missteps, reconciliations, and a few surprises that kept me engaged. There are moments of quiet reflection that add emotional depth, and then the narrative will snap back into high-energy sequences that feel cinematic in the best way. The author’s knack for visual detail makes many scenes pop — I could see the city lights, hear the background music, and almost feel the weather on the characters’ skin.

That said, the book isn’t flawless. A couple of plot threads felt a bit underdeveloped, leaving me wanting more explanation about certain character motivations. And the ending, while satisfying, leans a little towards neatness; I would have enjoyed a touch more ambiguity or risk. A few sentences occasionally veered into purple prose, breaking the otherwise crisp rhythm, but those instances were infrequent.

Overall, Should Be a Movie is an entertaining, well-written read that will particularly delight anyone who loves contemporary fiction with strong dialogue and cinematic flair. It’s the kind of book you’ll want to recommend to friends and — yes — imagine being adapted for the screen. I’m giving it four stars because it’s consistently enjoyable and emotionally engaging, even if a little tightening in places would have made it exceptional.

title: Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and the three horsemen will do anything
text:
The final book of the Riders duology, and I’m happy with how it ended. Seeker by Veronica Rossi picks up where Riders left off. Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and Darryn and the remaining three horsemen will do anything to bring him back.

One thing that I don’t care for about this book is the romance. Not every story needs a love story, especially a story that’s so tightly focused on a group of friends. The romance didn’t add to the story and Darryn’s continuous pulling away from Gideon was exasperating by the middle of the book.

Cutting the romance out of the story, like Riders, it’s a very neat story with a unique point of view. The remaining horsemen are doing all they can to find Bass in The Rift. The Rift forces them to face their fears, and face their innermost demons.

Without giving much away, the journey to find Sebastian is one full of haunting memories and really learning more about the characters. I don’t feel like there was as much character development as their was in the previous book, but I don’t think that it’s really a bad thing with this book. I also wish that this book only had Darryn’s or only Gideon’s point of view, like the first book, and not bouncing between both.

I do wish there were more books in the series. Books from the other horsemen’s points of views would be interesting, and I’d definitely read them. All in all, a series that is enjoyable and provides a pretty unique premise for the characters.

Right out of the box the fit and finish impressed me — the paint job looks like real aged metal without the cold, heavy feel of steel, and the rivet details and reinforced brow give it an authentic look that draws compliments from other players.

Comfort was my biggest concern, and this helmet delivers. The interior padding is thick enough to keep the foam cheek and forehead pieces from rubbing raw after several hours of wear, yet breathable so I don’t get overheated during intense scenarios. The chin strap is sturdy and easy to adjust one-handed, which is handy when I’m suiting up quickly. The helmet sits securely even during running and shield bashing; I never felt it shift or loosen.

Durability appears excellent — I’ve had a few decent impacts from foam weapons and some accidental drops, and the helmet has only picked up a few scuffs that add character. No cracks or structural issues. Cleaning is simple: a quick wipe with a damp cloth removes dirt and sweat stains without affecting the finish.

Sizing was accurate based on the manufacturer’s chart; I double-checked my measurements and ordered the recommended size and it fits perfectly. Shipping was fast and packaging prevented any dings in transit.

Overall this helmet gives a great balance of authenticity, comfort, and durability for LARP use. It looks great in photos, feels secure during play, and stands up to rough handling. I’d recommend it to anyone wanting a convincing, functional helmet without the cost and weight of real metal armor.

title: Alternative history strategy with a dash of random dice rolling
text:
As others have mentioned, Dust is like a beefed-up version of Risk where you can drop Mechanized Armor Units from the sky and send strategic bombers on a grand tour of alternate history WWII. It's fun, it's easy, and it requires just enough imagination and skill to keep you interested for hours.

The game itself comes with 2 rule books and about a million game pieces. The good news is, these pieces are actually kind of fun and more often than not you'll find yourself organizing units together as your opponent figures out his next move. Dust also comes with two different rule books, one for Premium and one for Epic. This is just shorthand for "long game" and "longer game". Along with these items, players also use cards to determine what types of moves they'll make and what special abilities they'll be able to bring into play with each turn.

If I only had one complaint with the game it's that it doesn't really capitalize on its theme all that much. Sure you get a great map of the apocalyptic future-scape, a ton of pieces representing everything from submarines to Mechs, and a card system that provides some pretty great artwork, but overall the whole idea of this "alternative history" World War II is all in your head. You don't really follow any stories, so most games end up being a large-scale RISK that doesn't suck as much as its predecessor.

All in all, I recommend this game for nothing else than being fun and entertaining.

title: User-Friendly Design, But Tricky Connection
text:
The BEST feature here is the dedicated buttons for each function, as opposed to the “rocker” style most of these remotes have. Also, these buttons are silent (unlike some of the others which sound like clickers!)

Unfortunately, this unit has one thing to BEWARE of. While the Manual directions are very clear about how to pair the Movo with your phone or other device, you get NO INSTRUCTIONS WHATSOEVER regarding connection/regular usage! This is unfortunate since making a Bluetooth connection is QUITE TRICKY.

HERE IS HOW TO CONNECT THIS REMOTE TO USE IT (this assumes you have already paired it up with your phone as per the directions): 1. Don’t even bother to open Settings; 2. Simply hold down the red Power button—BUT KEEP HOLDING IT DOWN until it turns first RED, then it FLASHES GREEN, then it becomes SOLID GREEN, then finally turns RED again. 3. RELEASE the Power button just as the light turns RED again!

This is the ONLY WAY I have found that works every time, and it is fairly easy. FAIRLY easy! Practice it a couple of times if you are having trouble with the connection.

Also, be sure to TURN THE POWER OFF when you’re finished using the Movo by holding the Power button down awhile—until the light turns red and then goes out! This will save battery life.

Once you get the hang of using the Power button, I think you will find this remote is a good one.

I own 4 of these bottles of varying sizes. One of them is the BPA free version. I have never liked the rubber bite valve and have always taken them off right away. There is a rubber flap that covers the air intake hole that prevents water from getting out. The downside to this is it also prevents air from getting out when the bottle is just sitting. When there is cold water in the bottle and it sits at room temperature and warms up, the water expands and leaks out the main valve. A solution is to remove the little rubber flap that covers the air intake hole but this makes it more prone to spilling when the bottle tips over.

Two of the bottles (both older 0.5L) seem to have a small opening and very little water comes out no matter how hard I suck on it. There appears to be two moving rubber parts in the mouthpiece that get stuck easily and no amount of cleaning gets them to work properly.

One bottle (newer BPA free 1L) the mouthpiece turned orange for no particular reason. It doesn't affect the performance, it just makes it look dirty when it isn't. That same bottle the lever to flip up the valve broke off. I have never dropped the bottle, it just broke off from regular use.

This leaves only 1 bottle (older 0.75L) out of 4 that I haven't had any problems with.

I have written to the email on their website about warranty claims and have never even received a response from them.
(edit: I did eventually get 2 new caps after a couple emails and they seem to be working fine but the water flow still seems slower than the older cap I have that still works. It looks like they changed the design some and possibly reduced the opening.)

Overall I love the bottle that works and wish they would all work like they are suppose to.

I don't see the sense in complaining about the micro-USB end of the cable because it goes right into the charger base.  And the USB-A end would fit in any USB 2.0 or USB 3.0 port or wall adapter. I bought the Up as a gift for my teenage son who’s been getting into trail running and cycling, and it’s become one of those rare purchases that actually exceeds expectations. Right out of the box the unit felt solid and well-made. Setup was straightforward — the quick-start guide was clear, and pairing with my phone took two minutes. The app is intuitive and gives useful summaries without being cluttered.

The first thing that struck me was the accuracy of the activity tracking. Steps, distance, and elevation on hikes matched the readouts on his watch and my bike computer within a small margin. Sleep tracking has been surprisingly helpful: he used to complain about feeling tired all day, but after a few nights of reviewing the detailed sleep stages and suggestions, he changed his evening routine and now reports waking up more refreshed. Battery life is strong; we go several days between charges even with nightly sleep monitoring enabled.

For someone active, the Up’s fitness coaching features are a standout. The guided goals and gentle reminders helped him increase daily movement without feeling nagged. It also integrates nicely with other apps we use for running, so we didn’t have to manually transfer data. Durability has been impressive — it’s been knocked, splashed, and worn during muddy trail runs and still looks and functions like new.

A few relatively minor quibbles: the band could be a touch softer for all-day comfort, especially in hot weather, and the vibration alerts are on the light side (easy to miss during a loud workout). Also, the app’s social/competitions features are a bit basic compared to larger ecosystems, but that’s not a dealbreaker for us.

Overall, the Up hits the sweet spot for reliable tracking, helpful coaching, and good battery life in a rugged package. My son is using it daily and his activity levels have gone up noticeably. If you want a solid, no-fuss tracker that actually helps you move more and sleep better, this one is well worth the price.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I’ve read a lot of political books over the years, but this one genuinely stands out. It doesn’t just rehash tired talking points or rely on partisan slogans. Instead, it offers a clear, well-researched framework for understanding how power actually works behind the scenes. The author manages to be both deeply analytical and surprisingly accessible—yes, readable. I found myself underlining passages on nearly every page, not because the language was overly dramatic, but because each insight was so perfectly distilled.

What I appreciated most was the balance. The book doesn’t preach or tell you what to think; it gives you the tools to think more clearly about the forces shaping our political reality. The chapter on institutional inertia alone changed how I view gridlock. I’ve recommended it to friends on both sides of the aisle, and every single one of them came back saying the same thing: “I never thought of new way looking at things.”

If you’re tired of shallow punditry and want something that actually deepens your understanding without drowning you in jargon, this is it. I looked. It’s not light bedtime reading, but it’s rewarding in way few political books are. Five stars without hesitation.

title: Lacking in depth
text:
I really wanted to like this book. The premise was intriguing, and the early chapters had me hooked. But by the halfway point, I realized the author was just skimming the surface of what could have been a rich, complex story. The characters are sketched out with only the broadest of strokes—their motivations feel pasted on, their internal conflicts resolved with a single conversation. The world-building is similarly thin: we’re told about politics, history, and magic systems, but they never feel lived in or consequential.

What frustrates me most is the lack of depth in the central themes. The book gestures at weighty ideas—identity, power, sacrifice—but never digs into them. Every time it sets up a moral dilemma or a philosophical question, it either dodges it with a convenient plot twist or explains it away in a paragraph. I kept waiting for the narrative to slow down and wrestle with its own implications, but it just barrels forward on plot mechanics. The conflict feels manufactured; the stakes are high in theory but hollow in practice because we never truly understand why anyone believes what they do.

I’ve read other works by this author, and they handled nuance much better. This one reads like a rushed first draft that needed another round of revision to deepen the characters and the world. It’s not a terrible read—the prose is competent and the pacing keeps you turning pages—but I finished it feeling unsatisfied, as if I’d eaten a meal with no flavor. If you’re looking for something thought-provoking or emotionally resonant, look elsewhere. This is a shallow pool dressed up to look like an ocean.

title: Cute but not purposeful
text:
I bought this because the photos made it look charming and the size seemed perfect for a small corner by my sink. After using it for a few weeks I’m giving it three stars — it’s cute and well made in a decorative way, but it falls short as a genuinely useful kitchen item.

First the positives: the finish is attractive and matches the description. The paint/print hasn’t faded and there are no noticeable chips or defects out of the box. It feels reasonably sturdy for a decorative piece and the seams are neat. If your primary goal is to add a bit of personality to a windowsill, open shelf, or to complement a farmhouse/retro vibe, this will do that job fine. I also appreciate that it arrived carefully packaged; no scratches or scuffs.

Now the drawbacks that keep me from giving it more stars. The product is marketed as being functional for holding sponges/soap, but in practice it doesn’t drain well (if it’s designed to). Water collects in the bottom and even after draining a sponge for a while it still leaves a damp puddle. That makes the sponge stay wet and feel slimy after a few days — I’ve had to empty and dry it regularly, which defeats the point of a “hands-free” holder. If you use it for soap, the soap can end up sitting in a little pool and becoming mushy faster than I expected.

The size description was slightly misleading: it’s smaller than I pictured. It fits one compact sponge or a small bar of soap, but not much else. If you hoped to store multiple items (brush + sponge + scrubber), you’ll be disappointed. Also, there’s no non-slip base, so it slides on my counter when I grab the sponge unless I keep it on a textured tray.

In summary: attractive and decent quality for decoration, but not very practical for continuous everyday use unless you don’t mind occasional maintenance (emptying and drying). I’m keeping it because it brightens up the area, but if you need something primarily functional to keep sponges dry and neat, look for a holder specifically designed with drainage and non-slip features. This one is more about style than substance.

title: Not for everyone, but provides unique principles to filter through the "noise"
text:
In today's work ecosystem of forced multitasking, being "busy" all the time, and never feeling comfortable saying "no", Essentialism provides unique principles for sorting through the noise and figuring out what is truly "essential". The author himself says brilliantly that "essentialism is not one more thing -- it's a whole new way of doing everything". The key principles that I have uncovered from this book are the following:
(1) Work effectively, not efficiently (the latter does not imply that you are working on THE most important things)
(2) Learn to say no to things (personal, work, etc) and take greater control of your life
(3) Actively funnel to-do's, requests, etc through an internal "essential" test to decide whether something is truely important and should be done at all

One caveat, similar to many books in this genre. If you are a low-ranking associate at your job, you will find it difficult to implement a fair number of these strategies Day 1 (e.g. "how the hell am I supposed to do this while working at a [law firm / bank / advertising agency / etc]). That being said, the principles are still worth reading and keeping with you, because as you grow more senior in your role (even if you're just managing one person initially), they will become incrementally more valuable

Application is easy; the formula is forgiving, so even on days when I’m rushing practice, it doesn’t smear or streak easily. It holds up reasonably well through a couple hours of rehearsal, sweat, and movement, though I do touch up before any longer sessions or performances. The scent is mild and not overpowering, which I appreciate.

When they are trying to talk her into staying safe, they say things like "don't be such a Nancy Drew" or "you're running off like Dora the Explorer".

title: I love this book!
text:
I really enjoyed reading this book! Mona, the main character, is easy to relate to...and she has red hair! Being a ginger myself, I have a special affinity toward ginger characters (we're under represented)! My bias aside though, Holden's writing style really brings the characters to life. They are realistic...their lives aren't spectacular, they don't have these amazing careers or live in a mansion. They are normal people, living in an average house, complete with a crotchedy old neighbor! I love it. It was so easy to relate to their lives and picture them as my own neighbors or somebody I would be friends with. I was really touched by Mona's rediscovery of herself and her husband. There is a lot of laughter in Becoming Mona Lisa too...Mona and her husband have witty, cynical, comical personalities and I found myself laughing quite a bit. I also found myself feeling all gushy over the rekindling romance between husband and wife.

Holden does such an amazing job of describing the surroundings that I feel I could draw a picture of the Siggs home! I can picture the mean old codger that lives across the street, the bird infestation, the mannequins, even the Walmart that Mona works at. Throughout reading this book, I was reminded of the reasons I love my fiance and what brought us together. I don't know if Holden intended this...but it definitely reminded me not to take him or our relationship for granted. The book flows really well and I definitely found myself wanting to read more after I finished. So I'm really hoping there's a sequel to Becoming Mona Lisa, because I really wanna follow the next chapter in Mona's life...and I REALLY wanna know what's up with the room! I definitely strongly recommend this book.

title: A Very Good Electric Shaver for Sensitive Skin
text:
As someone with very sensitive skin, I have always had problems with razor burn after shaving. Dry electric shavers tend to butcher my skin. Traditional multi-blade razors (like the Mach 3) are easier on my skin, but as sensitive as my skin is, cuts are not uncommon. A few months ago I received a Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a gift and gave it a try. Thanks to the shaving gel that can be applied to the skin at the touch of a button while shaving, it provides a very close shave that doesn't cut my skin like a traditional razor, and there's very little skin irritation afterwards. As for closeness, I'd say that it's almost as good as a Mach 3 razor.

One aspect about this shaver that I like is that it operates from a rechargeable battery so that there's no electric cord to get in the way while shaving. Also, the shaving gel packets are easy to replace, it comes with a charger stand, it's easy to clean the rotating blades and it takes up little bathroom counter space. Further, it takes less time to shave and clean-up afterwards than with a traditional razor & shaving cream.

Overall, I regard the Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a very good shaver and rate it with 5 out of 5 stars. Granted, it is somewhat expensive, but if you have very sensitive skin like me, you might be as pleasantly surprised as I was with its performance.

title: Nice Cabinet and Board, BAD Darts
text:
I really wanted to love this set because, at first glance, it looks like a great value for the money. The cabinet is actually quite sturdy and looks professional once it is mounted on the wall. It does a good job of protecting the board and keeping the room organized. The dartboard itself is also decent; the sisal is tight, the numbers are clear, and it feels like it will hold up to a lot of play over the next few years.

However, the darts included with the set are a complete disappointment. I understand that this is a budget-friendly bundle, but these darts are almost unusable. The tips are inconsistent, and the flights are made of a cheap plastic that curls or tears after just a few throws. More importantly, the balance is completely off. I found myself struggling to hit basic targets, not because of my skill, but because the darts wobble mid-air. They feel lightweight and cheap, almost like toys you would find in a carnival game rather than actual sporting equipment.

If you are buying this for a game room or a garage, be prepared to spend an extra twenty or thirty dollars immediately to buy a proper set of brass or tungsten darts. I ended up using an old set I had in the attic, and the difference in performance was night and day.

In short, the hardware is great, but the accessories are garbage. I am giving this three stars because the cabinet and board are high quality enough to justify the price, but the inclusion of such poor-quality darts is a major letdown. It is a good foundation for a home setup, but do not rely on the darts that come in the box. Buy the set for the board, and buy your darts elsewhere.

title: The plight of the Third World
text:
Accomplished master of the police procedural Henning Mankell strays from this genre in his latest novel, "Kennedy's Brain". In his novel, Mankell in the guise of a mystery, has penned what is in reality a social commentary. Mankell who resides at least partially in Mozambique, takes aim at the plight of the African underprivileged particularly relating to the AIDS epidemic and it's exploitation by the pharmaceutical companies.

Swedish archaeologist Louise Cantor whose specialty is ancient Greek artifracts is leading an expedition in Greece sponsored by Uppsala university. She happily anticipates taking a break to return to Stockholm and visit her son Henrik. Much to her shock and dismay she arrives at his flat, unable to raise him on the phone, to find him lying dead in bed. She is stunned to learn that an autopsy confirms that he overdosed on barbiturates.

Unable to believe that Henrik would take his own life she commences her own investigation. She travels across the world to a remote area of Australia to recruit her estranged husband Aron and inform him of their son's death. Together they go through his papers that direct them to an apartment their son kept in Barcelona. Hacking into his computer they discover that he was HIV positive and that he had business that took him to Mozambique.

Louise Cantor proceeds to Africa after the mysterious disappearance of her ex husband. While there she is confronted by danger and the horrors of a village designed to care for AIDS victims where Henrik had worked. She discovers that there is quite a bit more going on there than administering to the sick.

Mankell paints a graphic picture of the misery endured by the suffering in Africa while being critical of those who opportunistically use them for financial gain. The plot of "Kennedy's Brain", metaphor for an inexplicable and secretive mystery is very much similar to Le Carre's "The Constant Gardener".

I bought this sling hoping it would be an affordable, authentic-feeling replacement for the tired, cracked leather piece on my Mosin Nagant 91/30, and it exceeded my expectations. The sling holds the rifle securely when slung and doesn’t slip under load. The leather softened a bit with rubbing-in and now conforms to my body nicely.

Functionally it performs exactly as advertised — a dependable field sling that feels period-appropriate. Aesthetically it complements the rifle well; the color and finish match the vintage look of my Mosin. After a couple of range sessions and a few walks in the woods, there’s only mild, attractive patina developing.

If I have one nitpick it’s that the edge finish could be slightly smoother, but that’s purely cosmetic and hasn’t affected performance. Overall I’m very pleased — great value for the price and a perfect fit for the 91/30. If you’re looking for a solid replacement sling that’s ready to use out of the box, this one is a great choice. Five stars.

title: Straightforward in an unspectacular way
text:
Since Mark Waid introduced a group of lab assistants to work under Bruce Banner, I’ve harped on the fact that they’ve had very little in the way of character development. The Indestructible Hulk #16 finally addresses that issue by delving into the past of Mr. Jessup, largely because, as this issue informs us, he’s going to die within a week. Spending a full issue to build up a character just so readers will feel some sort of impact when he dies seems a little cheap to me, but I still think this marks progress, as one of the things this book has been lacking is a good supporting cast.

The art here is done by Mahmud Asrar, who does a pretty good job. Nothing here really blows me away, but it’s a welcome change to have an entire issue follow one art style after the last arc cycled through multiple artists on a page-by-page basis.

As a whole, this issue does what it needs to do in a straightforward if unspectacular way. We finally get some background on some of Banner’s supporting cast, we get the suspense of knowing that said character is going to die, and we get some Hulk smashing action. This is an above-average issue that will hopefully lead into bigger things to come when the story gets rolling.

title: Fantastic new read!
text:
Katherine Center does it again! What You Wish For is a book I closely relate to. Sam is an elementary school librarian in Galveston who's amazing school is radically changed when their beloved principal dies and is replaced by Duncan, a no nonsense man who believes the school is shoddy in its security. Sam used to know Duncan, back when he was a fun-loving teacher, but can't understand why he's so different. Katherine Center always knows how to reach the right tone- the story is at turns sweet, eye-opening, soulful, tragic, and hopeful. She also gets the school politics exactly right- teachers know that a principal can make or break staff and student morale. It is refreshing to read a book that gets this right!

One recommendation- read Happiness for Beginners by Center first (or reread it if it's been awhile). This novel is completely a standalone book. Trust me, however- read it, not only because it's a fantastic book, but because it will add greatly to your enjoyment of What You Wish For.

title: Superb SSD! Awesome performance.
text:
The last time I built a PC was back in 2014, so I'm not up-to-date on todays tech. I did some research and came across these newer M.2 SSD's. I'm not new to SSD's. My last PC actually has a Samsung 840 PRO. Those were lightning fast in their day and still are.

When it comes to daily tasks for me, it's mostly web browsing and streaming with light gaming mixed in a few times a week. I play Overwatch, CS:GO, Path of Exile, Rust, Diablo 3: RoS, GTA V, and a few others. Load times are definitely quicker with an SSD compared to a traditional HDD. From pushing the power button to desktop takes about ~11 seconds.

I don't do heavy data transfers, so I don't reach the true potential of this drive, but I wanted to invest in the longevity and dependability with Samsung. Just be careful when looking at M.2 SSD's. NVMe's aren't compatible with certain (older) motherboards. I made that mistake when I went to buy another 970 EVO for my laptop (HP Pavilion 15). The laptop was only compatible with M.2 SATA SSD's and not NVMe's.

text:
Sabaal is a captive Jakkattu imprisoned on Earth by the Mezna priests who experiment on her. Javan 6ix is a tek - half Miscegenate, half machine - beginning to question his life in the city. Norwood Thorne is too smart for a human, too inquisitive for a man, leading his sister Julip down the path of questioning the Temple, the Mezna and all the history they've learnt on the Rez.

Sabaal's escape is the part of the catalyst that throws them all together, leading them to question whether everything the Mezna has been telling them is true. Because beyond their fences, the Feral - the Undone as they name themselves - have information that will turn their understanding of the world upside down.

The Jakkattu Vector is action-packed, with Tyler propelling you from one scene to another, giving you glimpses of the truth, glimmers of the lies these human-Mezna hybrids have grown up with, expecting you to piece them all together before the horrifying reveal. In between, she engages your emotions with the innocence of the young Thornes as they grow up, navigating the thin line between independence and insolence in their quest for truth. And then she feeds you heartbreak on a platter.

The Jakkattu Vector is gritty and grim yet inexplicably hopeful as each of strand of humanity - human, Miscegenate, Undone - come to terms with who they are and what the Mezna has done to them.

Note: I received an ARC from Novel Publicity in exchange for an honest review as part of a blog tour.

title: Good noise suppression and durability for a fantastic price
text:
I bought these after looking through various first- and third-party solutions for low-noise Mavic Pro props. I'm using them on an original Mavic Pro (not a Platinum) and I absolutely love them for 3 reasons:

1, they make a big difference in terms of the Mavic's sound output. I haven't done formal tests with a decibel meter, but it's obvious that the flights are significantly quieter with these props both indoors and out. I now tend to have some trouble hearing my Mavic once it's up to about 150-200ft even when directly overhead (though obviously quick altitude changes or movements change that). It's made it much less obtrusive than the original props. I haven't tried other brands and therefore can't compare to other manufacturers' low-noise props, but you'll definitely notice a big improvement over the stock blades.

2, their durability seems just as good as the original props'. I read several reviews of other low-noise props that complained that the gold tips were made of a softer, more easily deformed plastic. That isn't the case with these, as it's the same material along the entire length. That may make a slight difference when it comes to aerodynamics, but it means I don't have to worry about them when folding up the props (by the way, they fold up just fine despite their slightly larger size, as long as you're a little careful when unfolding the back legs and don't get the pairs intertwined). The paint scuffs relatively easily, but that's it. I've replaced one set after stupidly crashing into some scrubby branches, but even then there were only a few minor nicks and gouges that I probably could have gotten away still flying with, but at this price it's stupid not to just get another set.

3, obviously the price is amazing. These are half the price of all other manufacturers' props that I could find, and at $8 for a complete set it's really hard to argue with when you get such significant noise reduction. I can't imagine going back to anything else. I'd buy 2 sets just to have some spares.

text:
I first purchased this brush back in 2013. After just a few shaves the brush separated from the handle and I started a return. I wanted a replacement, but it was out of stock so Simply Beautiful sent me a refund instead, without requiring me to return the defective brush. I decided to attempt a repair of the brush. After gluing it back together with marine epoxy the brush is still working fine but showing it's age through normal wear. Now five years later (2018) I decided to purchase a backup to have on hand for when the old brush becomes worn out. So I ordered a second brush thinking by now the manufacturer had probably worked out the issue. Unfortunately, again after just a few uses the new brush also separated from the handle. This time the seller, Simply Beautiful, sent me a replacement. The replacement seems to be performing fine after a few weeks of usage. So far, so good.

In summary, I like the brush. It suits my needs. But I am disappointed in the manufacturing of the product.
If you order one of these be prepared for this issue. And maybe have some Marine Epoxy on hand.

As a side note, it is not unusual for some brushes to have a "wet dog" odor when new. This can be remedied by repeatedly soaking the brush in soapy water overnight. Through normal usage the odor will eventually go away.

I bought this for my 12-year-old niece to have something fun to do when she comes over, and it has been a total hit. From the moment she opened the box she was completely absorbed — the pieces are colorful and well-made, not flimsy at all, which was a relief. The instructions were clear and easy to follow, so we were able to start right away without any frustration. It’s the kind of toy that sparks creativity and keeps kids engaged for longer than a typical five-minute toy.

What I really appreciate is how it encourages problem-solving and patience. My niece loved figuring out how the different parts fit together, and she felt proud when she finished each section. It’s challenging enough to be interesting but not so complicated that she got discouraged. I also liked that there’s room for variation so she could customize a few things and make it her own. The finished result looked impressive for a kid project, which boosted her confidence and made her want to show it off to family members.

Durability seems excellent so far. After several play sessions and being packed away in a tote, the pieces still look new and haven’t warped or lost color. Cleanup is simple — everything fits back into the original box without losing small bits, which is a major plus for me as the adult responsible for storage.

This toy has become a go-to activity during visits, providing quality, screen-free entertainment that both of us enjoy. It’s also reasonably priced for the amount of play value it delivers. I’d recommend this to anyone looking for a thoughtful gift for a preteen who likes hands-on activities. It’s fun, educational, and sturdy — exactly what I hoped for.

title: This is a excellent read for new leaders.
text:
This is a story about Debbie Brewster. She is the new head of corporate client services.

Debbie's current situation is her team scores are the lowest in the company and she has to figure out how to improve them.

Debbie begins by trying to assess her situation on her own but then realizes she needs help.

Debbie discovers the companies mentorship program and signs up for it.
She gets Jeff as her mentor. Jeff is the companies president. They spend several weeks together. Jeff gives Debbie his secrets to becoming a successful leader. He teaches Debbie the SERVE model. He asks Debbie several direction questions about her self and team. Debbie's homework assignment is to answer those questions and bring the answers with her at their next meeting.

Serve stands for:
1)See the future - where are you going with your team

2)Engage others and develop them - Assign the right people to the right jobs and help them to smooth out their rough edges.

3)Reinvent Continuously - Continue to learn

4)Value Results and Relationships - Get results from those in the right position by being relationships.

5)Embody Values - Walk the talk. Be a role model for what you believe in and your team will follow.

As Debbie learns, understands and implements Jeff's teaching she begins to see excellent results.

This book is a quick but powerful read. I highly recommend to new leaders.

title: Original fantasy with strong world building and characters
text:
Full disclosure: I won this in a Goodreads giveaway.

It's very, very rare to come across a truly original entry in the epic fantasy world, these days. Though in some ways I'm not even sure fantasy describes this book. Yes, it's obviously fantasy with magic and different races and such things, but at the same time it doesn't seem to focus on those things. It doesn't have the 'feel' of a typical fantasy book, and to me that's a good thing. Perhaps because it lacks some of the heaviness that many serious fantasy novels have. I did find that to be a good thing, though. It let the story move fairly quickly without getting bogged down on small details.

The world itself is very well laid out, especially because the reader is discovering it as the main character does. Rather clever of the author, there. Didn't even occur to me as I was reading, but in retrospect it worked and was very entertaining.

Characters...complex, interesting, well-rounded. I could go on, but you get the idea. At no point did I get the feeling I was dealing with cut outs or your typical fantasy cliches. Though I'll admit I'm a sucker for an anti-hero, which the main character definitely is. The relationships throughout the story are just as interesting, and nothing is ever quite as it seems.

I found the story itself to be very compelling and very original. It was one of those books that I couldn't wait to pick up when I had to set it down to go do something else. Halfway through I found myself lamenting the fact that there aren't any other books in the series written yet. I'm not going to talk much about it because there really is a lot to give away. I, for one, did not see the twists coming.

I really look forward to the next book in the series and finding out more about these characters, as well as the world they live in. Unlike so many books, these days, there's a very satisfying ending to this tale. Yes, it's apparently part of a larger story arc, but the author has not neglected the necessary resolution in each smaller part.

title: Yuck.
text:
I was skeptical when I first opened the package. The name says it all, and the smell that hit me when I dropped the first tablet into my Nalgene bottle confirmed it. Yuck is not a product you buy because you enjoy it. You buy it because it works.

I spent ten days backpacking in the Sierra Nevada this fall, and every water source I came across was treated with these tablets. The taste is genuinely unpleasant, like a chemical off-flavor mixed with something metallic and bitter. But here is the truth: I did not get sick. Not once. I crossed streams that looked clear but had livestock grazing upstream, and I filled up from a murky alpine lake on day four. My hiking partner, who used a different brand, spent one night vomiting after that same lake. I was fine.

The instructions are simple: one tablet per liter, wait thirty minutes. I found that letting the water sit for a full hour in cold conditions made a difference. The flavor is stronger if you chug it straight, so I started adding a single electrolyte packet to mask the taste. That helped a lot. Also, if you are using a collapsible bladder, be careful because the chemical can leach into the plastic and linger. I switched to a hard-sided bottle after the first two days.

Is it pleasant? Absolutely not. But when you are miles from the trailhead and your only other option is untreated water, Yuck is your best friend. I will keep a supply in every pack I own. If you prioritize safety over flavor, this is the product to get.

title: Sarah has a beautiful way with words
text:
The 411 by Maria:
I received this book right before Mother's Day. It is absolutely incredible. It is one perfect, powerful poem. A poem made into a book for mother's to give daughters and friends to give each other.

Having a daughter for me, was on my bucket list. I knew I didn't have much say in the matter and prayed for Goddess as hard as I could without going overboard afraid that if I begged too hard, God would feel it was unfair and unwarranted.

What Sarah Kay does is takes everything I have ever felt or thought about my daughter and put it into words. Every girl should have a copy of this book. They should read it and re-read it because Sarah speaks the truth. Life will hit you in the face and wait for you to get back up so it can kick you in the stomach. This is a healthy dose of reality but written in a poetic, joyful way, truly beautiful way.

Apologize when you've done something wrong. .
But don't you ever apologize for the way your eyes refuse
to stop shining; your voice is small,
But don't you ever stop singing.

That lines brings tears to my eyes. It is everything I would have wanted someone to say to me as a child and it exactly how I want my Goddess to grow up. Never ever stop singing.

After you read the book for the 10th time, go back and watch Sarah Kay read it. She really is very special and I want to thank her for writing everything I would want to say if I knew how.

text:

The plastic used for the dispenser is incredibly brittle. I barely applied any pressure to the pump during my second morning of use, and the entire neck of the bottle snapped right off. It didn't just crack; it shattered into small shards of plastic. I ended up spilling nearly a third of the product all over my bathroom counter, which was frustrating and wasteful. 

Now I am stuck with a bottle that I have to manually unscrew and pour out, which defeats the purpose of buying a pump-action dispenser for hygiene and portion control. It feels like the manufacturer cut corners on the materials to save money, and it completely ruins the user experience. I cannot recommend this to anyone who values durability. It is a shame because the actual cream works well, but I cannot justify spending this much money on something that breaks within the first few days. title: Great for documents.  Horrible for photos. Get it on sale and it's a steal!
text:
If I could do it, it would be 3.5 stars. Here is the skinny:

Pros:

Scanning and printing of normal documents is great.

You can scan to a network folder, your computer, to FTP, to a USB stick, or email as an attachment right from the printer. It's more than reasonable for first page out and multiple pages.

Easy setup. Printing from your phone is easy. Internet printing capability (print from anywhere, ready when you get home).

Toner is like all color laser printers, relatively expensive for the brand name but much cheaper than inkjet in the end.

Have been successful faxing using a OBI200 and a Google Voice number so very handy when you need to occasionally fax but don't have a physical land-line in the house.

While it isn't silent, it is not unreasonably loud. My old Canon inject makes more racket (clicks, clacks, bangs) when it starts up.

I have never had wake from stand-by issues. Wakes from sleep pretty fast.

Cons:

It is big (small con). But all color lasers tend to be in this size and up as they need to be able to hold and align all those cartridges. As a matter of fact, due to the pull-out tray design and smaller physical cartridges this is probably on the smaller side of color laser printers.

Flatbed color scanning from your computer of things like photographs, is IMHO HORRIBLE, with out of whack colors and edge diffractions and all sorts of oddities. It's to the point that I wonder if it's defective. Oddly, scanning of documents seems pretty good. I need to do some experimentation to see if it's a software driver issue or something but I've scanned direct into Photoshop, Picassa, and Acrobat and they all are pretty sub-par. The computer driver scanning controls are now very basic, not like they used to be years ago with much more control...maybe that's part of the problem.

Also, when _printing_ photographic type images the colors are massively over-saturated...okay for presentation graphs, charts, and stuff but again waaaayy off base for anything else. While I understand this is a business oriented machine, even businesses scan/print photographs and it shouldn't be this far off (a lack of functionality/settings in the printer driver could be partly to blame).

If there’s one small quibble, the glue pages are best used with a regular glue stick rather than the included paste to avoid mess, but that’s a minor issue and expected with kids’ activity books. title: Great Little Toy for Older Children and Adults
text:
I have been a fan of toy steam engines since I received a German made WILESCO engine for Christmas in 1961! This little engine by SunnyTech, a Chinese company, is very well made, with all brass parts, except for an O-ring to seal the boiler. When I first fired the engine up it ran like who-shot-john! I was rather amazed. This will make a great gift for any budding engineers that you may know, or any professional engineers, for that matter.
There are some pitfalls that the buyer should be aware of:
There are no instructions, at least in the one I bought has no instructions, just an exploded drawing showing how it should be put together. It is a good thing that I had experience with toy steam engines.
NEVER fill the boiler more than 2/3 full.
When running, it will spray some water, this is normal for a steam engine.
It does vibrate when running, place it on a stable surface.
The engine gets HOT when running. Take appropriate precautions.
Use alcohol as a fuel. Ethel or methyl alcohol (+95%) will work best. I tried 91% Isopropyl alcohol and it works fine, although it covered the boiler with soot. So you might want to avoid that.
NEVER use any petroleum derived fuel such as gasoline or Coleman fuel.
The engine is designed to only run for a few minutes on one boiler of water. Blow the lamp out immediately when the boiler is low on water or you may damage the engine with excess heat.
Remember, this is a toy but only for older children and adults.

I finally decided to try the Great Nutc the Great Nutcracker, and honestly, it lives up to the name. 

The first thing I noticed is the build quality. It’s made of heavy-duty cast metal with a solid, comfortable grip. No wobble, no flex—just a clean, decisive crack every time. I tested it on pecans, almonds, walnuts, and even a few stubborn hazelnuts. The hinge mechanism is smooth and the cracking chamber is well-designed; it holds the nut securely so you don’t have to chase pieces around the counter. Shells split cleanly, and the meat comes out in large, intact pieces far more often than with my old tools.

Cleaning is easy? The smooth surfaces wipe down quickly, and it doesn’t rust or discolor. I’ve had mine for three months of heavy holiday use and it still looks and works like new. The only minor note is that very small nuts like pistachios aren’t ideal—but that’s true of any standard cracker. For everything else, this is the best nutcracker I’ve owned. If you do a lot of baking or just enjoy fresh nuts, this is a worthwhile investment. Highly recommended.

text:
How many creative ways can one pose the vulgar? And we don't mean pose in the effete way, either. Perhaps this book will make you feel like Charles Manson playing the kazoo before an audience of irritable emperor penguins. Maybe.

It is hard not to take the printed "volume one" as anything but a threat, but it is a kindly one under the care of a good reader. Spitzer's short rocket-style blasts of the absurd, visceral, and tradition-baiting vulgarity makes for that kind of nostalgic reading many of us had as kids with the flashlight under the bed covers reading Mad Magazine. If you liked Spitzer's "Riding the Unit", you'll most definitely enjoy this more. In some ways, the irreal-ist quality of these shorts, wondrously masked by trademark obscenity, turns The Art of Fiction (1984) on its ear. Again, maybe.

There's simply not one bit of bathos in the whole lot, so hang on tight to your lawn furniture and have this book kicking around your cottage this summer.

I bought this pack of ink cartridges because the price looked good and I needed replacements for my home printer. I was hopeful, but after using the first cartridge it was clear something was wrong. I replaced the cartridge with a brand-new one from the pack and had the same experience: it lasted only a handful of pages before going dry.

Print quality started okay but degraded quickly, with faint, streaky text and uneven coverage. I tried cleaning the printheads and running the printer’s maintenance cycle, which helped only a little and didn’t change the fact that the cartridge capacity seemed far below what it should be. I double-checked that I had installed everything correctly and used the correct cartridges for my model.

I like the idea of a lower-cost alternative to OEM ink, but these cartridges felt like poor value since I had to buy more replacements so soon. text:
I read Jennifer Donnelly's first foray into adult fiction when it was still in hardcover & I enjoyed it so much I wrote the author to offer my encouragement.
It is what I like to call "a sweeping saga" that moves from 1880's London during the time of Jack the Ripper, to New York City. The heroine, Fiona is left as the sole support of her only remaining family, her little brother. The man she has loved is tricked into marrying another, so she immigrates to New York to find an uncle & start a new life. Along the way to becoming a successful entrepreneur, she has many obstacles to overcome and it makes for a very satisfying read.
There are a few minor historical inaccuracies that do not, in my opinion, detract from the book in any way. I would recommend the book to anyone who enjoys Barbara Taylor Bradford or Barbara Delinsky.

title: OK
text:
I bought this OK fitness tracker a few weeks ago after reading some mixed reviews and wanting something affordable to monitor steps and sleep. Overall I’m moderately satisfied — it does many things adequately but nothing outstanding.

Setup was straightforward and the companion app is simple to navigate, though a bit slow to sync at times. Step counting seems reasonably accurate for daily walks, but it occasionally misses short indoor steps or counts arm movements as steps when I’m doing dishes. Heart rate monitoring works well during steady-state cardio but lags during interval workouts and sometimes shows spikes that don’t match how I feel.

Battery life met the advertised claim; I got about five days between charges with regular use and notifications enabled. The band is comfortable enough for everyday wear and the display is readable in daylight, though a bit dim indoors at the lowest setting.

I appreciate the sleep-tracking feature, but the sleep stages feel approximate and sometimes label restless nights inaccurately. Customer support responded politely when I had a sync issue, but resolution took a few days.

If you want a budget-friendly tracker with basic features, this is fine. If you need highly accurate metrics for serious training, consider a step up.

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I was tired of sitting all day and decided to make the switch to a standing desk converter. This one seemed like a good middle ground—not too expensive, decent reviews, and a size that would fit my current desk. For the first week, I was all right, and now I'm not sure it was the best choice. Let me start with what I think so far.

Assembly was straightforward enough. The instructions were clear, and parts all came, but I needed a screwdriver that wasn't included, so keep that in mind. It took me about 45 minutes to get it together by myself. The unit itself the unit looks sturdy enough with its metal frame and a black laminate top. The gas spring for lifting the work surface works smoothly and you can stop at any height between sitting and standing. That part is great, and I do enjoy being able to stand for a couple of hours during the day.

Now for the "beware" part. The biggest issue is stability. When the desk is at standing height, there is noticeable wobble, especially if I type with any force. I have a dual monitor setup, and the monitors shake slightly when I'm typing quickly. I've tightened everything twice, but the wobble persists. It's not dangerous, but it's distracting. At sitting height, it's fine. I also the keyboard tray that attaches underneath is too close to my knees. My legs hit the tray if I sit cross-legged or even normally sometimes. I had to adjust my chair to a awkward sitting position. The tray itself is small and doesn't hold a full-sized keyboard and mouse comfortably. I use a tenkeyless keyboard, and it fits barely, but no room for a mousepad. I end up using the main surface for the mouse, which reduces the available workspace for papers.

Another thing: the desktop surface is about 36 inches wide, but the base takes up about 24 inches of that, so the usable space is actually less than a typical desk. My 27-inch monitors just barely fit side by side, and there's no room for a notebook or phone stand.

Overall, I've had this for three months now. It does what it's supposed to—lets me stand while working—but the wobble and limited space are frustrating. For the price, I think there are better options out there. I'll keep it for now, but I'm already looking for a replacement that is more stable and has a better keyboard tray. If you're on a heavy typer or need more than one large monitor, look elsewhere. Three stars. It works, but beware of the compromises.

title: Feels even better than it looks (and no problems in Linux)
text:
When another HTPC-style keyboard finally irritated me enough to replace it, I decided to try the diNovo Edge. In photos, the Edge looks attractive enough, but I always thought that the slimness made it look a little, well, flimsy. After actually getting it and trying it in person, (a) it looks even classier than the photos, and (b) it's got a nice heft and rigidity to it that gives it a feeling of quality I was not expecting. It really is a brushed aluminum piece there, not shiny plastic. Admittedly, it's expensive, but after trying it out I don't think it's disproportionately so.

About the trackpad ("TouchDisc"): I noticed some reviews commenting that it's nothing special. That's partially true; for the most part, it works just like normal laptop trackpad, which is good. The scrolling support has an interesting feature, though: on normal rectangular laptop trackpads, you place your finger at the right edge of the trackpad, and move it up and down to scroll. But you soon hit the top or bottom edge of the trackpad and have to stop. On the diNovo Edge you start the same way, by placing your finger at the right edge, but because it's round you instead move clockwise or counterclockwise to scroll, so you never have to stop. So once you start it scrolling you can just keep spinning your finger in circles around the outside edge over and over, pause, or change direction. The speed and accuracy of this approach are both big improvements, particularly when scrolling up and down long pages.

As for Linux support: no need for special drivers for the support of the main keys or the touchpad. In fact, many of the special media keys worked as expected out of the box, including the volume slider. Depending on what you're using to map keyboard shortcuts, though, not all of the media keys were available to be mapped without some tweaking. For these, a program called "keytouch" (probably available in most package managers) let me program the rest; it included settings for a different diNovo keyboard that seems to work fine for the Edge and includes most of those other keys already.

title: Riddle of the Book
text:
It might seem surprising, but professional bibliographers (and I am one) invariably judge a book first by its publisher. In the case of this book, it is published by Springer, a prestigious European information conglomerate. This is important because the author of this book has notably airy qualifications as a "reporter." Digital Publishing allows everyone to be an author and anyone to be a publisher, and if you can tweet you can be a "reporter." Thus, it is truly important for readers to have some sort of crap detector in place. Unfortunately, the publisher test failed on this book.

This book has virtually no redeeming substance; Wikipedia says it better -- and cheaper. The author's writing style relies on a snotty-know-it-all approach, that is particularly irritating because he has no credentials. (As an example, he even manages to insult little Corvallis, Oregon as "a jerkwater town," even though the place is a pleasantly progressive college town). Essentially, the book is about grinding axes with political correctness uber alles.

Technically, the Kindle version of the book has way too many formatting errors and unpleasant (and unnecessary) decorative images. Why ebook publishers -- and especially wealthy publishers like Springer -- can't seem to at least look at their digital product in Kindle Previewer is a bigger riddle than Kennewick Man.

My take-away from this book is that I will no longer give Springer-Verlag an automatic pass. It's easier to lose respect than to earn it, mein Herren.

Third night, I woke up on the floor. The center support beam had snapped clean in two. Not a cheap metal frame, this one is wood slats with a metal subframe, but the weld on the middle bracket failed. My mattress landed on the floor, the slats scattered everywhere. I'm lucky I wasn't hurt, but the frame is completely unusable. Tried contacting the seller—no response. Amazon return process was okay, but I have to repackage this broken heap and haul it to a drop-off. For the price, I expected at least a month. A week? Unacceptable. The wood slats are thin and flimsy, the screws stripped easily, and the whole thing feels like it was designed by someone who has never slept on a bed. Save your money and buy something with a solid steel frame or actual wood. This thing is dangerous. I will never buy from this brand again. Do not waste your time or risk your safety. One star is too generous.

title: Loved it!  Exciting, Danger, and Loads of Adventure.
text:
Katelin has found some peace and finds she looks forward to returning and spending the summer with her grandmother. Alone, without Simon, Katelin not only finds her own adventure but encounters a young man who sends flutters through her stomach. Through the journey, Katelin and her elfin friends discover how deeply her loyalty, fearlessness and determination runs. Together they must overcome the tyrant of the Elfin world and keep the Orb out of his grasp. The only question is, is Katelin strong enough or will she bite off more than she can handle?

What a fantastic fantasy! I enjoyed the first book but was blown away by the second. Sharon Dwyer set the "worlds" up very well, the characters were very well developed; Katelin was perfect! Dwyer captured Katelin’s "attitude" and emotional well-being accurately. Dwyer skillfully wrote the stories so that her readers do/will connect with Katelin in one way or another. The connection between the worlds was realistically done - meaning the characters had believable crossover and purpose. The first book was excellent!

The second book, I LOVED! I enjoy reading books where the female character is strong without knowing it. Piney, while not a cute character in real life, became adorable and perfect for Katelin. Dwyer expertly built up the suspense between the two books and the characters. I am intrigued on how Nana and the other worlds play out in Katelin's birthright ... I suspect a twist somewhere!

Dwyer’s The Fastasmagorical Forest series is exciting, inviting and mesmerizing. Once you get into the books, there is no stepping away. Lots of fun, plot twists, and adventure.

Very well done! While a book for young adults, those of us who enjoy fantasy, magic and adventure will love this book as well! I cannot wait for the series to continue!!!

title: Pleasantly surprised
text:
I’ll admit, I ordered these silicone food storage lids after a particularly frustrating evening of wrestling with plastic wrap that refused to cling, then gave up entirely and slid off a bowl of leftover soup. I didn’t have high hopes. The price was reasonable, the photos looked fine, but I figured I’d be back to using the original wrap within a week. I am genuinely pleased to say I was wrong.

The set came in a simple package, no frills. The silicone feels thicker than I expected, not flimsy at all. I have a mix of odd-sized bowls and containers—some square, some round, a few with slight rims—and I was skeptical that one lid popped on a rectangular casserole dish that I actually smiled. It sealed tight without any stretching or snapping. I gave it the shake test over the sink, and nothing leaked. That was the moment I started feeling pleasantly surprised.

I’ve been using them for about three weeks now. They work great on my stainless steel mixing bowls, on a ceramic pasta bowl that’s a bit wider at the top, and even on a plastic containers that never had matching lids. The seal is reliable for both fridge and pantry storage. I also tried one on a half-cut avocado, and it stayed fresh overnight with minimal browning. Microwaving? Yes, I tested a lid on a bowl of soup for two minutes, and it didn’t warp, no weird smell. They’re easy to clean by hand, and I’ve thrown a couple in the dishwasher without issue.

The only reason I’m giving four stars instead of five is that the smallest size is a little loose on my. It barely covers a ramekin, and I wish it were an inch larger to fit standard cereal bowls. Also, after several washes, one lid developed a faint white film that scrubbed off with a vinegar rinse, but it’s something to note. Still, for the money, I am genuinely surprised at how much these have reduced my reliance on single-use plastic wrap. I’m buying another set to keep at the office. If you’re skeptical like I was, give them a try. They might just win you over too.

title: Easy Vegetable Dishes for Even Your Picky Eater
text:
From the Book's description:

Everyone knows that vegetables are healthy and a necessary part of our daily diet. But not everyone knows just how delicious they can be. Sensational Vegetable Recipes shows you how to make great main meals from vegetables, as well as side dishes and delectable snacks. There's also a chapter on quick one-step ways to cook ten of the most popular vegetables. The clear step-by-step photographs guide you through each of the recipes, clearly explaining techniques that may be new to you. And there is practical advice on buying, storing and preparing vegetables, and ideas to let you take advantage of the great range of fresh and packaged produce available in markets today.

My Review:

I bought this book at my local Borders store in the bargain/clearance section years ago. What caught my attention was the bright colored vegetable dishes and the claim of step-by-step. Since then, I"ve made many of the recipes, including a family favorite "Savory Fennel Crumble", easy side dishes such as "Warm tomato and herb salad", "Asparagus and snow pea salad", Main dishes like "Vegetable lasagna", "Vegetable Pie" and so on. I've even tried the sections on the most popular vegetables, carrots, onions and so on.

The recipes truly are easy, step-by-step, for anyone, from the novice home cook to the tried and true professional chef. Falling somewhere in between, I found the recipes easy, delicious and crowd-pleasing. I've taken them to pot-luck dinners where everyone wants to know the recipe! They are made with common, every day ingredients, easily found in your hometown grocery store, the steps are not complicated. You may even win over your family's picky eater!

I would recommend this vegetable cookbook to anyone looking for something fresh for the family dinner. Even though it is no longer in print, there should be copies floating around the internet and used book stores. Easily five stars.
