title: It is like having a conversation with her
text:
Full disclosure: I have met Angelo Lowery at a writer’s retreat in Sedona Arizona. Angelo is in person, as she is portrayed in her memoir, “I am and the Spirit Walks with me,” a force to be reckoned with.
When I met Angelo, it was the first time in my life I met someone who has a direct line of communication to God. Her eyes are full of light, and she exudes a natural sense of strength and power. Reading her book, it was a surprise to me to hear all that she has endured in her life – abuse, betrayal, stunning loss. And yet, in her life, she has been able to rise above the pain to directly touch God. She has turned betrayal into blessing, loss into communion and pain into healing.
Angelo’s book is imperfect, as are many self-published books that do not have the benefit of a high-rolling publishing house behind them. But in its imperfection, it is perfectly Angelo. It is like having a conversation with her. She writes as she speaks, in a lovely, sometimes innocent, sometimes all-knowing, inspired and warm tone….until she speaks the words she hears from God. It was fascinating to read how distinctly different were the voices of her book – hers versus God’s.
Angelo is a warrior, she has survived countless horrors that would crumple the best of us. How did she do that? She shares that she always knew she was somehow chosen by God to do special work (Angelo is a gifted healer today). Was this the key to her resilience? For many who suffer adversity, their experience becomes an excuse to visit adversity on others. For Angelo, it became an opportunity to draw close to God and heal both herself and others.
I would love for Angelo to share next how we mere mortals, those of us who have not felt chosen, can also rise above adversity in our lives to become a conduit of good and love and spirit as she has done. Thank you for sharing your heroin’s journey, Angelo.

text:
The scale was relatively cheap so I was concerned about its precision and accuracy, so I weight 6 coins to see if the claims could be verified. The test showed the Standard Deviation of the measurements was less that one milligram per gram. As to the accuracy the standard provided was not much use as it was probably used to do the initial calibration of the scale, but it was useful in assessing the repeatability, which was very good. I got 100 grams each time I weighted it. To get an idea about the accuracy I used the coins, which when new have very consistent weights. The coin test showed about 0.25% deviation from what clean new coins should have weighed. As the coins were neither new or clean, in my opinion, this is very good for a scale of this price. As I am going to use the scale to titrate my medicines, the accuracy and repeatability are very important to me. These scales appear to be way within my criteria. The scale appears to be well made, but at this time I have no idea how reliable it is.

Now the bad news: parts of the protective shielding were not included in the package. The vendor promised to send me the missing parts but they have not arrived yet. I’ll update this review in two weeks or so with an assessment of the vendors performance. Update: they arrived!

I have found the scale is repeatable, but is does not respond to a small load change. Say 4 mg plus or minus. The work around is to put pressure on the scale for a second or so and it will adjust the reading correctly. This second delay is a little irritating but it probably deals with air currents and vibrations constantly changing the readings and the microprocessor spending time averaging the readings. I have been titrating one of my meds to 1.375 mg dose, which works out to 60 mg of the ground up tablets and I was able keep 37 doses all with in +/- 1.5%

text:
I have never before read a book where the author is so shamelessly self-promoting as Chris Brownfield. As another reviewer previously pointed out, his arrogance removes most (if not all) of his credibility, and makes this book very difficult to enjoy. For someone who was clearly not an outstanding JO (not by a long shot), he has way too much criticism and not enough respect for his fellow Navy submariners.

For a book titled "My Nuclear Family", Brownfield spends a lot of time talking about his IA in Iraq and his problems with the US government and the War on Terror. All organizations, particularly the US government has it's fair share of problems, however I hardly consider a sub JO an expert on politics or the intricacies of war. His claims that submarines are obsolete in today's Navy only further demonstrate his ignorance on the subjects.

I was led to read this book because I am quite familiar with the Navy's nuclear training pipeline and the job requirements of a submarine JO. As such, I was most interested in the first part of Brownfield's book which focuses on his time as a JO on the USS Hartford. It seems to me that Brownfield was a sub-standard officer at best, and is now a disgruntled ex-employee of the Navy who wanted to write a bitch-fest about how difficult his job had been while simultaneously making himself out to be the lone person deserving of respect in a profession he believes to be fallen.

I wouldn't recommend this book to anyone. The officers currently serving in our sub force are an important part of our national defense and are very deserving of our respect and gratitude, despite what Brownfield thinks.

I bought this laptop about two months ago after needing an affordable replacement for my aging machine, and I’m really impressed with the value it delivers. Right out of the box setup was straightforward — Windows walked me through updates and drivers installed without any extra hassle. The build feels solid for the price point; the chassis isn’t premium metal, but it’s sturdy with no flex and the hinge is tight and reliable.

Performance has been more than adequate for my day-to-day needs. I use it for web browsing with many tabs open, streaming, office work, video calls, and light photo editing. The processor handles multitasking smoothly and I haven’t experienced any slowdowns for these tasks. Battery life comfortably lasts me a workday with moderate use — typically around 6–7 hours — so I can take it on the go without needing frequent charging. Charging is reasonably quick as well.

The display is clear and bright enough for indoor use; colors are decent for casual photo editing and watching videos, though it’s not a professional-grade panel. Keyboard typing feels comfortable with good key travel, and the touchpad is responsive and accurate. Built-in speakers are fine for casual listening; I use headphones for better audio when watching movies.

There are a couple of small downsides: the webcam is average and low-light performance could be better, and the preinstalled bloatware required a quick cleanup. Otherwise, this laptop gives a lot of functionality for the money. If you need a reliable, budget-friendly laptop for everyday tasks, this is an excellent choice. I’d buy it again.

title: Opened my EYES!
text:
I have to admit, I picked up this book with a fair amount of skepticism. The title "Opened my EYES!" felt a bit dramatic, and I wasn't sure what to expect. But after reading it, I can honestly say it's the most accurate description possible. This book genuinely shifted the way I see things. It's not often that a single volume can change your entire perspective on something you thought you understood, but that's exactly what happened here.

The author presents complex ideas in a way that feels accessible and deeply personal. I found myself nodding along, then stopping to reread passages because they hit so close to home. What I appreciated most is that it doesn't just point out problems it offers practical ways to see them differently. The chapters are well-structured, each building on each other without becoming repetitive. There were moments when I actually felt a sense of relief realizing that the patterns I had been stuck in for years were not unique to me.

If you are someone who feels like you've been going through life on autopilot, or if you've ever wondered why certain situations keep repeating, this book is for you. It's not a quick fix, but it's a powerful starting point. I've already recommended it to three friends and plan to read it again to absorb the parts I might have missed. For anyone on the fence, just get it. It lives up to its title in the most honest way possible.

title: I recommend this book to any one who is interested in organizing their contacts!
text:
I bought this book because my contact list had become a disorganized mess—names without context, old numbers, duplicate entries across phone, email, and social media. I wasn’t expecting a miracle, just something practical. What I got was far better: clear, actionable guidance that I could apply immediately.

The author breaks the process into manageable steps: auditing current contacts, deciding what to keep, consolidating duplicates, and adding meaningful tags or notes so each entry is useful. I appreciated the balance between big-picture principles (like why maintaining relationships matters) and nitty-gritty tactics (how to export and merge lists, best practices for naming conventions, and templates for brief outreach messages). The examples felt realistic and not overly technical, which made them easy to follow even though I’m not tech-savvy.

I followed the recommended 90-minute audit and was able to streamline hundreds of entries into a clean, searchable list. The section on maintaining momentum—simple weekly habits to keep the list current—has been a game-changer. My follow-up outreach felt more personal because I had context at my fingertips.

If you want to stop wasting time hunting for contact details and start using your network more intentionally, this book is worth it. Practical, friendly, and full of useful templates and checklists—exactly what someone trying to get organized needs.

text:
I bought this device based on a lot of positive reviews and for the first three weeks, it performed exactly as advertised. The setup was intuitive, the build quality felt solid, and it integrated perfectly with my other home electronics. I was genuinely impressed with the performance and thought I had found a great deal.

It was incredibly frustrating to have a piece of tech fail so quickly, especially when it had been working flawlessly up until that point. I was convinced I had just bought a lemon and was prepared to leave a one-star review and demand a full refund.

That is where the experience changed. I reached out to their customer service team via email, and I was surprised by how quickly they responded. Unlike many electronics companies that make you jump through endless hoops or try to convince you that the failure is your fault, they were professional and efficient. They acknowledged the issue immediately and, without making me go through a lengthy return process for the broken unit, they shipped me a brand-new replacement via expedited shipping.

The new unit arrived within three days and is currently working perfectly. While I am still slightly concerned about the long-term reliability since the first one died so fast, the way the company handled the situation completely saved the experience for me. It is rare to find a company that actually stands behind its warranty and values the customer's time.

I am giving this four stars instead of five because a product shouldn't fail within thirty days, regardless of how good the support is. But because the replacement process was seamless and the product itself is great when it works, I would still recommend it to others. Just make sure to keep your receipt and contact their support if you run into any glitches.

text:
I rarely write reviews, but I had to for this one — Opened my EYES! completely changed how I look at my daily life and the choices I make. From the first chapter I felt like the author was speaking directly to me: clear, compassionate, and unafraid to challenge common assumptions. The blend of personal anecdotes and practical exercises made the ideas land in a way that was both emotionally resonant and immediately useful.

What surprised me most was how accessible the writing is. Complex concepts are explained in straightforward language, and the short reflection prompts at the end of each chapter helped me turn insight into action. I started small — just a five-minute breathing practice and a couple of the suggested journal questions — and already noticed a shift in my focus and patience. Several passages made me pause and reconsider long-held habits, and the “reality check” sections were gentle but incisive.

The pacing is excellent; the book moves quickly enough to stay engaging but contains enough depth to be worth revisiting. I also appreciated the resource list at the back — books, apps, and websites that expand on the topics covered. The author’s voice feels trustworthy and grounded, not preachy, which made it easy to accept the tougher suggestions.

After finishing it, I gifted copies to two friends because I genuinely thought they would benefit. If you’re open to looking at your life with a little more clarity and intention, this book is a must-read. Five stars.

title: Wonderful Book - Looking forward to a 2nd Ed.
text:
Fr. Emmanuel does an admirable job of commenting on various liturgical questions, and does not balk at some of the more contentious issues (cf. "The Gate and the Curtain" pp. 181-2; who knew that St. John Chrysostom mentioned the use of a Curtain?!), providing multiple perspectives. It is set up as a textbook including multiple layers of depth in commentary, from the more casual student of Liturgy, to the more scholarly.

A second edition would be most welcome, as there are a number of page cross-references which are incorrect, and at least one diagram is mentioned which does not appear in the text. Much recourse in footnotes is made to electronic sources, which may simply be the direction of modern scholarship, but does evoke a double-take when used in a field that stretches back millennia.

In all, a wonderful start, and a second edition to take care of minor housekeeping issues will be most enthusiastically received.

title: A fantastic thriller!
text:
THE VACATION by T.M. Logan primarily follows Kate, a wife and mother of two meeting up with her three best friends and their families at a stunning vineyard villa in France for a vacation to celebrate their 40th birthdays. It is meant to be a time to reconnect with each other and their families with good wine, good food and good company. Things aren’t starting off on an ideal note, however.

Kate has a feeling that something is going on with her husband and she manages to log into his phone to check his messages. She sees a back and forth conversation which seems to confirm that her husband is having an affair. Worst yet, the messages imply that the other woman is one of her best friends. As Kate seeks to identify the traitorous friend, it is clear that all of her friends have secrets to hide.

I have been in the mood for thrillers and this one did not disappoint. Once I got into the story, I could not put it down! We are primarily reading from Kate’s POV, hearing her suspicions, seeing her interactions with her friends and family. The author also gives us occasional chapters from the perspective of other characters, Kate’s friends, their husbands and the kids as well. It seems that almost everyone has something to hide and the author does a great job of dropping clues to redirect Kate’s suspicions and the readers’ as well.

This is very much a slow burn book for the first three-quarters or so. There is a lot of family drama and mystery going on which creates that slow build up to the last quarter where things really start to happen, ramping up the thriller elements. On top of the issues of what is going on with Kate’s wife, there are clearly secrets between the teens of their families and with the other women. The slow burn is done very well and it kept me entirely hooked throughout as the author takes the time to really delve into the different characters and potential suspects for everything that is going on.

title: Beautiful Photos - Good Healthy Recipes

Mediterranean food has a reputation for being not only delicious, but healthy. The diet is rich in fruits and vegetables as well as healthy oils and lean meats and fish. There are dozens, maybe hundreds of good Mediterranean cookbooks out there, and one that is excellent and includes a huge number of recipes for variety is 1000 Mediterranean Meals: Every Recipe You Need for the Healthiest Way to Eat by Valentina Harris. This cookbook has everything: appetizers, side dishes, soups, salads, mains with or without meat and even desserts. Although they are touted as healthier dishes, they are still mouthwatering, and no one will suspect that eating them will contribute to better health.

Almost all of the recipes include a photograph, which makes the book appealing. Most cooks want to know what the dish should look like. The recipes are written in the classic style with a list of ingredients and easy-to-follow instructions that cooks at all levels can successfully make them.

The variety of the dishes is vast, and there is something for every taste. Most of the recipes include several variations to that everyone can individualize them to their personal tastes. The recipes come from several of the twenty-one countries that border the Mediterranean Sea. Popular classics are included, such as Hummus and Tzatziki, as well as some unique dishes like Huevos Revueltos and Egyptian Sweet Couscous.

Anyone who likes Mediterranean food will love reading and cooking from this excellent cookbook. There will be dozens of recipes that appeal to almost every cook.

text:
2/20/22 update: Today I needed to replace two cartridges, so I used two that had been provided to me by the vendor after my initial 1-star review of this product in which I noted that the cartridges were not compatible with my HP printer. The replacement cartridges worked just fine, so I have updated my review to 5-stars. Kudos to the vendor for addressing my issue. Please read below for prior reviews and additional background.

2/8/22 update: Within a day of my leaving the 1-star review, below, the vendor contacted me offering a /replacement or a refund. They said that their cartridges had "gone through a upgrade just because of t/he firmware update". That statement was not totally clear to me, but I took it to mean that the printers had a firmware update and that they had upgraded these cartridges so that they'd be compatible. I appreciated the offer of replacement or refund since I was out of the return period, and decided to give them another chance. So....I took the replacement which arrived today (only 3 days after they initially contacted me). My printer is not currently in need of any cartridges, but when it is, I will try the replacements and update my review accordingly. In the meantime, I've upgraded my review from 1 start to 3, for their attempt to make it right. Can't give a higher rating until I confirm whether the cartridges work.

Original Review: Even though the product description listed my HP printer as one that these cartridges would work in, and even though they appeared to be a match and were easy to install in the printer, they were not compatible. The printer indicated it had detected a non-HP chip, and the cartridge was blocked. This prevented the printer from doing any printing/copying. Unfortunately, since I buy my cartridges in advance, so that I'm never caught without ink, by the time I discovered this issue, I was beyond the refund period, so I had to eat the $70+ cost (including tax). I was pretty surprised by this....these cartridges had good ratings, and I ALWAYS buy off-brand cartridges and I rarely have problems. Maybe I just got a bad batch, but figured I should post this review just in case it's becoming a trend for these.

One is a grazer, one inhales anything, and the third is a true diva who turns her nose up at everything unless it meets her very specific standards. She’s the reason I’ve spent more money than I care to admit on trial-sized cans and bags that ended up donated to the shelter. The difference was immediate. I opened the pouch and was met with a rich, meaty smell that didn’t have that overly processed, artificial fishy odor I’ve come to dread. The texture is a smooth pâté with visible shreds of real meat, not that gluey, jelly-filled mess that some brands push. I spooned a small portion into her bowl and she actually walked over to inspect it—normally she sniffs and walks away. This time she licked the bowl clean and meowed for more. My other two cats loved it too, which is rare because the grazer often ignores new foods.

I’ve been using it as a topper on her regular kibble and sometimes as a standalone meal. Her coat looks shinier, and there’s been no upset stomach, which I’ve dealt with before when switching foods. If you have a feline food critic at home, give this a shot. It’s the first product in years that has passed the picky test in my house. Highly recommend.

Instead, it seems to leave a residue or a streak that is hard to buff out without further scrubbing, which I worry will only make the coating wear off faster. title: High Adrenaline Thriller with quirks
text:
Music Notes is Manning Wolfe's second installation in the Texas Lady Lawyer series. It's a fast-paced, intense thriller with an eclectic cast, one of those stories that will keep you up so late at night you'll need extra coffee in the morning. Merit Bridges, the perky but powerful protagonist and her quirky team of paralegals find themselves, yet again, in opposition to a deliciously delusional villain intent on their demise.
When the rehabilitated rock guitar hero, Liam Nolan, is brutally murdered with his own guitar, Merit is not only responsible for his estate but feels morally obligated to help solve the crime. Enter Davey Ray Bell who claims to be Liam's love child. Though Davey seems lost and alone there may be some validity to his claim. Meanwhile, Liam's former manager, L A Baron, hopes to grab all the glory and the cash. When he fails to convince the legal authorities of his claim to the riches, he uses his vast resources to attempt to destroy Merit's career and reputation.
The writing is very visual and personal. Wolfe's characters are complex and for the most part driven by more than just material gain. Though the story is definitely dark, it's handled with a quirky humor and panache that brings this storyteller to the pinnacle of legal thriller authors. As an extra bonus, it's set in Austin Texas where the old hippie culture still clashes with the techno-boom of the early 21st century. Wolfe's Texas Lady Lawyer stories scream to be made into a Showtime summer miniseries featuring Reese Witherspoon and her ponytail as the protagonist. Check your local listings, but as always read the book first.

title: Do buy
text:
I’ve been using Do Buy for about three weeks now, and I’m genuinely impressed with the results—enough to leave a solid 4-star review. First off, the texture is lovely: lightweight, absorbs quickly, and doesn’t leave any greasy residue. I have combination skin that’s prone to breakouts, and this hasn’t clogged my pores at all. In fact, I’ve noticed fewer small bumps and a more even tone since I started using it. The scent is subtle and fresh, not overpowering—thankfully, because strong fragrances often irritate my skin.

What I appreciate most is the hydration. My skin feels plump and softer in the morning, and makeup applies smoothly on top. I’ve also used it as a night treatment, and it seems to calm redness overnight. For the price point, it’s a great value compared to other products in this category.

Why only 4 stars? A couple of minor quibbles. The packaging is functional but not very elegant—the pump dispenser works fine, but the bottle feels a bit cheap for the price. Also, I wish it came with a little more product; I’m already halfway through and three weeks isn’t long enough to confirm long-term benefits. It’s too early to say if it will visibly fade my dark spots or fine lines, but so far, so good.

Overall, I’d recommend Do Buy if you want a gentle, effective hydrator that plays well with other products. Just don’t expect miracles overnight. I’ll likely repurchase, but I’ll keep an eye on how long the bottle lasts.

title: Excellent Zoom, Great Pics
text:
This camera replaced my previous Canon (3MP PowerShot S30). I will only buy Canon cameras, their picture quality is superb for a point-n-shoot. What sold me on the SX120IS was the 10X optical zoom.

The 10X optical zoom is spectacular! It gets wonderful pictures of our kids on the baseball field, and at concerts and shows. Pictures that 3X optical zoom could never do. Pictures from 100 ft look like you were standing only 15 ft away. I've had other parents ask me to take pictures of their kids, because they couldn't get close enough for a good shot. Yes, 10X is awesome.

The 10 megapixels are good, and the pictures are still great, but I am not impressed by pixel count. The overall picture quality is as good as my previous 3 MP canon, but not better. However, now the files are 3.3 times larger on my hard drive. Slower to open, slower to upload to web, and harder to email. The up-side to 10 MP is when pictures need cropped, there are still plenty of pixels remaining to make a good 8.5x11 print.

Do not be taken by the 3.0" LCD. Yes, it is big. But the resolution is not tight, so even though the LCD is bigger there aren't more pixels in it. And the menu fonts are big. I would have been just as happy with a 2.5" LCD with a tighter resolution.

All of the shooting modes are great, and easy to use. This camera has more "special" modes than my last camera, and they are nice. But one mode it does not have, and I miss it, is the panoramic stitch-assist mode. If you try to do a pano stitch with this camera, you'll have to guess at where you left off.

Overall this is a great camera. I would recommend it to anyone who wants beautiful pictures and a lot of optical zoom. Can't beat the price either.

title: A Colorful Spectrum of Poetry and Painting
text:
Victoria Franks paints pictures with oil and with words, each complementing the other. Her book of poetry and art The Aroma of Coffee is colorful and sensual. From the mountains of South America and the deserts of Arizona to the swamps and shores of Northwest Florida, Franks details the unique beauty she perceives.
Her work covers the gamut of pride in country and despair at war and loneliness to passion, love, and joy. Her poetry shows us the simple yet difficult life of Columbians alongside the complexities of their struggle. Every topic she covers resounds with insightful truth.
Flavored with chocolate, potatoes and corn, mojitos and margaritas, the aroma of coffee is merely a tease. Her work is colored with every hue of the spectrum and accented with Spanish words that roll off the tongue as well as the page, their English definition less important than their fluidity.

I wanted to like this product — the packaging looked nice and the shade matched what I expected from the photos. I'm giving it three stars because it has both positives and drawbacks that are worth knowing before you buy.

Now the big caveat: the drying time. It takes much longer to fully set than I anticipated. I followed the instructions, and while the product felt tacky for a long time, it didn't truly dry for nearly twice as long as similar items I’ve used. That meant I had to be extra careful getting dressed, putting on jewelry, or touching my hair. A few times it transferred onto my scarf and sleeve despite trying to be careful. If you’re in a hurry most mornings, this will be frustrating.

Another small issue is that if you try to layer it before it’s fully dry, it pills and becomes uneven. I learned to apply a thinner layer and wait patiently, but that reduced the coverage and required a second coat with more drying time.

Overall, it’s an okay product if you plan ahead and don’t need something quick. Good finish and tolerable wear, but the long drying time and transfer risk keep it from being a favorite. I’d recommend it only to people who can spare the extra time for application.

title: Sheds like other goat hair brushes, but great value
text:
I’ve been using this goat hair makeup brush for a few weeks now, and for the price it’s a solid find. Right away it felt soft and comfortable in my hand — the handle has a good weight and the bristles are plush without feeling flimsy. It picks up powder and blush nicely and blends product out to a natural, airbrushed finish. For everyday use it performs well.

That said, it does shed. I noticed loose hairs coming out the first couple of uses and I still get an occasional stray bristle when I wash it. It’s comparable to other goat hair brushes I’ve owned in that regard, so it wasn’t a deal-breaker for me, but if you’re expecting a completely shed-free brush you might be disappointed. Washing gently and letting it dry flat helped reduce the amount of shedding over time.

Cleaning is straightforward — soap and lukewarm water do the job — and the brush retained its shape after drying. The bristles didn’t become splayed or scratchy. I’ve used it with powder blush, bronzer and a light face powder, and it worked well across those products. It’s not a dense buffing brush for heavy cream products, but that’s not what I bought it for.

Overall, I’m happy with this purchase. Performance is very good for the price, and while the shedding is a downside, it’s consistent with other natural goat-hair brushes I’ve owned. If you want an affordable, soft brush for powders and blending, this one delivers great value. I’d recommend it with the caveat that you should handle it gently and expect a bit of shedding initially.

title: Best new table-top or Skype-it role playing game!
text:
I have played this game both as a play tester Storyteller and Player for many years now, and I love it. Everyone (especially the stalwart Dungeons & Dragons players disappointed with the watered down D&D latest editions) loves the game system and basic premise: to become emperor at all costs (even at the expense of the other players). In that respect, it's like Celebrity Apprentice or Survivor in that the players work together but all are really scheming to outdo each other to eventually rise to such power as to become Emperor or Empress.

The whole game has an open spell system (this book [[ASIN:0692088644 The Adventurer's Rulebook: An Essential Component of the Immortal Empires Role-Playing Game for Mature Players]] ) where you create your own spells with a straightforward point system, 10 huge magical fighting arts (this book and the Storyteller's Codex) with 40 fighting art powers each, nonmagical Talents for fighters and thieves, politicians and assassins, and much more.

The system uses d10s only, and the opposed roll system is perfect. It allows the weaker characters a chance against the great characters, as in real life. Overall, it's a great game, in my humble opinion, and a great learning tool for math, vocabulary, and yes, even Latin!

To get a feel for the game, because it is costly (but it is well worth it as these are premium 8.5x11" full color laminate hard cover books), people should order the three available novels:

[[ASIN:1543132170 Mirror Motives: Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age (Immortal Empires Sextology) (Volume 1)]]
[[ASIN:1543141161 The Starborn War: Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age (Immortal Empires Sextology) (Volume 2)]]
[[ASIN:0692076018 Keeper of the Myst (Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age) (Volume 3)]]

as well as the other core rulebook for the game:

title: Great sprinkler for little kids!
text:
I bought this sprinkler for my three-year-old and five-year-old, and it has been an absolute lifesaver during this heatwave. We have tried a few different water toys over the last couple of summers, but most of them are either too aggressive with the water pressure or too complicated to set up. This one is perfect for little kids who are still getting used to the feeling of water spraying on them.

The setup was incredibly simple. I just hooked it up to our standard garden hose, turned on the water, and it was ready to go in less than two minutes. One thing I really appreciate is that the water pressure is gentle. My youngest can run right through the middle of it without getting overwhelmed or scared, which was a big concern for us with our previous sprinkler. It creates a fun, misty environment that keeps them cool without soaking them so instantly that they freeze up.

The build quality is surprisingly durable. My kids are not exactly gentle with their toys, and they have spent hours jumping and sliding around it, but it has held up perfectly. The material feels thick and sturdy, and we haven't noticed any leaks at the hose connection, which is usually where these things fail. It is also very easy to deflate and store away when we aren't using it, so it doesn't take up much room in the garage.

What I love most is how much active play it encourages. Instead of just sitting in a plastic pool, my kids are running, jumping, and chasing each other through the water. It keeps them physically active and completely entertained for long stretches of time. It is rare to find a toy that both children are equally obsessed with, but this has become the highlight of their day.

If you have toddlers or young children and you are looking for a way to keep them cool in the backyard without any stress, I highly recommend this. It is affordable, safe, and provides hours of entertainment. It is exactly what we were looking for to make our summer more enjoyable. I am very happy with this purchase.

title: Good for some but not myself unfortunately (Not recommended for left handed users)
text:
I was a Wacom user for about 12 years, using a Intuos v3 large- Now don't get me wrong, it's not that this tablet is necessarily bad, but I just don't think it's for me. While the drawing surface is about the same size as the intuos 3 I had, the size overall is quite a bit smaller, and I need larger tablets because of my carpal tunnel. I tend to draw with my whole arm/elbow, so it's difficult to adjust to after having a bigger tablet for such a long time.

The surface is also incredibly matte which is... odd feeling? The buttons both on the tablet and the pen are fairly inconveniently placed even for a right handed user I tend to press them often when moving to type or holding the edge as I draw. I can't imagine how bad it'd be for a left handed user. Now to the button on the pen; something about the placement is just... off. I never had this issue with my intuos pen, but I CONSTANTLY press it, which turns the pen off. Constantly. I'll be working and turn off my pen about 4-6 times within about 2 hours maybe?

All in all this tablet just isn't for me and was honestly a quick fix for my previous tablet finally dying on me. I am quite confident at the moment that I'll be going back to wacom once I have the extra income to do so.

Pros:

• The desktop shortcut to the tablet menu is actually quite helpful. It makes it easy to adjust the overall pen pressure of the tablet.
• 8 extra pen nibs in the bottom of the pen stand.

Cons:

• Incredibly matte drawing surface. Which in my personal opinion not as nice as a nice glossy, smooth, drawing surface.
• Shortcut buttons are super inconvenient and poorly placed.
• Button on pen is very poorly placed. Probably one of my biggest issues so far.

title: Very easy to fly
text:
I bought this drone for my 12-year-old after reading that it was “very easy to fly,” and overall it has delivered on that promise. Right out of the box the setup was straightforward — charged the battery, synced the controller, and we were hovering in the backyard within ten minutes. The controls are responsive and intuitive; the beginner mode is especially helpful for someone just learning how to keep a steady hover and make gentle turns.

The flight stability is impressive for a toy in this price range. Even on slightly windy days it holds position well, and the built-in altitude hold keeps it from drifting up or down unexpectedly. The battery life is okay — we get about 8–10 minutes per charge, which is typical for toys at this level. I purchased an extra battery and that doubled our playtime without much fuss.

Camera is decent for casual footage; not high-res but fine for family videos and a few fun clips to share. The drone is fairly durable too — it survived a couple of hard landings without damage to the propellers or body, which gave me confidence that it will last through normal kid use.

Why four stars and not five? Two small complaints: the charging cable is short and the controller range could be a bit better for longer flights. Also, replacement parts aren’t super easy to find locally. Despite that, considering the price and how easy it is to learn, I’d recommend this as a great starter drone for kids and beginners.

title: Lacking in depth
text:
I really wanted to like this book because the premise sounded exactly like what I was looking for. The table of contents promised a comprehensive guide, and the initial chapters started off strong with some decent foundational information. However, as I got deeper into the text, I realized that the author spends far too much time on the basics and almost no time on the actual application.

It feels like a collection of blog posts rather than a fully realized book. Every time the author touched on a complex topic that required real nuance, they would give a superficial overview and then move on to the next point without providing any actionable steps or detailed examples. I found myself constantly waiting for the "how" and the "why," but it never arrived. By the halfway mark, I felt like I was reading a summary of a better book rather than the actual source material.

The writing style is clear enough, but that doesn't make up for the lack of substance. If you are a complete beginner who has never heard of this subject, you might find it useful for an hour or two. But if you have any prior knowledge or are looking for an authoritative deep dive, this is a waste of money. I expected a masterclass and got a brochure. I ended up having to buy a different book on the same topic just to get the actual answers I needed. I cannot recommend this for anyone seeking a thorough education on the subject.

title: Mixed Emotions
text:
A dark and foreboding novel of a thousands years ago -- the coldness of the climate and the land accentuated by the lack of the sun's light -- although it teasingly seems to appear on the horizon to prematurely announce its impending return.

"The Wolf in the Whale" is populated by ancient, mysterious, powerful and hardy people - Norsemen and women living, fighting and dying in a new world. The whole novel brings with it a sense of perpetual cold and darkness.

The spirits seem to reign in this book -- they talk to the shamans young and old, and bestow upon them certain powers as the situations deem -- The chief protagonists are a young girl and her older brother, who use their wits to survive -- and who are transmuted back and forth to animal spirits and back again to human.

The narrative is excellent - one can feel the harsh living conditions and can be caught up in the spirit world that revolves around each person like a whirlpool of snow and cold air. The veil between the spirit, animal and human world is very thin indeed.

However, I felt that the book dragged on for too long -- and after a while this reader began to feel mired down in spots, as if walking thru a powdery snow capped with thin ice - very slow going.

So although "The Wolf in the Whale" transported me quite well, back to an era where the spirits and animals spoke with and transferred powers on primitive warrior humans fighting to survive in a cold and forbidding land - it was a wearying journey for me, as it was, IMHO, far too long.

text:
This looks like a fun puzzle. The concept is great. The execution? Not so much.

First of all, this puzzle, which is the size of two old 45 records stacked atop one another, arrives in a plastic package the size of your house.

Well, maybe not quite that big, but it is much, much larger than necessary. MUCH larger. So I was already not very happy with it. Then, I tried to open it, and made another discovery: if you for some reason need to perform emergency surgery in your home, the plastic encasing this puzzle will double as a scalpel.

Honestly, I think they just want you to buy it and put it on display in the box. This package is next to impossible to open.

And wasteful. Did I mention yet that this plastic package is much, much too big for it’s contents? Because it is.

Once I finally got the puzzle out, I mixed it up, spun it round, did the entire hokey-pokey. Then I started the process of solving it. I ordered the most challenging one since I am good at puzzles and wanted something that would tax my brain.

I am little, and have the hands to match. Even my childlike fingers had difficulty maneuvering the tiny inner rings. After about the fifth one from the center, it gets easier.

It took me under three minutes to solve. For the most difficult one. Counting the issues I had moving and turning the tiniest rings. Either I am some sort of prodigy, or this doesn’t deliver on the hours of fun puzzling promised. I tried the other side to see if it was a fluke. It was not. Nor is this like a Rubik’s Cube, where after you solve it, it’s fun to mix it up and try again. I haven’t had the urge to pick it up again after my initial tests, which I think says something.

Bottom line: extremely wasteful packaging containing a no-challenge “puzzle.” Maybe this would be better marketed as a fidget toy. Or to very small children. Would not recommend.

text:
I was delighted to find this author, known for his travel narratives and splendid prose, an Englishman born in 1908 and only dying recently at age 95 in Saffron Walden, Essex, where he had lived modestly and politely, shyly even. Luigi Barzini described reading his prose as "like eating cherries" and Graham Greene - with whom Lewis shared many similarities in adventures, courage and quiet, commanding prose - had "no hesitation in calling him one of the best writers, not of any particular decade, but of our century".

In this work - part of a multiple volume autobiography, there was only one decision Lewis made that damaged his intellect in this readers view - he agreed to an investigative reporting trip to Peru accompanied by Lord Snowden as his photographer, traveling "incognito". Lewis seemed genuinely surprised that was far from a successful trip, or experience, and as for the `incognito' - well at least it got the author free upgrades to First Class flights and entertainment by British Ambassadors and Peruvian society!

The author had a fascinating and often wildly exciting life, serving in the British Forces in Italy during WWII followed by a career in journalism reporting on Vietnam, Burma, Indo China and producing a splendid series of books for Jonathan Cape - who used to entertain his authors with dinners of burnt Irish Stew - on the mafia in Sicily, and the threatened indigenous peoples of Latin America.

Writing with a compassion and light wit Lewis crafted over thirty books and one of his five children, his second son Gareth, has also published a book called 'Deceit'.

title: Flyover Nation- A window into our country's soul.
text:
I bought Flyover Nation out of curiosity and finished it in two sittings — surprised, moved, and a little ashamed that I’d underestimated what a “travel through America” book could do. The author doesn’t romanticize or caricature; instead, he listens. The portraits of small towns, factory floors, church basements, and open highways are honest and granular, full of people whose stories stay with you. What I appreciated most was the balance: empathy without sentimentality, critique without condescension. The writing is clear and often quietly lyrical, making the book both informative and emotionally resonant.

As someone who grew up in the Midwest but has lived in cities for years, this felt like a necessary reminder of the complexity and dignity of places often dismissed as “flyover.” It also challenged some of my assumptions and opened new ones. Thought-provoking, humane, and beautifully observed — a book I’ll recommend and return to.
